Definition 2.3.13

(Definition-Construction)
.

Write
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}N
as a union of group indschemes
\displaystyle\bigcup_{\alpha}N_{\alpha}
, each containing
\displaystyle N_{0}:=\mathcal{L}^{+}N
; let
\displaystyle\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha}
denote their Lie algebras. For
\displaystyle N_{\alpha_{1}}\subseteq N_{\alpha_{2}}
, there is a canonically defined connecting map
\displaystyle C^{*}(\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha_{1}},-)\Rightarrow C^{*}(\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha_{2}},-\tensor\det(\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha_{2}}/\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha_{1}}))
. There is a
semi-infinite cohomology
functor

C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},-):\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}T}\to\textnormal{KL}_{\kappa}(T)

whose composition with the forgetful to
Vect
is given by

V\mapsto\colimit_{\alpha}C^{*}(\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha},V\tensor\det(\mathfrak{n}_{\alpha}/\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n}));

For each
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
we set

C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},-)^{{\check{\lambda}}}:=\Hom_{\Rep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)}(k^{\check{\lambda}},C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},-)):\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}T}\to\textnormal{Vect}.

Wakimoto Modules

For any
\displaystyle w\in W^{\textnormal{fin}},{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
, the
Wakimoto module of type
\displaystyle w
, denoted
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w,{\check{\lambda}}}\in\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I,\heartsuit}
, is defined in
[
Gai21
, Section 2.4]
. Here we will give a “quick and dirty” definition:

Definition 2.3.14
.

For
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
, the type 1 Wakimoto module
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}
is the unique object in
\displaystyle\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}
satisfying

\langle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}},-\rangle_{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}^{I}}\simeq C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},-\tensor\det(\mathfrak{n}^{-})^{\tensor-1})^{-{\check{\lambda}}}:\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{-\kappa}^{I}\to\textnormal{Vect};

For
\displaystyle w\in W^{\textnormal{fin}}
, we define the type
\displaystyle w
Wakimoto module
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w,{\check{\lambda}}}
as

\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w,{\check{\lambda}}}:=j_{w,*}\star\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}.

Remark 2.3.15
.

Wakimoto modules are the “limiting behavior” of Verma modules as they are twisted by elements of the affine Weyl group; more precisely we have (
[
Gai21
, Section 3.3.2]
)

\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}\simeq\colimit_{\mu\in\Lambda^{\sharp,+}}j_{-\mu,*}\star\mathbb{M}_{\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}+\mu}.

We will mainly be interested in the
type 1
Wakimoto modules
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}
and the
type
\displaystyle w_{0}
version
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w_{0},{\check{\lambda}}}
; these should be considered as semi-infinite Verma at the negative level (resp. semi-infinite dual Vermas at the positive level).
We will mostly only need their formal properties listed below:

For all levels

The following properties are true for Wakimoto modules at all levels:

•

(
[
Gai21
, Section 2.5.9]
) For any
\displaystyle\mu\in{\Lambda^{\sharp}}
,
\displaystyle w\in W^{\textnormal{fin}},{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
, we have
\displaystyle J_{\mu}\star\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w,{\check{\lambda}}}\simeq\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w,{\check{\lambda}}+\mu}
;

•

(
[
Gai21
, Section 2.4.7]
])
\displaystyle C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n}^{-},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n}^{-},\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}})^{{\check{\lambda}}^{\prime}}=\begin{cases}\det(\mathfrak{n}^{-})^{\tensor-1}&\textnormal{if}~{\check{\lambda}}^{\prime}={\check{\lambda}}+2\check{\rho}\\
0&\textnormal{else}\end{cases}

•

(
[
Gai
, Section 1.3.7]
)
\displaystyle C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},\mathbb{W}_{\kappa}^{w_{0},{\check{\lambda}}})^{{\check{\lambda}}^{\prime}}=\begin{cases}\mathbb{C}&\textnormal{if}~{\check{\lambda}}^{\prime}={\check{\lambda}}\\
0&\textnormal{else}\end{cases}

For negative levels

At negative (and critical) levels, Kac-Kazhdan theorem implies that Wakimoto modules will converge to the opposite Verma within finite time.
For
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
sufficiently dominant, we have

\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}\simeq\mathbb{M}_{-\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{w_{0},{\check{\lambda}}}\simeq\mathbb{M}_{-\kappa}^{\vee,{\check{\lambda}}};

whereas for
\displaystyle\check{\mu}
sufficiently anti-dominant, we have

\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{1,\check{\mu}}\simeq\mathbb{M}_{-\kappa}^{\vee,\check{\mu}}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{w_{0},\check{\mu}}\simeq\mathbb{M}_{-\kappa}^{\check{\mu}}.

Now we check that Definition
2.3.6
is a valid one:

Lemma 2.3.16
.

The type 1 Wakimoto modules
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}
form a set of compact generators of
\displaystyle\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{-\kappa}^{I}
.

Proof.

It follows from the properties of Wakimoto sheaves that, for every
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
, we can choose
\displaystyle\mu\in({\Lambda^{\sharp}})^{+}
such that
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}+\mu\in\check{\Lambda}^{+}
, and have
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}\simeq j_{-\mu,*}\star\mathbb{M}_{-\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}+\mu}
. Since
\displaystyle j_{-\mu,*}
is an invertible operation and Vermas are compact generators, we know that
\displaystyle\mathbb{W}_{-\kappa}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}
are compact as well. To show they generate, it suffices to show that every Verma can be written as a
finite
colimit of Wakimoto modules. Fix some
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}_{0}
admissible and
\displaystyle\tilde{w}\in W^{\textnormal{aff},\textnormal{ext},\sharp}
such that
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}=\tilde{w}\cdot{\check{\lambda}}_{0}
, and invoke Kashiwara-Tanisaki localization. Then we have that in such case,

\Gamma_{-\kappa}(\textnormal{Fl}_{G},j_{\tilde{w},!}\star\delta_{1})^{I}\simeq\mathbb{M}^{{\check{\lambda}}}_{-\kappa}\hskip 10.00002pt\Gamma_{-\kappa}(\textnormal{Fl}_{G},J_{\tilde{w}}\star\delta_{1})^{I}\simeq\mathbb{W}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}_{-\kappa},

that the support range (more precisely, images in
\displaystyle K_{0}
) of
\displaystyle j_{\tilde{w},!}
and
\displaystyle J_{\tilde{w}}
are the same, and the nonzero map
\displaystyle\mathbb{M}^{{\check{\lambda}}}_{-\kappa}\to\mathbb{W}^{1,{\check{\lambda}}}_{-\kappa}
is induced by a map
\displaystyle j_{\widetilde{w},!}\to J_{\widetilde{w}}
that is isomorphism on the open strata (
[
AB09
, Theorem 5, Lemma 27]
). The claim now follows by induction on support dimension.
∎

Remark 2.3.17
.

Our standard objects are designed such that for every
\displaystyle M\in\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}
, we have

\Hom_{\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}}(\Delta_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}},M)\simeq C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}N,M)^{{\check{\lambda}}};

and the costandards are their right orthogonals.

2.4
Jacquet Functor and Local-Global Correspondence

It follows from definition that the fiber of the functor

C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}\circ\textnormal{res}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\mathscr{L}}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}G\times_{G_{x}}B_{x}}\to\mathcal{KL}(T)_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}}

at the distinguished point
\displaystyle x
is precisely
\displaystyle C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}N,-):\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}\to\textnormal{KL}_{\kappa}(T)
. Now, because
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(G)_{\kappa}
is an
unital
factorization category with vacuum
\displaystyle\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}
, we have (Proposition
10.5.22
) an equivalence of categories

(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})\simeq\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,0]}}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}G\times_{G_{x}}B_{x}});

using the fact that
\displaystyle C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}\circ\textnormal{res}
is lax-unital we obtain a functor

\textbf{J}^{\textnormal{KM}}_{\kappa}:\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}\simeq\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,0]}}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}G\times_{G_{x}}B_{x}})\xrightarrow{C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}\circ\textnormal{res}}C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\mathcal{KL}(T)_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}}),

whose composition with taking the fiber at
\displaystyle x
recovers
\displaystyle C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}N,-)
. We will refer to this functor as the
Kac-Moody Jacquet
11
11

11

The name “Jacquet functor” has its origins from the Whittaker side of the fundamental local equivalence.
functor
.

For the rest of this subsection, consider the special case
\displaystyle X=\mathbb{P}^{1}
, and let
\displaystyle\overrightarrow{x}:=(0,\infty)
be the two distinguished
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle\mathbb{P}^{1}
. The natural multi-point generalization of the above construction gives a functor

\textbf{J}^{\textnormal{KM}}_{\kappa}:(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})_{0}\tensor(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})_{\infty}\to C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}([\mathcal{KL}(T)_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\overrightarrow{x}}(\mathbb{P}^{1})_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}),

where on the LHS we use subscripts to indicate that we identify these two categories as fibers as
\displaystyle 0
resp.
\displaystyle\infty
, and on RHS we use subscript to indicate that we work with the multi-marked-point version of the unital Ran space (c.f. Example
10.4.10
).

Set

\textnormal{Bun}_{G}(\mathbb{P}^{1})^{\textnormal{level}_{B},\overrightarrow{x}}:=\textnormal{Bun}_{G}(\mathbb{P}^{1})\times_{[(\textnormal{pt}/G)_{0}\times(\textnormal{pt}/G)_{\infty}]}[(\textnormal{pt}/B)_{0}\times(\textnormal{pt}/B)_{\infty}]

(where subscripts
\displaystyle 0
and
\displaystyle\infty
are to clarify where these reductions take place), and consider the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Bun}_{B}(\mathbb{P}^{1})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\mathsf{q}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\mathsf{p}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Bun}_{G}(\mathbb{P}^{1})^{\textnormal{level}_{B},\overrightarrow{x}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Bun}_{T}(\mathbb{P}^{1})}

Recall from
[
Gai17
]
the
geometric constant term functor

\textnormal{CT}_{*}:=\mathsf{q}_{*}\circ\mathsf{p}^{!}:\textnormal{DMod}_{[\kappa+\kappa_{\textnormal{crit},G},0]}(\textnormal{Bun}_{G}(\mathbb{P}^{1})^{\textnormal{level}_{B},\overrightarrow{x}})\to\textnormal{DMod}_{[\kappa+\kappa_{\textnormal{crit}_{G}},0]}(\textnormal{Bun}_{T}(\mathbb{P}^{1}));

also recall the line bundle
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textnormal{Tate}(\mathfrak{n})}
on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Bun}_{T}(\mathbb{P}^{1})
, which satisfies

\mathcal{L}_{\textnormal{Tate}(\mathfrak{n})}|_{\mathcal{P}_{T}}\simeq\det R\Gamma(\mathbb{P}^{1},\mathfrak{n}_{\mathcal{P}_{T}}[1])

here
\displaystyle\mathfrak{n}_{\mathcal{P}_{T}}
is the associated vector bundle of the adjoint action, and the (integral) twisting corresponding to this line bundle is the

\displaystyle[-\kappa_{\textnormal{crit}_{G}},E_{\textnormal{anom}}]
. We incorporate this shift into our definition by setting

\textnormal{CT}_{*}^{\textnormal{shifted}}:=[\mathcal{L}_{\textnormal{Tate}(\mathfrak{n})}[-d]\tensor-]\circ\textnormal{CT}_{*}:\textnormal{DMod}_{[\kappa+\kappa_{\textnormal{crit},G},0]}(\textnormal{Bun}_{G}(\mathbb{P}^{1})^{\textnormal{level}_{B},\overrightarrow{x}})\to\textnormal{DMod}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}(\textnormal{Bun}_{T}(\mathbb{P}^{1})),

where
\displaystyle d
is a number that depends on the connected component of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Bun}_{T}(\mathbb{P}^{1})
: over the
\displaystyle\lambda
-component it is
\displaystyle-\langle\lambda,2\check{\rho}\rangle-\dim(\mathfrak{n})
.

In Section

, we will construct two

\displaystyle[\textnormal{Loc}]_{\overrightarrow{x}}
and

\displaystyle\textstyle{(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})_{x_{0}}\tensor(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})_{x_{\infty}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

The role this diagram plays will become evident during the proof of the main theorem.

2.5
Conversion into Sheaves

Let
\displaystyle[\kappa,0]
be a non-degenerate level and
\displaystyle[\check{\kappa},0]
be its Langlands dual level. As we explained in the introduction, we have a unital factorization category
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}})
whose fiber at any point on the curve is given by
\displaystyle\check{\kappa}
-twisted D-modules over
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}})
, and there is an equivalence of unital factorization categories

\textnormal{FLE}_{T}:\mathcal{KL}(T)_{[\kappa,0]}\simeq\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}});

we would like to pass through this equivalence to transform the output of
\displaystyle\textbf{J}_{\kappa}^{\textnormal{KM}}
into D-modules. For technical reasons, however, we will use a slight variant as follows.

A first caveat is that the category at the receiving end of our Jacquet functor has a nonzero
\displaystyle E
-term in its parameter, namely
\displaystyle E_{\textnormal{anom}}
. This can be taken into account as follows.

Definition 2.5.1
.

Let
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
be the
\displaystyle\check{\rho}
-shifted affine Grassmannian
, whose
\displaystyle S
-points classify:

•

a point
\displaystyle x:S^{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{cl}}\to\textnormal{Ran}
;

•

a
\displaystyle\check{T}
-bundle
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}
on the adic disc
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}}
around the graph of
\displaystyle x
;

•

an isomorphism
\displaystyle\alpha
of
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}
on the punctured disc with the restriction of
\displaystyle\omega^{\check{\rho}}
;

There is an isomorphism of unital factorization spaces
\displaystyle-\tensor\omega^{\check{\rho}}:[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
. We let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}
denote the unique twisting on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}
whose pullback along this map gives
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{[\check{\kappa},0]}
. There is then a unital factorization category
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})
, and we have (c.f. Section
5
) another equivalence of unital factorization categories

\textnormal{FLE}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}_{T}:\mathcal{KL}(T)_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}\simeq\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}})

induced by
\displaystyle\textnormal{FLE}_{T}
.

For technical purposes it is better to work with
negatively-weighted
factorization algebras on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}
; geometrically this means working with the
configuration space
. We refer readers to
[
GL19
, Section 4]
for proofs of statements in this subsection.

Throughout this subsection, let
\displaystyle\overrightarrow{x}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{k})
is a fixed set of
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle X
. For each smooth curve
\displaystyle X
, we have

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}(X)
the scheme of
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}^{<0}\setminus\{0\}
-colored divisors on
\displaystyle X
;

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}^{\circ}(X)
, the open part where each point is marked by a negative simple root;

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}
, the ind-scheme where the marking on
\displaystyle x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}
are now allowed to be any element of
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}
;

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}^{={\check{\lambda}}}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}^{={\check{\lambda}}}
, the stratification by total weights.

The space
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}(X)
admits an additive semigroup structure, and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}
is a module space of it. Using
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}^{\circ}(X)
in replacement of
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Ran}\times\textnormal{Ran}]_{\textnormal{disj}}
one still has a notion of factorizable structures over the configuration space; we will use the same notations as before to denote these variants as well.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
be any factorizable twisting on the
\displaystyle\check{\rho}
-shifted affine Grassmannian. As we will show in Section
10.8
, to each factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
supported on a certain subspace
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}
(the fibers of which corresponds to
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}^{<0}\subseteq\check{\Lambda}
), one can attach a factorization algebra
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}
over the configuration space, and we have a reduction functor

\textnormal{Red}_{\textnormal{Conf}}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\overrightarrow{x}}}))\to A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}})).

Remark 2.5.2
.

There are a few key differences in using configuration spaces vs. the Ran space: it is an actual scheme (in the module case, ind-scheme), and has very strong finiteness properties (so that operations such as Verdier duality are well-behaved). Also note that for the configuration space, the factorization condition does not involve
diagonal restriction
.

Let us return to our Jacquet functor. Consider

\begin{split}&(\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I})_{x_{0}}\xrightarrow{\textbf{J}^{\textnormal{KM}}_{\kappa}}C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}([\mathcal{KL}(T)_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}}]_{(\textnormal{Ran}_{x_{0}})_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})\\
&\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\textnormal{FLE}^{\check{\rho}}_{T}}\textnormal{FLE}^{\check{\rho}}_{T}\circ C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}([\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}(\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}})]_{(\textnormal{Ran}_{x_{0}})_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}).\end{split}

(2)

We remind that at the fiber level, the functor
\displaystyle C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}
is given by
\displaystyle C_{*}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{n},\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{n},-)
. Cohomological estimates from Proposition
8.2.10
below therefore guarantees that the process lands in the full subcategory of factorization modules supported on the configuration space, and we can continue the process above as

\xrightarrow{\textnormal{Red}_{\textnormal{Conf}}}[\textnormal{FLE}^{\check{\rho}}_{T}\circ C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))]_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x_{0}})).

(3)

We define

\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}:=\textnormal{FLE}^{\check{\rho}}_{T}\circ C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0}))\in\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}(\textnormal{Conf}))

and refer to the combination of Equation (
2
) and (
3
) as

\textbf{J}_{\kappa}:\hat{\mathfrak{g}}\operatorname{-mod}_{\kappa}^{I}\to\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x_{0}})).

We shall proceed to show that this functor is an equivalence for
\displaystyle X=\mathbb{A}^{1}
, under mild constraint on
\displaystyle\kappa
.

Remark 2.5.3
.

We note (without proof) that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Red}_{\textnormal{Conf}}
in this case is in fact an equivalence, so that
\displaystyle\textbf{J}_{\kappa}^{\textnormal{KM}}
is already an equivalence of categories.

2.5.4
Highest Weight Structure

Another benefit of working with configuration spaces is the following highest weight structure for factorization modules, developed in
[
GL19
, 5.3]
. Assume
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}
is a non-unital factorization algebra on the configuration space as above, and such that it is
ind-holonomic
as a D-module. Let us consider the case
\displaystyle\overrightarrow{x}=(x)
a single fixed point. Then:

•

For every
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
there exists a
standard
object
\displaystyle\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\check{\lambda}}
and a
costandard
object
\displaystyle\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\check{\lambda}}
within the category
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x}))
;

•

The standard objects form a set of compact generators of
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x}))
, and the costandards are their right orthogonals, in the sense that

\Hom_{A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x}))}(\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{{\check{\lambda}}},\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\check{\mu}})\simeq\begin{cases}\mathbb{C}&{\check{\lambda}}=\check{\mu}\\
0&\textnormal{else}\end{cases}

Moreover, this property characterizes the standard object
\displaystyle\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\check{\lambda}}
(resp. costandard object
\displaystyle\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\check{\lambda}}
) as the unique object that exhibits such property with respect to all costandard (resp. standard) objects;

•

The standard object has the following universal property: for every
\displaystyle M
, we have

\Hom_{A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x}))}(\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{{\check{\lambda}}},M)\simeq\iota_{\mu\cdot x}^{!}(M)

where
\displaystyle\iota_{\mu\cdot x}
is the inclusion of the point
\displaystyle(\mu\cdot x)
into
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot x}
;

•

The costandard object has the following universal property: for every
\displaystyle M
, we have

\Hom_{A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot c}))}(M,\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{{\check{\lambda}}})\simeq\iota_{\mu\cdot x}^{*}(M);

•

All standard and co-standard objects are regular (resp. regular holonomic) if
\displaystyle A
is.

2.6
Jacquet Functor is an Equivalence

We will first need the following fact:

Proposition 2.6.1
.

For any smooth curve
\displaystyle X
,
\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
is the
trivial
local system when restricted to a single copy of the curve
\displaystyle X_{-{\check{\lambda}}}
for
\displaystyle-{\check{\lambda}}
a simple negative root.

Proof.

We start by noting that
\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
is an
universal
factorization algebra in the sense of
[
Cli19
]
: indeed, our construction evidently commutes with étale pullbacks along curves. This reduces us to the case of
\displaystyle X=\mathbb{A}^{1}
.
It is easy to verify that torus FLE is compatible with pullback along
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}\to\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}
, which implies that

\oblv_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}\to\mathbb{A}^{1}}(\Omega_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}^{\textnormal{Lus}})\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{[\check{\kappa},0]_{\leftarrow\omega^{\check{\rho}}}}(([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}})_{\textnormal{dR}}\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbb{A}^{1})

is produced from

\oblv_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}\to\mathbb{A}^{1}}(C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0})))\in[\mathcal{KL}(T)_{\mathscr{L}_{[\kappa,E_{\textnormal{anom}}]}}]_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}

via FLE. Next note that the action of
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
on the curve itself induces a weak
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
action on both these two categories above, and this weak action is respected by torus FLE; moreover, the algebra
\displaystyle\oblv_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}\to\mathbb{A}^{1}}(C^{\frac{\infty}{2}}(\textnormal{res}(\mathbb{V}_{\kappa}^{0})))
admits an weak
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
-equivariance structure with respect to this action, as we have
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\simeq\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}G\times\mathbb{A}^{1}
(and similarly for
\displaystyle[\widehat{\mathcal{L}G}]_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}
, etc). If we let
\displaystyle j_{-{\check{\lambda}}}:\mathbb{A}^{1}_{-{\check{\lambda}}}\to(([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}})_{\textnormal{dR}}\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbb{A}^{1})
denote the inclusion of the
\displaystyle-{\check{\lambda}}
-component, then by this weak equivariance we know that
\displaystyle\oblv(j_{-{\check{\lambda}}}^{!}(\Omega_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}^{\textnormal{Lus}}))\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(\mathbb{A}^{1}_{-\lambda})
is a constant coherent sheaf with
\displaystyle!
-fiber being
\displaystyle k
everywhere (c.f. Proposition
8.2.10
). As such it is a local system, but any local system on
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
is trivial.
∎

Corollary 2.6.2
.

The factorization algebra
\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
is constructible along the diagonal stratification of the Ran space; in particular, it is ind-regular holonomic.

Proof.

Follows formally from factorization property.
∎

Given the Proposition above, Section
2.5.4
tells us that
\displaystyle\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}}
and
\displaystyle\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}}
are well-defined objects for
\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
.
From now on, let
\displaystyle X=\mathbb{A}^{1}
be our background curve, and let
\displaystyle x_{0}\in X(\mathbb{C})
denote the origin. Our main theorem is that

Theorem 2.6.3
.

For
\displaystyle\kappa
satisfying Condition
1.1.3
,
\displaystyle\textbf{J}_{\kappa}
is an equivalence of categories, and satisfies, for every
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
,

\textbf{J}_{\kappa}(\Delta_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}})\simeq\Delta_{\textnormal{Conf},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}}\hskip 10.00002pt\textbf{J}_{\kappa}(\nabla_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}})\simeq\nabla_{\textnormal{Conf},\kappa}^{{\check{\lambda}}}.

The proof of this will be delayed to Section
8
.

Remark 2.6.4
.

At this point we
do not yet know
what
\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
is; in fact, we will only be able to identify it
after
this theorem has been established.

2.7
Quantum Torus

In this section,
\displaystyle q
will denote a
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}^{\times}
-valued (multiplicative) quadratic form on
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}
. In order to utilize the results established in
[
Gai21a
]
we need some restrictions on
\displaystyle q
imposed in
loc.cit.
, namely that:

(non-degenerate)

\displaystyle q(\check{\alpha})\neq 1
for every root
\displaystyle\check{\alpha}
;

(avoids

small torsion)

For every simple factor
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
and every long root
\displaystyle\check{\alpha}_{l}
in
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{ord}(q(\check{\alpha}_{l}))\geq d_{i}+1
, where
\displaystyle d_{i}
is the lacing number of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
;

(almost

admissible)

For every simple factor
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
, every short root
\displaystyle\check{\alpha}_{s}
and every long root
\displaystyle\check{\alpha}_{l}
, we have

\textnormal{ord}(q(\check{\alpha}_{s}))\geq h_{i}-1\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{ord}(q(\check{\alpha}_{l}))\geq h_{i}^{\vee}-1,

where
\displaystyle h_{i}
the Coxeter number of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
and
\displaystyle h_{i}^{\vee}
the dual Coxeter number of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}_{i}
(this condition appears in Section 2.3.1 of
loc.cit.
).

Condition in
[
KL94a
]

We make a quick detour to compare this restriction with the restriction imposed by
[
KL94a
]
. Suppose our group is simple, and we are starting with a
negative rational level
, given by a bilinear form

(c+h^{\vee})\kappa_{\textnormal{min}}\hskip 10.00002ptc=\frac{-p}{q}\in\mathbb{Q}^{<0}\hskip 10.00002pt(p,q)=1;

here
\displaystyle\kappa_{\textnormal{min}}:=\frac{1}{2h^{\vee}}\textnormal{Kil}_{\mathfrak{g}}
is the minimal bilinear form on
\displaystyle\Lambda
.
Then, tracing through definition, one sees that the quadratic form
\displaystyle q
produced from our equivalence (extended to the negative level via duality) will be
\displaystyle\exp\left(\frac{-\pi i}{dc}\check{\kappa}_{\textnormal{min}}\right)
; here
\displaystyle d
is the lacing number of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{g}
, and
\displaystyle\check{\kappa}_{\textnormal{min}}
is the minimal bilinear form for the Langlands dual group. We thus obtain

q(\check{\alpha})=\begin{cases}\exp\left(2\pi i\frac{q}{dp}\right)&\check{\alpha}~\textnormal{short}\\
\\
\exp\left(2\pi i\frac{q}{p}\right)&\check{\alpha}~\textnormal{long}\end{cases}

which results in Table
1
.
In particular, one sees that the almost admissibility condition from Definition
8.2.6
is precisely the almost admissibility condition above.

Convention 2.7.1
.

For the rest of this subsection, we will assume the restrictions above on
\displaystyle q
are met.

Quantum Torus

Choose
a bilinear form
\displaystyle b^{\prime}
such that
\displaystyle b^{\prime}(\lambda,\lambda)=q(\lambda)
. We let
\displaystyle\Rep_{q,b^{\prime}}(T)^{\heartsuit}
denote the
braided monoidal
Grothendieck abelian (1, 1)-category whose underlying monoidal category is the standard monoidal category
\displaystyle\Rep(T)^{\heartsuit}
and whose braided structure is given by

k^{\lambda}\tensor k^{\mu}\xrightarrow{b^{\prime}(\lambda,\mu)}k^{\mu}\tensor k^{\lambda}.

As explained in
loc.cit.
, for any other choice
\displaystyle b^{\prime\prime}
, we have a
canonical
braided monoidal equivalence

\varphi_{b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime}}:\Rep_{q,b^{\prime}}(T)^{\heartsuit}\simeq\Rep_{q,b^{\prime\prime}}(T)^{\heartsuit};

moreover, this identification can be made compatible for any triple
\displaystyle(b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime},b^{\prime\prime\prime})
. Since the category of braided monoidal (1, 1)-category is only a (2, 2)-category, the category is in fact independent of the choice of
\displaystyle b^{\prime}
and we are allowed to write simply
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ch}(\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit})
be the category of unbounded chain complexes in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
. Equipped with the injective model structure
[
Lur12
, 1.3.5.3]
), it is a braided monoidal model category. Observe that the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ch}(\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit})^{\textnormal{cofib}}
of cofibrant objects clearly form a braided monoidal subcategory, the unit
\displaystyle k
is cofibrant, and monoidal tensor with any object preserve weak equivalences.
It follows from
[
Lur12
, 5.1.2.4, 4.1.7.4]
that

\mathcal{D}(\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit})\simeq N(\textnormal{Ch}(\Rep_{q}(T))^{\textnormal{cofib}})[\textnormal{quasi-iso}^{-1}]

admits a canonical
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category structure.

Definition 2.7.2
.

The
quantum torus

\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
is the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category constructed above.

2.7.3
Koszul Duality

By inverting the braiding (but keeping the monoidal structure intact), there is a canonical equivalence of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG categories
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)\simeq\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)^{\textnormal{rev-br}}
, where the superscript on RHS reminds ourselves of the reversed braiding. We have a perfect pairing

\tensor^{0}:\Rep_{q}(T)\tensor\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)\to\textnormal{Vect}

obtained by ind-extending the pairing

(c_{1}\in\Rep_{q}(T)^{c},c_{2}\in\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)^{c})\mapsto\Hom_{\textnormal{Vect}^{\check{\Lambda}}}(k,c_{1}\tensor c_{2}).

As explained in
[
Gai21
, 8.1]
, this gives identifications of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG categories

\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)\simeq\Rep_{q}(T)^{\textnormal{rev}}\simeq\Rep_{q}(T)^{\vee}

(4)

where the second category is obtained from
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
by reversing the multiplication
and
the braiding, and the third one inherits an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
structure from the second one.

Warning 2.7.4
.

One should not think of
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\textnormal{rev}}
as having a forgetful functor to
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
: indeed, the functor
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\vee}\to\Rep_{q}(T)
is given by ind-extending the graded linear dual functor. The usage of “rev” here is in accordance with
[
Lur12
, 4.1.1.7]
.

Let
\displaystyle A
be an
augmented

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra internal to
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, then
[
Lur12
, 5.2.5.38]
defined the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-Koszul dual
of
\displaystyle A
, which is the universal augmented
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra

\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A)\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))

equipped with an
\displaystyle(A,\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A)^{\textnormal{rev}})
-bimodule
12
12

12

Here the action is internal to the category of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-algebras in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
.
structure on
\displaystyle k\in\mathbb{E}_{1}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))
lifting the
\displaystyle A
-left module and
\displaystyle\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A)^{\textnormal{rev}}
-right module structure coming from the augmentations.
From
[
Lur12
, 5.2.5]
we know that
\displaystyle\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A)
exists for those
\displaystyle A
compact within
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
and is computed as
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Bar}^{(2)}(A)^{\vee})^{\textnormal{rev}}
, where:

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Bar}^{(2)}(A)
is the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-coalgebra obtained from applying the bar construction twice;

•

\displaystyle\vee
denotes the (right) dual object which obtains the structure of an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
;

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{rev}:\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\Rep_{q}(T))\simeq\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))
is the equivalence induced by
\displaystyle\mathsf{rev}
, the automorphism of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-operad that reverses the last coordinate.

Definition 2.7.5
.

Recall that for any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-category DG
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
there is an equivalence
[
Lur12
, 5.4.4.10]

\textnormal{AugIdeal}:\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C}):\bullet\oplus\textbf{1}_{\mathcal{C}}

giving by taking augmentation ideal and formally adjoining the monoidal unit.
For
\displaystyle A\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
we define

\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{nu}}(A):=\textnormal{AugIdeal}(\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A\oplus k)).

Bialgebras

For any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
category
\displaystyle\mathcal{V}
we introduce the category of bi-augmented bialgebras

\textnormal{BiAlg}(\mathcal{V})_{\textnormal{biaug}}:=\mathbb{E}_{1}\textnormal{-CoAlg}_{\textnormal{coaug}}(\mathbb{E}_{1}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\mathcal{V}));

We have adjunctions

\textnormal{Bar}:\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\mathcal{V})\adjoint\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\mathcal{V}):\textnormal{coBar}\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{Bar}:\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\mathcal{V})\adjoint\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-CoAlg}_{\textnormal{coaug}}(\mathcal{V}):\textnormal{coBar}

computable via the (co)bar construction.

Let
\displaystyle H\in\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
be a bialgebra within
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, and assume
\displaystyle H
is dualizable as an object of
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
. Then the dual object
\displaystyle H^{\vee}
is again an element of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\mathbb{E}_{1}\textnormal{-CoAlg}_{\textnormal{coaug}}(\Rep_{q}(T)))\simeq\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
. As a graded vector space, its
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
-piece is the linear dual of the
\displaystyle(-{\check{\lambda}})
-piece of
\displaystyle H
. The automorphism
\displaystyle\mathsf{rev}
as above induces a map

\textnormal{rev-comult}:\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\Rep_{q}(T))\simeq\textnormal{BiAlg}_{\textnormal{biaug}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))

which maintains the multiplication structure on a bialgebra but reverses the comultiplication structure.

Lemma 2.7.6
.

Assume that
\displaystyle H
lies in the heart of
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, is compact, is concentrated in non-positive weights, has 1-dimensional zero weight component and is ind-conilpotent as a coalgebra. Then we have

\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\textnormal{coBar}(H))\simeq\textnormal{coBar}(\textnormal{rev-comult}(H^{\vee}))\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)).

Proof.

We apply the standard “red-shift” trick: namely, consider the braided monoidal auto-equivalence

\textnormal{Shift}:\Rep_{q}(T)\to\Rep_{q}(T)\hskip 10.00002pt\left(A=\bigoplus_{{\check{\lambda}}}A^{\check{\lambda}}\right)\mapsto\bigoplus_{{\check{\lambda}}}A^{{\check{\lambda}}}[2\textnormal{ht}({\check{\lambda}})]

Our assumption on
\displaystyle H
guarantees that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shift}(H)
is a
connected
conilpotent bialgebra (i.e. its coaugmentation coideal is concentrated in purely positive cohomological degrees). In such case,
[
GY16
, Corollary 0.2]
(more precisely, its evident generalization to
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}
-graded vector spaces) guarantees that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Bar}\circ\textnormal{coBar}(\textnormal{Shift}(H))\simeq\textnormal{Shift}(H)
, from which we know that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Bar}\circ\textnormal{coBar}(H)\simeq H
as well.
Thus we compute

\textnormal{KD}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\textnormal{coBar}(H))\simeq(\textnormal{Bar}^{(2)}(\textnormal{coBar}(H))^{\vee})^{\textnormal{rev}}\simeq(\textnormal{Bar}(H)^{\vee})^{\textnormal{rev}}\simeq\textnormal{coBar}(\textnormal{rev-comult}(H^{\vee}))

where the last step follows from definition.
∎

2.8
Quantum Groups

Definition 2.8.1

(Quantum Groups)
.

Let
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{free}}(N^{-})
denote the bialgebra internal to
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
generated by
\displaystyle\{f_{i}\}
, where
\displaystyle i
ranges over the set of negative simple roots
\displaystyle\{-\alpha_{i}\}
, and
\displaystyle f_{i}
is of degree
\displaystyle-\alpha_{i}
. It lies in the heart and has a
Hopf algebra
structure, and has comultiplication given by

f_{i}\mapsto f_{i}\tensor 1+1\tensor f_{i}.

Assuming the condition on
\displaystyle q
above
, we define
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N)
be the quotient of
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{free}}(N^{-})
by the two-sided ideal generated by the quantum Serre relations as defined in
[
Gai21a
, Section 3.2.7]
.

We define
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}(N)
as the graded dual of
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-})
; it is again a Hopf algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
.

Definition 2.8.2
.

Given any algebra
\displaystyle A
in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, we set

A\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))_{\textnormal{loc.nilp}}

as the ind-completion of the category of finite-dimensional
\displaystyle A
-modules in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
.

Remark 2.8.3
.

If
\displaystyle A
is a bialgebra, then
\displaystyle A\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))_{\textnormal{loc.nilp}}
gains the structure of an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-algebra
internal to

\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)\operatorname{-mod}^{r}(\textnormal{DGCat})
.

Definition 2.8.4
.

We define

\textnormal{Rep}_{q}(B):=U_{q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}(N)\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{Rep}_{q}(T))_{\textnormal{loc.nilp}}.

and its relative Drinfeld center

\textnormal{Rep}_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G):=Z_{\textnormal{Dr},\textnormal{Rep}_{q}(T)}(\textnormal{Rep}_{q}(B)):=\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{2},/\Rep_{q}(T)}(A\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))_{\textnormal{loc.nilp}})

via Definition
12.1.7
.

Remark 2.8.5
.

In other words,
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)
is the universal
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-category acting from the left on
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(B)
, in a way that is compatible with the
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
-action on the right. For an even more explicit description, see
[
Gai21
, Section 4.4.2]
.

By Theorem
12.0.2
,
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)
coincides with
\displaystyle\Omega_{q}\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
, where
\displaystyle\Omega_{q}:=\textnormal{coBar}(U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-}))
. There is an obvious forgetful functor

\oblv_{\textnormal{mxd}\to\textnormal{Lus}}:\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)\to\Rep_{q}(B);

whereas the following is less evident:

Lemma 2.8.6
.

The forgetful functor
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)\xrightarrow{\oblv_{\textnormal{mxd}\to\textnormal{Lus}}}\Rep_{q}(B)\xrightarrow{\oblv}\Rep_{q}(T)
factors through another forgetful functor

\oblv_{\textnormal{mxd}\to\textnormal{KD}^{-}}:\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)\to U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-})\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T)).

The proof of this will be delayed until Section
12.2
.

Remark 2.8.7
.

As explained in
[
Gai21
]
, both
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(B)
and
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)
are equipped with canonical
\displaystyle t
-structures, such that heart of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Rep}_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)
can be explicitly described as graded vector spaces equipped with a locally nilpotent action of
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}(N)
and another action of
\displaystyle U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-})
. We will not need this description in this paper.

Definition 2.8.8

(Definition-Construction)
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{ind}_{\textnormal{Lus}\to\textnormal{mxd}}:\Rep_{q}(B)\to\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)
denote the left adjoint of
\displaystyle\oblv_{\textnormal{mxd}\to\textnormal{Lus}}
, and let
\displaystyle\textnormal{coind}_{\textnormal{KD}^{-}\to\textnormal{mxd}}
denote the right adjoint of
\displaystyle\oblv_{\textnormal{mxd}\to\textnormal{KD}^{-}}
.

We define the quantum
Verma
modules
\displaystyle\mathbb{M}_{q}^{{\check{\lambda}},\textnormal{mxd}}
, for each
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}\in\check{\Lambda}
, as

\mathbb{M}_{q,\textnormal{mxd}}^{{\check{\lambda}}}:=\textnormal{ind}_{\textnormal{Lus}\to\textnormal{mxd}}(k^{{\check{\lambda}}}).

and the quantum dual Verma modules
\displaystyle\mathbb{M}_{q}^{{\check{\lambda}},\textnormal{mxd},\vee}
as

\mathbb{M}_{q,\textnormal{mxd}}^{{\check{\lambda}},\vee}:=\textnormal{coind}_{\textnormal{KD}^{-}\to\textnormal{mxd}}(k^{{\check{\lambda}}}).

It then follows from definition that these objects satisfy the right orthogonal property, and that
\displaystyle\mathbb{M}_{q}^{{\check{\lambda}},\textnormal{mxd},\vee}
form a set of compact generators of this category.

Definition 2.8.9

(Contragredient Duality)
.

As shown in
[
Gai21
, Section 8.3.1]
, the graded linear duality on
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
induces a duality

\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)^{\vee}\simeq\Rep_{q^{-1}}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G),

in a way compatible with the forgetful functor down to the quantum torus. We will let
\displaystyle\mathbb{D}_{\textnormal{Quant}}
denote the resulting contravariant functor on compact objects. As expected, we have

\mathbb{D}_{\textnormal{Quant}}(\mathbb{M}_{q}^{{\check{\lambda}},\textnormal{mxd}})\simeq\mathbb{M}_{q^{-1},\textnormal{mxd}}^{-{\check{\lambda}}-2\check{\rho}}[\dim(\mathfrak{n})].

2.9
Categorical Verdier Duality

Convention 2.9.1
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
be the (rectlinear) little 2-disk operad introduced in
[
Lur12
, 5.1.0.2]
, and let
\displaystyle(\mathbb{E}_{2})_{\textnormal{BSO}(2)}
be the variant introduced in
[
Lur12
, 5.4.2.16]
where we allow orientation-preserving rotation of the disk. By considering the canonical tangent
\displaystyle\textnormal{SO}(2)
-bundle, a
\displaystyle(\mathbb{E}_{2})_{\textnormal{BSO}(2)}
-algebra structure gives rise to an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}
-algebra structure (defined in
[
Lur12
, 5.4.5.1]
) for any smooth 2-dimensional manifold
\displaystyle M
.

Definition 2.9.2
.

By an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, we mean an element of the category
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
. Likewise we have the notion of a
\displaystyle(\mathbb{E}_{2})_{\textnormal{BSO}(2)}
DG category and a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}
DG category.

Let
\displaystyle X
be a smooth algebraic curve over
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
. In
[
GL19
, Section 29.4]
, authors of
loc.cit
. appealed to (without proof) the following folklore result:

•

Given a
\displaystyle(\mathbb{E}_{2})_{\textnormal{BSO}(2)}
DG category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, one can (by considering the tangent bundle) obtain a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
DG category then a
topological
factorization category
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathcal{C})
over
\displaystyle X(\mathbb{C})
;

•

Moreover, to each
\displaystyle(\mathbb{E}_{2})_{\textnormal{BSO}(2)}
algebra
\displaystyle A
internal to
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, one can attach first a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-algebra then a factorization algebra
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(A)
within
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathcal{C})
, and there is an equivalence of DG categories between the category of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-modules of
\displaystyle A
inside
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
and (non-unital) factorization modules of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(A)
supported at one point inside
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathcal{C})
.

In Section
6
we give a full proof of this result; the precise statement is given in Proposition
6.3.3
, Corollary
6.3.6
and Proposition
6.3.8
.

Remark 2.9.3
.

One categorical level down, the strategy is clear: first apply
[
Lur12
, 5.5.4.10]
, then apply covariant Verdier duality. On the categorical level there is no Verdier duality, so the crux of the proof is to construct a functor from the latter to the former.

Remark 2.9.4
.

The concept of an (algebraic) factorization category, a topological factorization category, and an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-category are
all inequivalent
concepts. For intuition purpose one can sometimes think of the first two as various kinds of
lax

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure; we do not attempt to make this intuition precise.

Our input
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
category is
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
. In Section
7
, we further identify the output with the topological factorization category of
\displaystyle q
-twisted analytic sheaves over the
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}
. We let
\displaystyle\Omega_{\mathbb{E}_{2},q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}
denote the topological factorization algebra obtained from (the augmentation ideal of)
\displaystyle\Omega_{q}\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))
. It thus remains to show:

Proposition 2.9.5
.

\displaystyle\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
and
\displaystyle\Omega_{\mathbb{E}_{2},q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}
correspond to each other under the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence (defined in Section
13
).

The proof of this statement will again be delayed until Section
8
. As explained in the introduction, this finishes the proof of our main theorem.

Remark 2.9.6
.

By this comparison result and the
\displaystyle*
-fiber computation from Proposition

C_{*}(U_{q^{-1}}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-}),k)\simeq\begin{cases}\mathbb{C}[-\ell(w_{f})]&{\check{\lambda}}=w_{f}(\check{\rho})-\check{\rho},w_{f}\in W_{\textnormal{fin}}\\
0&\textnormal{else}\end{cases}

holds true for all levels that satisfy Condition

. For
\displaystyle q
a root of unity of odd order (along with some slightly more stringent conditions) this was established purely algebraically in

]
; we note that our result also provides a proof for the even order case that was not covered by

.

It follows from construction that the equivalence (at positive level) sends

and intertwines

.

3
Factorizable Kazhdan–Lusztig Category

We begin by developing the factorizable Kazhdan–Lusztig category. Throughout this section we will freely use results from Section
11
.

3.1
The Players

Notation 3.1.1
.

In this section, we use the following notations:

•

\displaystyle X
is a smooth separated algebraic curve, and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}:=\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}(X)
is the corresponding unital Ran space;

•

\displaystyle H
is a finite type affine algebraic group;

•

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the corr-unital factorization group whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is the loop group
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}H_{x}
(see Section
10
);

•

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the co-unital factorization group whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is the arc group
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x}
(see Section
10
);

•

We have a strictly
unital
morphism
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to\mathcal{L}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
;

•

\displaystyle[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the unital factorization space whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is the affine Grassmannian
\displaystyle[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{x}\simeq\mathcal{L}H_{x}/\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x}
(see Section
10
);

•

We have a strictly
co-unital
morphism
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
;

•

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the formal completion of
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
along
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, which inherits a corr-unital factorization structure whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}\simeq\mathcal{L}H_{x}\times_{[\mathcal{L}H_{x}]_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x}]_{\textnormal{dR}}
;

•

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the formal completion of
\displaystyle[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
along its unit section, which inherits a unital factorization structure whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}]_{x}\simeq\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}/\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x}
;

•

\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the classifying space of
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, which inherits a co-unital factorization structure whose fiber at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
is the quotient stack
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x}
;

•

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the Cech nerve of
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to[\mathbb{B}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, which is a cosimplicial object in the category of corr-unital factorization spaces and strictly unital morphisms. Explicitly,

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}:=[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\backslash\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}\cdots\times^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}/\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}},

where there are
\displaystyle m
terms of
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}
on the RHS. In the degenerate case
\displaystyle m=0
,

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}:=[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}.

Remark 3.1.2
.

The following description is helpful for understanding the corr-unital structure on
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
. Let
\displaystyle\phi:I\to J
be an injective map between finite sets. Recall the above corr-unital structure should provide the following correspondence

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{J}\leftarrow[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

between (convergent) prestacks. Unwinding the definitions, for an affine test scheme
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}
, the groupoid
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}(S)
classifies the following data (i)-(iv):

(i)

Maps
\displaystyle x_{j}:S\to X
labelled by
\displaystyle J
.

Let
\displaystyle\Gamma_{J}\to S\times X
(resp.
\displaystyle\Gamma_{I}\to S\times X
) be the schema-theoretic sum of the graphs of all the
\displaystyle x_{j}
(resp. of
\displaystyle x_{\phi(i)}
for
\displaystyle i\in I
). Note that we have a closed embedding
\displaystyle\Gamma_{I}\to\Gamma_{J}
.

(ii)

\displaystyle H
-torsors
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{0},\cdots,\mathcal{P}_{m}
on the adic multi-disk
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}
and isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]|_{\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]|_{\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}}

between their restrictions on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}
.

(iii)

Isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}},

where we view
\displaystyle[\mathcal{P}_{k}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}
as a
\displaystyle G
-torsor on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}
.

By restriction, (ii) and (iii) provides two chains of isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]|_{\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]|_{\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}.

(iv)

An isomorphism between the above two chains.

Recall
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{J}=[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\operatorname{Id}_{J}}
. Now the correspondence

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{J}(S)\leftarrow[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}(S)\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}(S)

is induced by the obvious op-correspondence

\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{J}\to\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{J}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}\leftarrow\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{I}}^{\prime}\setminus\Gamma_{I}.

Remark 3.1.3
.

In the special case when
\displaystyle m=1
and
\displaystyle I=\emptyset
, the correspondence

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{J}\leftarrow[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

is just

[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\backslash\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}/\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{J}\leftarrow[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{J}\to X^{J}.

We need the following techinical lemmas:

Lemma 3.1.4
.

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
satisfies
\displaystyle(\spadesuit)
in Construction
11.11.13
.

Proof.

By Remark
11.11.14
and Remark
3.1.2
, we only need to check

(a)

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle X^{J}
;

(b)

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}
is
\displaystyle*
-pullable;

(c)

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{J}
is an ind-(afp, affine and proper) apaisant indshematic morphism.

Consider the prestack
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{\phi}
that classifies data (i)-(iv) as in Remark
3.1.2
and

(v)

A trivialization of
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{0}
.

We have

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}\simeq[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{I}\backslash[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{\phi}.

Note that when
\displaystyle\phi=\operatorname{Id}_{J}
,
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{J}
is just the formal completion of
\displaystyle[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{J}\times_{X^{J}}\cdots\times_{X^{J}}[\operatorname{Gr}_{H}]_{J}
along its unit section. Moreover, using Beauville-Laszlo descent theorem, one can show that the map

[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

is an equivalence. This implies
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{\phi}
is a classical laft ind-scheme which is ind-(affine and proper) over
\displaystyle X^{J}
. As in Example
11.10.6
, this implies (a).

(b) follows from the fact that

[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{\phi}\simeq[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

is a flat apaisant cover of both
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}
and
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}
.

(c) follows from the fact that

[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{\times m}]_{J}

is a closed embedding.

∎

Lemma 3.1.5
.

For any
\displaystyle[m]\to[n]
in
\displaystyle\Delta
and any
\displaystyle\phi:I\to J
between finite sets, the morphism

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{n}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}]_{\phi}

is
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable.

Proof.

We can assume
\displaystyle[m]\to[n]
sends
\displaystyle 0
to
\displaystyle 0
. Then the proof of Lemma
3.1.4
implies the desired map can be obtained from

[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{n}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Gr}}_{H}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

by taking
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{J}
-quotient. This makes the claim manifest.

∎

Remark 3.2.14
.

Via the equivalence (
9
), the unital factorization structure on the LHS corresponds to the following canonical unital structure on the RHS. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
be any unital factorization functor and
\displaystyle L:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}
be a lax unital factorization monad such that
\displaystyle L\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{C})
is a factorization category
17
17

17

This is true if and only if for any
\displaystyle S_{\textnormal{dR}}\to T_{\textnormal{dR}}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
, the canonical functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\operatorname{-mod}(\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C}))\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{DMod}(S)\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\operatorname{-mod}[\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{DMod}(S)]

is an equivalence.
. Then
\displaystyle L\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{C})
has a canonical unital factorization structure such that
\displaystyle\operatorname{ind}:\mathcal{C}\to L\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{C})
is strictly unital. To see this, let
\displaystyle T
be an affine test point and
\displaystyle\mathfrak{t}:f\to g
be a morphism in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}(T)
. The desired unital functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(f_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\operatorname{-mod}(\mathbf{\Gamma}(f_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C}))\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\operatorname{-mod}(\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C}))

is induced by the functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(f_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\mathfrak{t}_{!}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ind}_{g_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\operatorname{-mod}(\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C}))

and the following canonical action of
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(f_{\textnormal{dR}},L)
on this functor:

\operatorname{ind}_{g_{\textnormal{dR}}}\circ\mathfrak{t}_{!}\circ\mathbf{\Gamma}(f_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\to\operatorname{ind}_{g_{\textnormal{dR}}}\circ\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},L)\circ\mathfrak{t}_{!}\to\operatorname{ind}_{g_{\textnormal{dR}}}\circ\mathfrak{t}_{!},

where the first natural transformation is provided by the lax unital structure of
\displaystyle L
, and the second natural transformation is the action of
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(g_{\textnormal{dR}},L)
on
\displaystyle\operatorname{ind}_{g_{\textnormal{dR}}}
.

3.3
The Twisted Version

Definition 3.3.1
.

A
multiplicative (unital) factorization line bundle
on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is a co-monoidal moprhism

\mathscr{L}:\mathbf{1}\to[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}),\operatorname{mult}^{!}]

between co-algebra objects in
\displaystyle[\operatorname{FactCat}_{\operatorname{un}}]_{\operatorname{lax-unital}}
such that the corresponding unital factorization algebra in
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H})
is invertible for the symmetric monoidal structure
\displaystyle[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}),\overset{!}{\otimes}]
.

We denote this unital factorization algebra in
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H})
by the same symbol
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
, and treat the other data in the above definition as implicit.

Example 3.3.2
.

The
\displaystyle!
-pullback functor along
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to\operatorname{pt}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
provides a multiplicative factorization line bundle, whose underlying unital factorization algbera is
\displaystyle\omega_{\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}}
.

Remark 3.3.3
.

By definition, for a multiplicative factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, we have

\operatorname{mult}^{!}(\mathscr{L})\simeq\mathscr{L}\boxtimes\mathscr{L},\;e^{!}(\mathscr{L})\simeq\omega_{\operatorname{pt}}

as unital factorization algebras in
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times\widehat{\mathcal{L}H})
(resp. in
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\operatorname{pt})
).

Remark 3.3.4
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
be a multiplicative factorization line bundle on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
. For any
\displaystyle s:S\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}
with
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, we obtain an invertible object

\mathscr{L}_{s}\in[\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s}),\overset{!}{\otimes}].

By the proof of
[
Ras20a
, Proposition 9.4.2]
, there exists a unique invertible object

\mathscr{L}_{s}^{\operatorname{QCoh}}\in[\textnormal{QCoh}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s}),\otimes]

such that
\displaystyle\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{s}^{\operatorname{QCoh}})\simeq\mathscr{L}_{s}
. Such an object is classified by a morphism
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s}\to\mathbb{BG}_{m}\times\mathbb{Z}
. The multiplicative structure on
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
can upgrade this morphism to a group homomorphism (lying over the projection
\displaystyle S\to\operatorname{pt}
). Since the fibers of
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s}\to S
are connected, this group homomorphism factors through
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s}\to\mathbb{BG}_{m}
. It follows that
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{s}^{\operatorname{QCoh}}
is indeed a line bundle in
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{s})^{\heartsuit}
and our definition of multiplicative factorization line bundle (via
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}
-theory) is essentially equivalent to that in
[
Zha17
]
defined via
\displaystyle\operatorname{QCoh}
-theory.

Remark 3.3.5
.

By Remark
3.3.4
, for a unital factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
and fixed equivalences
\displaystyle\operatorname{mult}^{!}(\mathscr{L})\simeq\mathscr{L}\boxtimes\mathscr{L},\;e^{!}(\mathscr{L})\simeq\omega_{\operatorname{pt}}
, there is at most one multiplicative structure on
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
whose structure equivalences are given by these fixed equivalences. In other words, the higher compatibilities in the definition of multiplicative factorization line bundles are
properties rather than additional data
.

Construction 3.3.6
.

For multiplicative factorization line bundles
\displaystyle\mathscr{L},\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, we define multiplicative factorization line bundles
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}\overset{!}{\otimes}\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
and
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{-1}
in the obvious way.

Definition 3.3.7
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
be a multiplicative factorization line bundle on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
. Let

\mathscr{L}|_{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}\in\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}^{+}H})

be the unital factorization algebra obtained as the image of
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
under the lax-unital factorization functor

!\operatorname{-pull}:\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H})\to\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}).

We say
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
is trivial on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H
, or
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}|_{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}
is trivial
if the unital morphism
\displaystyle\omega_{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}\to\mathscr{L}|_{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}
is an isomorphism.

Construction 3.3.8
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}

\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H

\displaystyle!

By construction, for any
\displaystyle[m]
, we have an isomorphism
18
18

18

When
\displaystyle m=0

!\operatorname{-pull}:\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H})\to\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H)

Example 3.3.9
.

We have the following multiplicative factorization line bundle

Remark 3.3.11
.

\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}
can also be defined as a geometric realization or totalization as follows. There is a functor

\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet})_{\mathscr{L},\Delta}:\Delta\to[\operatorname{FactCat}_{\operatorname{un}}]_{\operatorname{lax-unital}}

(p_{f})^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(-)\overset{!}{\otimes}(p_{f^{\leftarrow}})^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}}):\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m})\to\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{n}),

where

\displaystyle f^{\leftarrow}(0)=0,f^{\leftarrow}(1)=f(0)
. The higher compatibilities are provided by the multiplicative structure
19
19

19

For instance, the composition laws are provided by

p_{(g\circ f)^{\leftarrow}}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}})\simeq p_{g^{\leftarrow}}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}})\overset{!}{\otimes}p_{(g\circ f^{\leftarrow})}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}}).

of
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
.
By passing to left adjoints, we also have a functor

As in Remark

In particular, the sections of

Remark 3.3.12

(p_{f})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}[(p_{f^{\leftarrow}})^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}})\overset{\operatorname{act}}{\otimes}-]:\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{n})\to\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}).

As before, we have

\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}^{-1},\operatorname{co}}\simeq\lim\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet})_{\mathscr{L}^{-1},\Delta}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet})_{\mathscr{L}^{-1},\Delta^{\textnormal{op}}}.

Remark 3.3.13
.

Similar to the non-twisted version,
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}^{-1},\operatorname{co}}
are dual to each other in the symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle[\operatorname{FactCat}_{\operatorname{un}}]_{\operatorname{lax-unital}}
.

Remark 3.3.14
.

One should think
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
as a
factorization gerbe
on
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
equipped with a trivialization on
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, and
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}
as the unital factorization category for the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
-theory on
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
twisted by this gerbe.

Remark 3.3.15
.

Let
\displaystyle x\in X
be a closed point. The group homomorphism
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}\to\mathbb{BG}_{m}
in Remark

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}

\displaystyle{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}_{x}

\displaystyle\operatorname{Vect}
whose restriction on
\displaystyle{\mathcal{L}^{+}H}_{x}

\displaystyle\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathscr{L}_{x}}

3.4
The Tate Line Bundle

The goal of this subsection is to prove the following result:

Theorem 3.4.1
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
be a multiplicative factorization line bundle on
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
that is trivial on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H
. Then there exists a canonical equivalence

\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}\simeq\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}},\operatorname{co}}

in
\displaystyle\operatorname{FactCat}_{\operatorname{un}}
.

Remark 3.4.2
.

For any closed point
\displaystyle x\in X

[
Ras20a
, Proposition 7.18.2]
and
[
Ras20a

provides
an

\displaystyle[\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}]_{x}\simeq[\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}},\operatorname{co}}]_{x}
. We will explain in Remark
3.4.3
how to identify it with the restriction of our equivalence at
\displaystyle x
.

\displaystyle\mathbf{1}\simeq\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\operatorname{pt})\xrightarrow{!-\operatorname{pull}}\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m})\xrightarrow{!-\operatorname{push}}\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m}\times_{(\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H)}\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{m})\to
