Remark 3.4.3
.

In this remark, we sketch how to identify the restriction of our equivalence in Theorem
3.4.1
at a closed point
\displaystyle x\in X
with the equivalence constructed in
[
Ras20a
]
.

We need to translate Raskin’s construction to our setting.
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 7.17.4]
says the monoidal category
\displaystyle A:=[\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}([\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}]_{x}),\star]
is rigid
21
21

21

This is related to the following fact, which we do not prove nor use in this paper. Consider the lax unital factorization functor:

\lambda:\mathcal{I}ndCoh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{1})\overset{e^{!,\textnormal{ren}}}{\to}\mathcal{I}ndCoh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{0})\overset{?\operatorname{-push}}{\to}\mathcal{I}ndCoh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\operatorname{pt})\simeq\mathbf{1},

where
\displaystyle e:\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{0}\to\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{1}
is the morphism corresponding to the unique map
\displaystyle[1]\to[0]
. Then
\displaystyle[\mathcal{I}ndCoh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}),\star,\lambda]
is a Frobenius algebra object in
\displaystyle[\operatorname{FactCat}_{\operatorname{un}}]_{\operatorname{lax-unital}}
(see
[
Lur12
, Definition 4.6.5.1]
). A rigid monoidal DG category is in particular a Frobenius algebra object in
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}
, and Raskin’s construction actually only used this Frobenius algebra structure.
One can use this fact to obtain an equivalence
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}\simeq\mathcal{KL}^{*}(H)_{\mathscr{L}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Serre}}}
, where
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Serre}}
is a multiplicative factorization line bundle such that the
Serre automorphism
for the above Frobenius algebra (see
[
Lur12
, Remark 4.6.5.4]
) is given by tensoring up with
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Serre}}
. However, it is harder to identify
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Serre}}
with
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}}
. For instance, Raskin proved (the non-factorization version) of this identification in
[
Ras20a
, Theorem 9.16.1]
with the help of semi-infinite cohomologies.
. Consider the
geometric
left and right actions of
\displaystyle A
on
\displaystyle M:=\operatorname{Rep}(\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x})
defined respectively by (
8
) and (
11
), it is clear that these actions commute hence make
\displaystyle M
an
\displaystyle(A,A)
-bimodule. One can verify that tensoring up with
\displaystyle[\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}_{H}}}]_{x}
is a monoidal automorphism on
\displaystyle A
. Using this automorphism, we can twist the
\displaystyle A
-actions on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Rep}(\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x})
and obtain another
\displaystyle(A,A)
-bimodule
\displaystyle M_{\mathscr{L}}
.

In Raskin’s language, the left
\displaystyle A
-module structure on
\displaystyle M_{\mathscr{L}}
is the same as a weak
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}
-action on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Vect}
. Denote the corresponding weak
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}
-module by
\displaystyle C_{\mathscr{L}}
. The invariance and coinvariance are defined respectively as
\displaystyle(C_{\mathscr{L}})^{\operatorname{inv}}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{A\operatorname{-mod}^{l}}(M,M_{\mathscr{L}})
and
\displaystyle(C_{\mathscr{L}})_{\operatorname{coinv}}:=M\otimes_{A}M_{\mathscr{L}}
. One can verify that the cosimplicial (resp. simplicial) diagram defining them satsifies the Beck-Chevalley conditions, which implies

(C_{\mathscr{L}})^{\operatorname{inv}}\simeq[\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}]_{x},\;(C_{\mathscr{L}})_{\operatorname{coinv}}\simeq[\mathcal{KL}^{*}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}]_{x}.

In
[
Ras20a
, Proposition 7.18.2]
, Raskin used the general theory of rigid monoidal categories to obtain an equivalence

(C_{\mathscr{L}})^{\operatorname{inv}}\simeq(C_{\mathscr{L}}\otimes\chi_{\operatorname{Serre}})_{\operatorname{coinv}},

where
\displaystyle\chi_{\operatorname{Serre}}
is the weak
\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}_{x}
-module twisted from the trivial one by the
Serre automorphism

\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}
(see
[
Lur12
, Remark 4.6.5.4]
) on the rigid monoidal category
\displaystyle A
. Hence we only need to identify
\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}
with
\displaystyle[\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}_{H}}}]_{x}\otimes^{!}(-)
as symmetric monoidal functors. Recall the underlying endo-functor of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}
is the difference of two self-dualities on
\displaystyle A
whose pairing functors are

A\otimes A\xrightarrow{\star}A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{unit}_{\star},-)}\operatorname{Vect},\;A\otimes A\xrightarrow{\star^{\operatorname{rev}}}A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{unit}_{\star},-)}\operatorname{Vect}.

Using the base-change isomorphisms, we have
\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{unit}_{\star},x\star y)\simeq<\sigma^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(x),y>_{1}
, where
\displaystyle<-,->_{1}
is the pairing in Step 1 of our proof of Theorem
3.4.1
for the case
\displaystyle i=m=1
. Similarly we have
\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{unit}_{\star},y\star x)\simeq<\sigma^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(x),y>_{0}
. Since
\displaystyle\sigma^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
is an involution, we obtain
\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}\simeq\theta_{1}^{-1}\circ\theta_{0}
. Hence our proof of Theorem
3.4.1
provides an equivalence
\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}\simeq[\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}_{H}}}]_{x}\otimes^{!}(-)
as endo-functors. Now the monoidal structure on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Se}_{A}
would correspond to
some
multiplicative structure on
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\operatorname{Tate}}
. We only need to show it coincides with the standard one. But this follows from unwinding the definitions.

3.5
Variant: Factorization Module Category

We also need a factorization module version of the previous constructions. We introduce the following notations.

Notation 3.5.1
.

We use the following notations:

•

\displaystyle K\to H
is a fixed closed subgroup of
\displaystyle H
.

•

\displaystyle x:\operatorname{pt}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
is a fixed point of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
, which corresponds to a finite set
\displaystyle I_{0}\subset\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{pt},X)
, or equivalently, to closed points
\displaystyle x_{i}
of
\displaystyle X
labelled by
\displaystyle I_{0}
.

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}
is the laft lax prestack defined in Section
10
, and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
is its de-Rham lax prestack.

•

\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}:=[\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
, and similarly define
\displaystyle[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
.

•

\displaystyle H_{x}:=\prod_{j\in J}H_{x_{j}}:=\prod_{j\in J}H
and similarly define
\displaystyle K_{x}
.

•

\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}:=[\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}
, which is a co-unital factorization module space of
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
supported on
\displaystyle x
.

•

\displaystyle[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}:=[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}
is the formal completion of
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
along
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, which is a corr-unital factorization module space of
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}H]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
supported on
\displaystyle x
.

•

\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is the Cech nerve of
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}(\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x})]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to[\mathbb{B}(\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}})]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
, which is a cosimplicial corr-unital factorization module space of
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
.

Remark 3.5.2
.

By definition, we have

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\simeq[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x}^{\times(\bullet+1)}}\mathbb{B}K_{x}^{\times(\bullet+1)}.

Variant 3.5.3
.

As in the definitions of
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}}
, we can define crystal of categories over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
:

\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}},\;\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}},

equipped respectively with unital factorization module structures for the unital factorization categories
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}}
.

We can also define a crystal of categories over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
:

\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathfrak{h}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}

equipped rwith unital factorization module structures for the unital factorization categories
\displaystyle\mathcal{R}ep(\mathcal{L}^{+}H)
.

Example 3.5.4
.

Recall a map
\displaystyle y:\operatorname{pt}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}
corresponds to a finite subset
\displaystyle I\subset\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{pt},X)
containing
\displaystyle I_{0}
. Then

[\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H}K}_{\mathscr{L}}]_{y}\simeq\bigotimes_{x_{i}\in I_{0}}\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}_{x_{i}}\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H_{x_{i}}\times_{H_{x_{i}}}K_{x_{i}}}_{\mathscr{L}}\bigotimes\bigotimes_{x_{i}\in I\setminus I_{0}}\operatorname{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L},x_{i}}.

3.6
Functoriality For the Group

Construction 3.6.1
.

Let
\displaystyle(K^{\prime}\to H^{\prime})
be another closed embedding between finite type affine algebraic groups, and
\displaystyle(K^{\prime}\to H^{\prime})\to(K\to H)
be group homomorphisms. Note that
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
induces a multiplicative factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}^{\prime}
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}H^{\prime}
.

Then the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors induce lax unital morphisms

\operatorname{res}:\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}}\to\mathcal{KL}(H^{\prime})_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}},\;\operatorname{res}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}}\to\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}^{\prime}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}\times_{H^{\prime}_{x}}K^{\prime}_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}}

compatible with the factorization structures, which we refer as the
factorization restriction functors
.

Dually, the
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors lax unital morphisms

\operatorname{C}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}_{\operatorname{co}}:\mathcal{KL}(H^{\prime})_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime},\operatorname{co}}\to\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}},\;\operatorname{C}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}_{\operatorname{co}}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}^{\prime}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}\times_{H^{\prime}_{x}}K^{\prime}_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime},\operatorname{co}}\to\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}}

compatible with the factorization structures, which we call the
co-version of the factorization semi-infinite cohomology functor
.

Using (the factorization module version of) Theorem
3.4.1
, we obtain a morphism

\operatorname{C}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}:\mathcal{KL}(H^{\prime})_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{-\operatorname{Tate}}_{H^{\prime}}}\to\mathcal{KL}(H)_{\mathscr{L}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{-\operatorname{Tate}}_{H}},\;\operatorname{C}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}^{\prime}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}\times_{H^{\prime}_{x}}K^{\prime}_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}^{\prime}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{-\operatorname{Tate}}_{H^{\prime}}}\to\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}\otimes\mathscr{L}^{-\operatorname{Tate}}_{H}}

compatible with the factorization structures, which we call the
the factorization semi-infinite cohomology functor
.

4
Localization and Local-Global Correspondence

Notation 4.0.1
.

We keep Notation
3.5.1
. Also,

•

\displaystyle X
is assumed to be proper.

•

The multiplicative factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
is constructed from a central
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-extension
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{h}}_{\mathcal{D}}
of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{h}_{\mathcal{D}}:=\mathfrak{h}\otimes\operatorname{Diff}_{X}
using the method in
[
Zha17
]
.

•

\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
is the moduli stack of
\displaystyle H
-torsors on
\displaystyle X
.

•

Let
\displaystyle(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}
be the prestack such that
\displaystyle(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}(S)
classifies

–

a finite subset
\displaystyle I\subset\operatorname{Maps}(S^{\operatorname{cl,red}},X)
;

Let
\displaystyle\Gamma_{I}\to S\times X
be the schema-theoretic sum of the graphs of the maps
\displaystyle S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\to X
;

–

an
\displaystyle H
-torsor on
\displaystyle X\times S
equipped with a trivialization on the adic multi-disk
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma_{I}}^{\prime}
.

•

\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}\simeq\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x}}\mathbb{B}K_{x}
is the moduli stack of
\displaystyle H
-torsors on
\displaystyle X
equipped with
\displaystyle K
-structures at
\displaystyle x_{j},j\in J
.

•

\displaystyle\mathscr{T}
is the twisting on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
constructed from the central
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-extension
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{h}}_{\mathcal{D}}
using the method in
[
Zha17
]
.

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}
is the DG category of
\displaystyle\mathscr{T}
-twisted D-modules on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}
.

Remark 4.0.2
.

Consider

(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}:=(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}\times_{\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}},

which is an
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
-torsor on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
. A standard re-gluing construction extend this
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
-action to an
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}H]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
-action. The restricted
\displaystyle[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
-action preserves the projection to
\displaystyle(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\textnormal{dR}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}
. Hence
\displaystyle\mathscr{T}
induces a
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}
-gerbe on

(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}/[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}

equipped with a trivialization on

(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}/[\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\simeq\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbb{B}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}

Note that
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbb{B}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}
is just the formal completion of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
along
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}
.

On the other hand, recall that the multiplicative factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
induces a
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}
-gerbe on
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
equipped with a trivialization on
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
. By restriction, we obtain another
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}
-gerbe on
\displaystyle(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}/[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
equipped with a trivialization on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbb{B}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
.

It follows from the assumption that the above two
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}
-gerbes are canonical isomorphic.

Remark 4.0.3
.

Let
\displaystyle H^{\prime}\to H
be a group homomorphism. Then
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{h}}_{\mathcal{D}}
induces a central
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-extension
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{h}^{\prime}}_{\mathcal{D}}
of
\displaystyle\mathfrak{h}^{\prime}_{\mathcal{D}}
. We often write
\displaystyle(\mathscr{T}^{\prime},\mathscr{L}^{\prime})
for the corresponding twisting and factorization multiplicative line bundle.

Example 4.0.4
.

Since
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
is smooth, the dualizing complex
\displaystyle K\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})
is invertible. Let
\displaystyle K[-\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})]
be the corresponding line bundle, where
\displaystyle\operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})
is the locally constant function of dimension. Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{K}
be the integral twisting on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
given by this line bundle. It follows from definitions that
\displaystyle-\mathscr{K}
corresponds to the Tate central
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-extension.

The following result summarizes what we need to know about chiral localization.

.

Remark 4.0.6
.

Consider the following correspondence

\displaystyle(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\textnormal{dR}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}\leftarrow(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}/[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\to

\displaystyle\to[\mathbb{B}\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}

The morphism
\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}
should be viewed as the pull-push along this correspondence for a suitable twisted renormalized
IndCoh
-theory.

Warning 4.0.7
.

We did not claim
\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}
or
\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}_{\operatorname{co}}
have any factorization structure. In fact,
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})_{\mathscr{T}}\boxtimes\mathbf{1}
is not even a weak factorization category.

Construction 4.1.1
.

Let
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},\bullet}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
be the Cech nerve of the map

\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}\to(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}})^{H\operatorname{-level}_{\infty}}/[\widehat{\mathcal{L}H}\times_{H_{x,\textnormal{dR}}}K_{x,\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}.

We have isomorphisms
\displaystyle[(\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},\bullet})_{\textnormal{dR}}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\simeq(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\textnormal{dR}}\times\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}
.

Remark 4.1.2
.

In the special case when
\displaystyle x:\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
corresponds to the empty set
\displaystyle\emptyset\subset\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{pt},X)
, we obtain
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{\bullet}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}}
. By definition, we have

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\simeq[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}\times_{\mathbb{B}H_{x}^{\times(\bullet+1)}}\mathbb{B}K_{x}^{\times(\bullet+1)}.

Lemma 4.1.3
.

Each
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x},m}]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}}
is a
unital
lax prestack over
\displaystyle\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}
. In particular, the connecting morphisms are strictly unital.

Proof.

By Remark
3.5.2
and Remark
4.1.2
, we can assume
\displaystyle x:\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
corresponds to the empty set (i.e., we ignore the
\displaystyle K
-level structures).

Let
\displaystyle\phi:I\to J
be an injective map between finite sets. To prove the claim, we only need to show the correspondence

[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{m}]_{J}\leftarrow[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{m}]_{\phi}\to[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{m}]_{I}\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}

(that provides the corr-unital structure) has a degenerate right arm. Explicitly,
\displaystyle[\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H,\operatorname{glob}}^{m}]_{\phi}(S)
classifies

(i)

Maps
\displaystyle x_{j}:S\to X
labelled by
\displaystyle J
.

Let
\displaystyle\Gamma_{J}\to S\times X
(resp.
\displaystyle\Gamma_{I}\to S\times X
) be the schema-theoretic sum of the graphs of all the
\displaystyle x_{j}
(resp. of
\displaystyle x_{\phi(i)}
for
\displaystyle i\in I
). Note that we have a closed embedding
\displaystyle\Gamma_{I}\to\Gamma_{J}
.

(ii)

\displaystyle H
-torsors
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{0},\cdots,\mathcal{P}_{m}
on
\displaystyle S\times X
and isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{I}}

between their restrictions on
\displaystyle(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{I}
.

(iii)

Isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}},

where we view
\displaystyle[\mathcal{P}_{k}]\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}
as a
\displaystyle G
-torsor on
\displaystyle S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\times X
.

By restriction, (ii) and (iii) provides two chains of isomorphisms

[\mathcal{P}_{0}]|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\simeq\cdots\simeq[\mathcal{P}_{m}]|_{(S\times X)\setminus\Gamma_{I}}\times_{S}S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}.

(iv)

An isomorphism between the above two chains.

This makes the claim manifest because (ii)-(iv) do not depend on
\displaystyle J
.

∎

.

Recall we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}\simeq\lim_{U}\textnormal{DMod}(U^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}
, where the connecting functors are given by pullbacks. Consider the following compositions of unital morphisms:

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}_{U}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}}\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}}\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh(U^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}))\xrightarrow{\operatorname{push}}\textnormal{DMod}(U^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}\boxtimes\mathbf{1}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}_{U,\operatorname{co}}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}}\xrightarrow{*\operatorname{-pull}}\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\operatorname{Hecke}}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}}\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh(U^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}}))\xrightarrow{\operatorname{push}}\textnormal{DMod}(U^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}\boxtimes\mathbf{1}.

They are functorial in
\displaystyle U
, i.e., compatible with the pullback functors
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(U_{1}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})\to\textnormal{DMod}(U_{2}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})
. Passing to limits, we obtain unital morphisms

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L}}\to\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}\boxtimes\mathbf{1}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}_{\operatorname{co}}:\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathfrak{h}}\operatorname{-}mod^{\mathcal{L}^{+}H\times_{H_{x}}K_{x}}_{\mathscr{L},\operatorname{co}}\to\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}^{K\operatorname{-level}_{x}})_{\mathscr{T}}\boxtimes\mathbf{1}.

4.4
Compatibility with Propogation

Our strategy for the proof of Theorem
4.0.5
(3-4) is to reduce to the case when the factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
(resp.
\displaystyle A^{\prime}
) is the unit factorization algebra. To achieve this reduction, we need to use the tool of
propogation of factorization modules
, and prove
\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}
and
\displaystyle\operatorname{Loc}_{\operatorname{co}}
are compatible with propogations. We first explain what these propogations mean.

Remark 4.4.1
.

The propagation method was initially introduced by Beilinson and Drinfeld in
[
BDD04
, 4.4.3 and 4.4.9]
. We emphasize that this technique
only exists in the unital setting
.

Construction 4.4.2
.

Consider the laft lax prestack

\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}):=S\mapsto\textnormal{Fun}([2],\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}(S)).

We have two projections

p_{s},p_{t}:\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})\to\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}

“remembering” respectively the source and the target. Note that we have a
\displaystyle 2
-morphism
\displaystyle\mathfrak{i}:p_{s}\to p_{t}
. We equip
\displaystyle\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})
with the factorization module space structure (for the factorization space
\displaystyle\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
) such that
\displaystyle p_{t}
is compatible with the factorization module structures but
\displaystyle p_{s}
is not. For a map
\displaystyle y:\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}
corresponding to a finite subset
\displaystyle J
with
\displaystyle I_{t}\cap J=\emptyset
, the map

(\operatorname{Ran}_{\operatorname{un}}\times\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}))_{\operatorname{disj}}\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})

sends
\displaystyle(y,z)
to the point corresponding to
\displaystyle I_{0}\subset I_{s}\subset J\sqcup I_{t}
.

Remark 4.4.3
.

Explicitly, a map
\displaystyle z:\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})
corresponds to a chain
\displaystyle I_{0}\subset I_{s}\subset I_{t}
of finite subsets of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{pt},X)
such that
\displaystyle I_{0}\subset I_{s}
(resp.
\displaystyle I_{0}\subset I_{t}
) corresponds to the composition
\displaystyle\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})\xrightarrow{p_{s}}\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}
(resp.
\displaystyle\operatorname{pt}\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})\xrightarrow{p_{t}}\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}
).

Construction 4.4.4

(Propogation of factorization modules)
.

Let
\displaystyle V\to W
be a morphism between laft prestacks. For any unital factorization category
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
over

\displaystyle W
-family of unital factorization categories over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{un,dR}}

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
-module
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
over
\displaystyle V\times\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un,dR}}

\displaystyle\mathbf{cores}_{p_{t,\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathcal{C})
, which is a crystal of categories over
\displaystyle V\times\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})_{\textnormal{dR}}
, inherits a factorization
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
-module structure. Moreover, for any unital factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
in
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
, there is a canonical functor

\operatorname{prop}_{A}:A\operatorname{-FactMod}_{\operatorname{un}}(\mathcal{C})\to A\operatorname{-FactMod}_{\operatorname{un}}(\mathbf{cores}_{p_{t,\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathcal{C}))

such that the following diagram commutes

Construction 4.4.5
.

In the special case when
\displaystyle A=\operatorname{unit}
is the unit factorization algebra of
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
, we have the following commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{B\operatorname{-FactMod}_{\operatorname{un}}(\mathcal{C})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

where
\displaystyle\operatorname{ins}_{\operatorname{unit}}
is the functor of
unit insertion

\operatorname{ins}_{\operatorname{unit}}:\mathbf{\Gamma}(\operatorname{Id}_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(p_{s,\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\xrightarrow{\mathfrak{i}_{!}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(p_{t,\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C}).

Digression: what is propagation?

Let us explain the name. Suppose
\displaystyle A
is a unital factorization algebra and
\displaystyle N
is its, such that its fiber at a
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-point

y:=[\{x\}\subseteq\{x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\}]\in\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})(\mathbb{C})

is given by some vector space
\displaystyle N_{0}\tensor A_{0}^{\tensor(n-1)}
. The map
\displaystyle y
induces a map

\left(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},y}:=S\mapsto\{\alpha:S\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}\mid(x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\subseteq\alpha\}\right)\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})

Then the pullback of
\displaystyle\textnormal{prop}_{A}(N)
along this map produces a unital
\displaystyle A
-factorization module on the former, which should be thought of as consisting of
\displaystyle(N_{0},A_{0},\ldots,A_{0})
supported at
\displaystyle(x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})
respectively. Thus, it can be seen as “propagating” the algebra
\displaystyle A
to other points on the curve.

Another perspective is as follows. As explained in
[
Ras15
]
, via étale hyperdescent the category of
\displaystyle A
-unital factorization modules in
\displaystyle C

itself
form a weak unital factorization category under
chiral fusion
, and the underlying sheaf of
\displaystyle\textnormal{prop}_{A}(N)
can be seen as observing
\displaystyle A
as an element
\displaystyle A^{\textnormal{enh}}\in\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\mathcal{C}))
and
\displaystyle N
as an element
\displaystyle N^{\textnormal{enh}}\in A^{\textnormal{enh}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\mathcal{C}))
.
This is, of course, evocative of the “enhancement” equivalences

\textnormal{AlgEnh}:\mathcal{O}\textnormal{-Alg}(\mathcal{C})_{A/}\simeq\mathcal{O}\textnormal{-Alg}(A\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}))

\textnormal{ModEnh}:A\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{AlgEnh}(A)\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathcal{O}}(A\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathcal{O}}(\mathcal{C}))

which holds for any coherent
\displaystyle\infty
-operad
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
, any (weakly)
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
-monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
and any
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
-algebra
\displaystyle A\in\mathcal{C}
, as established in
[
Lur12
, 3.4.1.7]
and
[
Lur12
, 3.4.1.9]
.

Construction 4.4.6
.

In the special case when
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
are the constant crystals, i.e.,
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}=\textnormal{IndCoh}(W)\boxtimes\mathbf{1}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}=\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\boxtimes\mathbf{1}
, the functor

\operatorname{res}:\mathbf{\Gamma}(\operatorname{Id}_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(\operatorname{p}_{t,\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{C})

is just

p_{t}^{!}:\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})).

Hence we obtain a natural transformation

\displaystyle\textstyle{B\operatorname{-FactMod}_{\operatorname{un}}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\boxtimes\mathbf{1})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\operatorname{prop}_{A}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\oblv}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})}
\displaystyle\textstyle{A\operatorname{-FactMod}_{\operatorname{un}}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\boxtimes\mathbf{cores}_{p_{t,\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathbf{1}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\oblv}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(\operatorname{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces,}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p_{t,!}}

(19)

The diagram (
19
) does not commute in general. But we have the following results:

Lemma 4.4.7

(Propogation-restriction Lemma for Chiral Homology)
.

The diagram (
19
) commutes after taking chiral homology, i.e., after composing with

\operatorname{C}_{x,\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{ch}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(V).

Recall
\displaystyle\operatorname{C}_{x,\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{ch}}
is given by
\displaystyle!
-pushforward along
\displaystyle p:\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}\to\operatorname{pt}
. In the case when
\displaystyle B=A
, the following stronger result is true:

Lemma 4.4.8

(Propogation Lemma for Chiral Homology)
.

The composition

p_{!}\circ p_{s,!}\circ p_{t}^{!}\simeq p_{!}\circ p_{t,!}\circ p_{t}^{!}\to p_{!}

in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Funct}(\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\operatorname{un}}))\to\operatorname{Vect}
is an equivalence. Moreover, the natural transformation

p_{s,!}\circ p_{t}^{!}\to p^{!}\circ p_{!}

is an equivalence.

Remark 4.4.9
.

Before we prove, let us explain the names.
For a set of unital
\displaystyle A
-factorization modules
\displaystyle N_{1},\ldots,N_{k}
inserted at distinct points
\displaystyle x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}\in X(\mathbb{C})
, let us write the chiral homology as

\langle N_{1},\ldots,N_{k}\rangle^{A}_{x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}};

Given a unital factorization
\displaystyle A
-module
\displaystyle M
supported at
\displaystyle x
, the equality between fibers of
\displaystyle p_{s,!}\circ p_{t}^{!}(M)
and
\displaystyle p^{!}\circ p_{!}(M)
at some
\displaystyle(x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})
, given by the propagation lemma for chiral homology, translates to

\langle M,A,\ldots,A\rangle^{A}_{x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}}\simeq\langle M\rangle^{A}_{x},

which says that when computing
\displaystyle A
-chiral homology, extra copies of
\displaystyle A
would not affect the result. The propagation-restriction lemma, on the other hand, roughly states that if
\displaystyle M
is a
\displaystyle B
-factorization module and
\displaystyle A\to B
is a map between unital factorization algebras, then we have

\left\langle\langle M\rangle_{x}^{A},\langle M,B\rangle_{x,x_{1}}^{A},\langle M,B,B\rangle_{x,x_{1},x_{2}}^{A},\ldots\right\rangle\simeq\langle M\rangle^{B}_{x}

where the LHS now ranges over all of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}
.

Proof for Lemma
4.4.8
.

Consider the pullback diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\times_{\{x\}}\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{q_{2}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{q_{1}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\{x\}}

We claim that
\displaystyle(q_{1})_{!}
is well-defined, and the natural transformation
\displaystyle(q_{1})_{!}\circ(q_{2})^{!}\Rightarrow p^{!}\circ p_{!}
is an isomorphism. Indeed, this can be checked by by first establishing the corresponding facts for the following diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\times_{R}\textnormal{Ran}_{x}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\{x\}}

using the fact that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x}
is pseudo-proper, then use the universal homological left cofinality of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{x}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}
, provable as in
[
Gai15a
, 4.6.2]
. There is a map of lax prestacks

\iota:\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}})\to\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\times_{\{x\}}\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\hskip 10.00002pt(I_{0}\subseteq I_{s}\subseteq I_{t})\mapsto((I_{0}\subseteq I_{s}),(I_{0}\subseteq I_{t}))

\textnormal{such that}\hskip 10.00002ptq_{2}\circ\iota\simeq p_{t}\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{and}\hskip 10.00002ptq_{1}\circ\iota\simeq p_{s}.

It suffices to establish that
\displaystyle\iota
is universally homologically left cofinal. As in
[
Gai15a
, 4.6.5]
, it suffices to check that for every affine
\displaystyle S
, every
\displaystyle S
-point

((I_{0}\subseteq I_{1}),(I_{0}\subseteq I_{2}))\in\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\times_{\{x\}}\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}(S),

and every
\displaystyle t:T\to S
where
\displaystyle T
is affine, the category

\{J\in\textnormal{Ran}(T),K\in\textnormal{Ran}(T),\alpha:I_{0}|_{t}\subseteq J\subseteq K~\textnormal{such that}~I_{1}|_{t}\subseteq J,I_{2}|_{t}\subseteq K\}

is a contractible category; but this category has an initial element given by
\displaystyle(I_{1}|_{t},I_{1}|_{t}\cup I_{2}|_{t})
.
∎

Proof for Lemma
4.4.7
.

We first prove the special case
\displaystyle A\simeq\textnormal{unit}_{\mathcal{A}}
, for
\displaystyle\eta_{B}:\textnormal{unit}_{\mathcal{A}}\to B
the canonical map attached to any factorization algebra
\displaystyle B
. Let
\displaystyle\iota_{s}:\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\to\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}})
be the inclusion map
\displaystyle(I_{0}\subseteq I_{1})\mapsto(I_{0}\subseteq I_{1}\subseteq I_{1})
. It follows from Proposition
10.6.1
and Proposition
10.5.22
that

\textnormal{res}_{\eta_{B}}:B\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\mathcal{C})\to\textnormal{unit}_{\mathcal{A}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\mathcal{C})

is isomorphic to the functor on
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
induced by

p_{s}^{!}\circ\iota_{s}^{!}:\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}))\to\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}})),

So it suffices to establish
\displaystyle p_{!}\circ(p_{s})_{!}\circ p_{s}^{!}\circ\iota_{s}^{!}\circ p_{t}^{!}\simeq p_{!}\circ(p_{s})_{!}\circ p_{s}^{!}\simeq p_{!}
, which follows from the homological contractibility of
\displaystyle p_{s}
.

Each
\displaystyle f:A\to B
comes with a natural map
\displaystyle\eta_{B}\to f
, which by functoriality of
\displaystyle\textnormal{res}_{f}
induces a natural transformation

\alpha:(\textnormal{id}\times p_{!})\circ\textnormal{prop}_{\textnormal{unit}_{\mathcal{A}}}\Rightarrow(\textnormal{id}\times p_{!})\circ\textnormal{prop}_{A};

unfolding the construction of
\displaystyle\textnormal{res}_{f}
we see that
\displaystyle\alpha
is induced by the following natural transformation of functors
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}))\to\textnormal{Vect}
:

\alpha_{\textnormal{univ}}:p_{!}\circ(p_{s})_{!}\circ(i\circ p_{s})^{!}\Rightarrow p_{!}\circ(p_{s})_{!}

which is in turn induced the natural transformation
\displaystyle i\circ p_{s}\Rightarrow\textnormal{id}
(here
\displaystyle i:\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}}\to\textnormal{Arrow}(\textnormal{Ran}_{x,\textnormal{un}})
is the map
\displaystyle I_{0}\subseteq I_{1}\mapsto I_{0}\subseteq I_{1}\subseteq I_{1}
). Thus it suffices to show that
\displaystyle\alpha_{\textnormal{univ}}
is an equivalence. We get this by observing that
\displaystyle i\circ p_{s}
is universally homologically left cofinal, which follows from the same argument as in the previous lemma.
∎
