L:=(\operatorname{pr}_{1}^{*,\operatorname{CommAlg}^{\operatorname{cc}}})^{L}:\operatorname{CommAlg}_{\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))\to\operatorname{CommAlg}_{\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})).

Using the assumption that
\displaystyle H^{\prime}\to H
is surjective with unipotent kernel, one can check that the maps

[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}},\;\operatorname{Bun}_{H^{\prime}}\to\operatorname{Bun}_{H}

are
co-affine
27
27

27

A map
\displaystyle Y\to Z
is co-affine if for any affine test scheme
\displaystyle S\to Z
, the fiber product
\displaystyle S\times_{Z}Y
is co-affine in the sense of
[
Lura
]
.
. Hence we have

[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}})\simeq\operatorname{cSpec}(O_{1}),\;\operatorname{Bun}_{H^{\prime}}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}\simeq\operatorname{cSpec}(O_{2}),

where

\operatorname{cSpec}:\operatorname{CommAlg}_{\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))\to\operatorname{PreStk}_{/\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}}

is the (relative) co-affine spectrum functor (see
[
Lura
, Section 4.4]
), it is charaterized by the functorial equivalences

\operatorname{Maps}_{\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}}(\operatorname{Spec}(A),\operatorname{cSpec}(O))\simeq\operatorname{Maps}_{\operatorname{CommAlg}_{\operatorname{un}}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))}(O,A)

for any
connective

\displaystyle A\in\operatorname{CommAlg}_{\operatorname{un}}^{\operatorname{cn}}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))
. Consider the Weyl retriction functor

W:\operatorname{PreStk}_{/\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to\operatorname{PreStk}_{/\operatorname{Bun}_{H}}.

For any affine test scheme
\displaystyle Y
over
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
, we have

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}_{\operatorname{Bun}_{H}}(Y,W([\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}})))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}_{\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}}(Y\times X_{\textnormal{dR}},[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}_{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(Y\times X_{\textnormal{dR}},[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}_{\mathbb{B}H\times X}(Y\times X,\mathbb{B}H^{\prime}\times X)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Maps}_{\operatorname{Bun}_{H}}(Y,\operatorname{Bun}_{H^{\prime}}),

where we use the fact that the Weyl restriction functor
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{/X}\to\operatorname{PreStk}_{/X_{\textnormal{dR}}}
sends
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}H\times X
to
\displaystyle[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}
. Hence

W([\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H^{\prime}]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}H]_{X_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H}\times X_{\textnormal{dR}}))\simeq\operatorname{Bun}_{H^{\prime}}.

Since
\displaystyle\operatorname{cSpec}
is fully faithful (see
[
Lura
, Theorem 4.4.1]
), we obtain

L(O_{1})\simeq q_{*}(O_{\operatorname{Bun}_{H^{\prime}}})\simeq L(O_{2})

as desired.

It remains to show
\displaystyle(\operatorname{pr}_{1}^{*,\operatorname{CommAlg}})^{L}(O_{1})
is coconnective. Let
\displaystyle\mathfrak{n}
be the Lie algebra of the kernel
\displaystyle H^{\prime}\to H
. Recall we have a
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-algebra
\displaystyle\mathfrak{n}_{D}:=\mathfrak{n}\otimes D_{X}\in\textnormal{DMod}(X)
. Similarly, we have a
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
-family of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-algebras
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}}\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(X)
such that its restriction at a
\displaystyle H
-torsor
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}\in\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
is the
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}^{*}
-algebra
\displaystyle(\mathfrak{n}_{D})_{\mathcal{P}}
twisted by
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}
(defined via the adjoint action of
\displaystyle H
on
\displaystyle\mathfrak{n}
). Let
\displaystyle C(\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}})\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})\otimes\textnormal{DMod}(X)
be the
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
-family of commutative algebras that is Koszul dual to
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}}
(see Proposition
10.6.5
). By definition,
\displaystyle O_{1}\simeq C(\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}})
. By
[
FG12
, Proposition 6.4.4]
, we have

(\operatorname{pr}_{1}^{*,\operatorname{CommAlg}})^{L}(C(\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}}))\simeq C\circ\Gamma(X_{\textnormal{dR}},\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}}),

where
\displaystyle\Gamma(X_{\textnormal{dR}},\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}})\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})
is a
\displaystyle\operatorname{Bun}_{H}
-family of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Lie}
-algebras, i.e., a Lie-algebra object in
\displaystyle\operatorname{QCoh}(\operatorname{Bun}_{H})
and
\displaystyle C\circ\Gamma(X_{\textnormal{dR}},\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}})
is its Koszul dual. Then we are done because
\displaystyle C\circ\Gamma(X_{\textnormal{dR}},\widetilde{\mathfrak{n}_{D}})
is clearly coconnective.

∎

5
Toric Fundamental Local Equivalence

The starting point is the following classical result due to
[
Con13
, Theorem 1.6.6]
:

Proposition 5.0.1
.

For any classical Noetherian scheme
\displaystyle S_{0}
, we have an isomorphism of
\displaystyle S
-group schemes

\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/S_{0}}(\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}

where
\displaystyle\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/S_{0}}
denotes the relative group homomorphism prestack,
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}
is the relative loop space over
\displaystyle S_{0}
, and
\displaystyle\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})
is the constant group scheme.

In particular this gives a map of group prestacks known as the
Contou-Carrère symbol

\langle\bullet,\bullet\rangle:\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times_{S_{0}}\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}\to\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}}.

At one point it can be described as follows (
[
BBE01
]
). The determinant line bundle on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}
determines a central extension
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}}
, and we have, for any test affine scheme
\displaystyle A
,

\langle f,g\rangle^{-1}=\tilde{f}\cdot\tilde{g}\cdot\tilde{f}^{-1}\cdot\tilde{g}^{-1}\in\mathbb{G}_{m}(A)

for any
\displaystyle f,g\in\mathbb{G}_{m}(K)(A)
and
\displaystyle\tilde{f},\tilde{g}
any lifting to the central extension. Since the central extension canonically splits on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}
, the pairing is canonically trivial on
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}
and thus induces another group homomorphism

\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times_{S_{0}}(\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}/\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m})\to\mathbb{G}_{m};

In fact, this pairing is perfect in the following sense (
[
Con13
, Theorem 1.4.4]
):

Proposition 5.0.2
.

We have an isomorphism of
\displaystyle S_{0}
-group schemes

\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/S_{0}}(\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}/\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}.

Remark 5.0.3
.

An important property of this symbol is that it is
bi-multiplicative
, i.e. for every
\displaystyle S
-point
\displaystyle x,y,z\in\mathcal{L}\mathbb{G}_{m}(S)
we have:

\langle xy,z\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle\langle y,z\rangle,\langle x,yz\rangle=\langle x,y\rangle\langle x,z\rangle.

As observed in
[
Bei06
]
, the Contou-Carrère symbol is furthermore compatible with the flat connection on the loop group and is factorizable because the determinant line bundle is; therefore we have a (non-unital)
factorizable
version of the symbol:

[\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to\mathbb{G}_{m}\times\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}

Delooping on the first variable, we have a pairing between
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}
and its 1-dual, i.e. a map

[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}

which is explicitly describable as follows. An
\displaystyle S
-point of the LHS is given by

(x,\mathcal{P}_{1},\mathcal{P}_{2},\alpha)

where
\displaystyle x=(x_{i})_{i\in I}
is an
\displaystyle S
-point of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{1}
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{2}
two line bundles on the adic disk
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}}
, and
\displaystyle\alpha
a trivialization of
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{2}
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{\circ}_{\Gamma_{x}}
. Then the pairing sends it to

(x,\det(\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{1}),\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{1}\tensor\mathcal{P}_{2}))^{-1}\tensor\det(\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{O}),\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{2})))

where
\displaystyle\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{1})
sends
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{1}
to the corresponding lattice in the Tate vector space
\displaystyle\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\circ}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{1})
, which we identify with
\displaystyle\Gamma(\mathcal{D}^{\circ}_{\Gamma_{x}},\mathcal{P}_{1}\tensor\mathcal{P}_{2})
via
\displaystyle\alpha
;
\displaystyle\det
stands for the determinant line bundle.

The following was shown in
[
CH17
, Theorem 5.2.1]
:

Proposition 5.0.4
.

This pairing is again perfect. More precisely, we have an isomorphism of
counital
factorization spaces

\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/X^{I}}([\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{X^{I}}

after base-changing along
\displaystyle X^{I}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
.

The counital structure mentioned in the proposition above comes from a
corr-unital
structure of the pairing, given by a map of corr-unital factorization spaces

[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m},\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}

here the fiber product is taken as corr-unital factorization spaces (note this is really necessary:
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}
is
co-unital
but
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}
is
unital
). Unfolding definition, we see the corresponding unital structure, for any fixed injection
\displaystyle\alpha:I\to J
of finite sets, is given by

\displaystyle\textstyle{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{X_{J}}\times_{X^{J}}X^{J}\times_{X^{I}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{X^{I}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{([\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{X^{I}}\times_{X^{I}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{X^{I}})\times_{X^{I}}X^{J}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{X^{J}}\times_{X^{J}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}]_{X^{J}}}

the leftward map is given by restriction while the rightward one uses Beauville-Laszlo. Then the two maps to
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}
(via either leg) canonically give the same result, so we have a well-defined corr-unital map.

Using the pairing
\displaystyle\Lambda\tensor_{\mathbb{Z}}\check{\Lambda}\to\mathbb{Z}
, the above discussion immediately generalizes to give a pairing

[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}T]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}

uniquely determined by the requirement that, if
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{1},\mathcal{P}_{2}
are line bundles,
\displaystyle\lambda:\mathbb{G}_{m}\to T,\check{\mu}:\mathbb{G}_{m}\to\check{T}
, then the pairing on the induced
\displaystyle T
(resp.
\displaystyle\check{T}
) bundles should be the pairing of
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{1}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{2}
raise to the
\displaystyle\lambda(\check{\mu})
-th power.

5.1
Levelwise Cartier Duality

Recall that we have a placid presentation
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}T_{X^{I}}\simeq\limit_{i}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}}
by the
\displaystyle n
th jet schemes, where each
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}}
is a smooth affine
\displaystyle X^{I}
-group scheme. Consider the Cartier dual

Z_{n}:=\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/X^{I}}(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})

The goal of this subsection is to prove the following statement:

Proposition 5.1.1
.

Each
\displaystyle Z_{n}
is an ind-flat ind-finite group ind-scheme, and for each
\displaystyle n<m
, the map
\displaystyle Z_{n}\to Z_{m}
is an ind-closed embedding, and we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},X^{I}}\simeq\colimit_{n}Z_{n}
. In other words, this provides an ind-flat placid presentation of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},X^{I}}
.

Remark 5.1.2
.

An ind-flat placid presentation of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{G,X^{I}}
is expected to exist for all reductive
\displaystyle G
. However, we are currently unaware of such a construction.

Proof.

One readily reduces to the case of
\displaystyle T=\mathbb{G}_{m}
. Let
\displaystyle r:(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}\mathbb{G}_{m})_{X^{I}}\to X^{I}
be the projection, and set

\mathcal{O}_{n}:=r_{*}(\mathcal{O})\in\textnormal{QCoh}^{\heartsuit}(X^{I});

it is a Hopf algebra object in said category. It is clearly flat as an
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{x^{I}}
-module, and is in fact locally free (
[
GR71
, Corollary I.3.3.12]
), so we reduce to an immediate check on geometric fibers.

More explicitly, let
\displaystyle\Gamma_{n}
be the scheme-theoretic sum of
\displaystyle n
th neighborhood of the graphs in
\displaystyle X^{I}\times X
, and let
\displaystyle p:\Gamma_{n}\to X^{I}
be the projection map. If we consider
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}\simeq\mathbb{A}^{2}\times_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\{1\}
as embedded into
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{2}
via
\displaystyle x\mapsto(x,x^{-1})
, then we can write

\mathcal{O}_{n}\simeq\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))\tensor_{\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}\tensor K)}\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}

(36)

where
\displaystyle K:=p^{!}(\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}})
is the relative dualizing sheaf, and
\displaystyle\mathcal{V}_{r}^{\vee}:=\underline{\Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_{\Gamma_{n}}}(\mathcal{O}_{\Gamma_{n}}^{\oplus r},\mathcal{O}_{\Gamma_{n}})\in\textnormal{QCoh}^{\heartsuit}(\Gamma_{n})
.

The algebra map
\displaystyle\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}K)\to\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}
is induced by the trace map
\displaystyle p_{*}p^{!}(\mathcal{O})\to\mathcal{O}
, and the algebra map

\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}K)\to\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))

is induced by a sheaf map

p_{*}K\to p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K)\tensor_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K)\to\textnormal{Sym}^{2}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))\inj\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))

where all but the first map is canonical; the first map is in turn given by a coalgebra map

p_{*}(K)\to p_{*}(K)\tensor_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}p_{*}(K)

followed by the two maps induced by
\displaystyle K\simeq\mathcal{V}_{1}^{\vee}\tensor K\to\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K
given by projections
\displaystyle\mathcal{V}_{2}\to\mathcal{V}_{1}
. To get this coalgebra map, consider the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\Gamma_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\Delta}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\Gamma_{n}\times_{X^{I}}\Gamma_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{u}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\Gamma_{n}\times\Gamma_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p\times p}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X^{I}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\Delta_{X}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X^{I}\times X^{I}}

Then we have

p_{*}(K)\simeq p_{*}p^{!}\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}\simeq\pi_{*}\Delta_{*}\Delta^{!}\pi^{!}\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}\xrightarrow{\textnormal{counit}}\pi_{*}\pi^{!}\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}\simeq\pi_{*}\pi^{!}\Delta_{X}^{*}\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}\times X^{I}}\simeq\pi_{*}u^{*}(p\times p)^{!}(\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}\times X^{I}})

\simeq\Delta_{X}^{*}(p\times p)_{*}(p\times p)^{!}(\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}\times X^{I}})\simeq p_{*}(K)\tensor_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}p_{*}(K)

Note that each individual term on RHS of Equation (
36
) has a coalgebra structure (given by the obvious diagonal maps), which induces a coalgebra structure on the RHS that agrees with that of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n}
.
In particular, the surjective map
\displaystyle\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))\surj\mathcal{O}_{n}
is a coalgebra map. Let

\textnormal{Sym}^{\leq m}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K))\in\textnormal{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(X^{I})

denote the subcoalgebra corresponding to the
\displaystyle(\leq m)
-th symmetric power for
\displaystyle m\in\mathbb{N}
, and let
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
denote the sheaf-theoretic image within
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n}
.

Lemma 5.1.3
.

The coherent sheaves
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
are
locally free subcoalgebras
of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n}
, and the maps
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{n,m^{\prime}}
are bundle maps i.e. admit local splittings.

Proof.

Introduce the notation

\mathscr{F}:=\textnormal{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(p_{*}(\mathcal{V}_{2}^{\vee}\tensor K)),

and similarly
\displaystyle\mathscr{F}^{\leq m}
forr
\displaystyle\textnormal{Sym}^{\leq n}
. Denote the map
\displaystyle\mathscr{F}\to\mathcal{O}_{n}
by
\displaystyle\pi
, and let
\displaystyle\mathscr{K}:=\ker(\pi)
, so that

\mathcal{O}_{n,m}\simeq\mathscr{F}^{\leq m}/(\mathscr{F}^{\leq m}\cap\mathscr{K}).

First note that
\displaystyle\mathscr{K}\inj\mathscr{F}\xrightarrow{\Delta}\mathscr{F}\tensor\mathscr{F}
factors through
\displaystyle\mathscr{K}\tensor\mathscr{K}
, so
\displaystyle\mathscr{K}
is a subcoalgebra of
\displaystyle\mathscr{F}
. It follows that
\displaystyle\mathscr{F}^{\leq m}\cap\mathscr{K}
is a subcoalgebra of
\displaystyle\mathscr{F}^{\leq m}
and thus
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
is a subcoalgebra of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n}
.

Since our base scheme is reduced, to show
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
is locally free it suffces to check that fiber ranks are constant. Assume the collision pattern at a point
\displaystyle x\in X^{I}
is

(i_{1},\ldots,i_{N})\hskip 10.00002pti_{1}+\ldots+i_{N}=|I|;

in other words, the fiber of
\displaystyle\Gamma_{n}
at
\displaystyle x
is a product of
\displaystyle N
fat points given by
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(k[t]/t^{ni_{j}})
for
\displaystyle 1\leq j\leq N
. Since
\displaystyle\Gamma_{n}\to X^{I}
is Gorenstein, we know that

\mathcal{O}_{n}|_{x}\simeq\textnormal{Sym}(A^{\vee}\times A^{\vee})\tensor_{\textnormal{Sym}(A^{\vee})}k,\hskip 10.00002ptA:=\prod_{j=1}^{N}k[t]/t^{ni_{j}}.

Unfolding definition, we see we can rewrite it as

\mathcal{A}:=k[x_{j,c_{j}},y_{j^{\prime},c_{j^{\prime}}}]/\mathcal{I}\hskip 10.00002pt1\leq j,j^{\prime}\leq k,0\leq c_{j}<ni_{j},0\leq c_{j^{\prime}}<ni_{j^{\prime}}

where the quotient ideal
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}
is generated by the relation

\sum_{z=0}^{r_{j}}x_{j,z}y_{j,r_{j}-z}=\begin{cases}1&r_{j}=0\\
0&\textnormal{otherwise}\end{cases}\hskip 10.00002pt\forall 1\leq j\leq k,0\leq r_{j}<ni_{j}

The Hilbert series (as a filtered algebra) of
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}
is the same as that of
\displaystyle k[x_{j,c_{j}},y_{j^{\prime},c_{j^{\prime}}}]/\mathcal{I}^{\prime}
, where
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}^{\prime}
is the same as
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}
except we take
\displaystyle x_{j,0}y_{j,0}
instead of
\displaystyle(x_{j_{0}}y_{j,0}-1)
. The generators provided above are obviously a regular sequence, so the Hilbert series is given by
\displaystyle\frac{(1-t^{2})^{\sum_{j}ni_{j}}}{(1-t)^{2n|I|}}=\frac{(1-t^{2})^{n|I|}}{(1-t)^{2n|I|}}=\left(\frac{1+t}{1-t}\right)^{n|I|}
, which is independent of the collision pattern.
This computation also shows that the quotient
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m^{\prime}}/\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
is constant rank, therefore the inclusion is a bundle map.
∎

Introduce

\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{n,m}:=\underline{\Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}}}(\mathcal{O}_{n,m},\mathcal{O}_{X^{I}})

which is a commutative algebra object in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(X^{I})
, and is locally free because
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}
is. From the lemma above, the connecting morphisms of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}^{\vee}
are all surjective; consequently, they form a Mittag-Leffler system and thus
\displaystyle\colimit_{m}\underline{\textnormal{Spec}}_{/X^{I}}(\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{n,m})
is an ind-affine ind-scheme.

By construction, to check the ind-closed embedding statement it suffices to show that
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{n,m}\inj\mathcal{O}_{n+1,m}
is a bundle map, which holds as the quotient has constant rank (which can be readily deduced from the Hilbert series calculation above). We claim that
\displaystyle Z_{n}\simeq\colimit_{m}\underline{\textnormal{Spec}}_{/X^{I}}(\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{n,m})
. By Zariski descent it suffices to demonstrate on a Zariski covering
\displaystyle p:\textnormal{Spec}(A)\to X^{I}
. Let us write

B_{A}=\Gamma(\textnormal{Spec}(A),p^{*}\mathcal{O}_{n}))\hskip 10.00002ptB_{m,A}=\Gamma(\textnormal{Spec}(A),p^{*}\mathcal{O}_{n,m})),

so we have
\displaystyle B_{A}=\colimit_{m}B_{m,A}
as
\displaystyle A
-algebras. Setting
\displaystyle B_{m,A}^{\vee}:=\Hom_{A}(B_{m},A)
, we have

\textnormal{Spec}(A)\times_{X^{I}}\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/X^{I}}(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}}))\simeq\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/\textnormal{Spec}(A)}(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{\textnormal{Spec}(A)},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})

\textnormal{Spec}(A)\times_{X^{I}}\colimit_{m}\underline{\textnormal{Spec}}_{/X^{I}}(\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{n,m})\simeq\colimit_{m}\underline{\textnormal{Spec}}_{/\textnormal{Spec}(A)}(B_{m,A}^{\vee})

It is clear that both are affine schemes over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(A)
, so it suffices to match their
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(A)
-sections, i.e. we want

\Hom_{\textnormal{HopfAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})}(A[x,x^{-1}],B_{A})\simeq\colimit_{m}\Hom_{\textnormal{CAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})}(\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A},A),A).

Since the algebras in consideration are in the heart, we can rewrite the RHS as

\displaystyle\displaystyle\colimit_{m}\Hom_{\textnormal{CAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})}(\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A},A),A)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\colimit_{m}\textnormal{Eq}(\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A}^{\vee},A)\rightrightarrows\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A}^{\vee}\tensor_{A}B_{m,A}^{\vee},A))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{Eq}\left(\colimit_{m}\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A}^{\vee},A)\rightrightarrows\colimit_{m}\Hom_{A\textnormal{-mod}}(B_{m,A}^{\vee}\tensor_{A}B_{m,A}^{\vee},A)\right)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{Eq}\left(\colimit_{m}B_{m,A}\rightrightarrows\colimit_{m}B_{m,A}\tensor_{A}B_{m,A}\right)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\colimit_{m}\textnormal{Eq}\left(B_{m,A}\rightrightarrows B_{m,A}\tensor_{A}B_{m,A}\right)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\colimit_{m}\Hom_{\textnormal{HopfAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})}(A[x,x^{-1}],B_{m,A})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{HopfAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})}(A[x,x^{-1}],B_{A})

where in 4th line we use local freeness, in 5th line the two maps are comultiplication and diagonal, respectively, and the last line is because
\displaystyle A[x,x^{-1}]
is a compact object in
\displaystyle\textnormal{HopfAlg}(A\textnormal{-mod})
.

Recall that by Noetherian approximation, we have, for any classical
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})\to X^{I}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(A_{r})
is any Noetherian approximation of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})
,

\Hom_{\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl}}_{/X^{I}}}(\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{+}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{Pro}(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl,ft}}_{/X^{I}})}(\textnormal{``}\limit_{n,r}\textnormal{''}\textnormal{Spec}(A_{r})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})

\simeq\colimit_{n,r}\Hom_{\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl,ft}}_{/X^{I}}}(\textnormal{Spec}(A_{r})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\colimit_{n}\Hom_{\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl}}_{/X^{I}}}(\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})

Since for any classical scheme
\displaystyle S
and any classical
\displaystyle S
-group schemes
\displaystyle G,H
, we have

\Hom_{\textnormal{Grp}_{/S}}(G,H)=\textnormal{Eq}(\Hom_{/S}(G,H)\rightrightarrows\Hom_{/S}(G\times G,H))

we also have

\Hom_{\textnormal{Grp}(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl}}_{/X^{I}})}(\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{+}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\colimit_{n}\Hom_{\textnormal{Grp}(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{cl}}_{/X^{I}})}(\textnormal{Spec}(A_{0})\times_{X^{I}}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})

from which it follows that

\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/X^{I}}(\mathcal{L}^{+}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}})\simeq\colimit_{n}\underline{\Hom}_{\textnormal{Grp}/X^{I}}(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T_{X^{I}},\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}}).

By Proposition
5.0.4
, it follows that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},X^{I}}\simeq\colimit_{n}Z_{n}
.
∎

5.2
Fourier-Mukai Transform

Introduce the notation

B_{n}:=[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T]_{X^{I}}.

We have a pairing map as before:

F_{n}:Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}.

Let
\displaystyle p_{1},p_{2}
denote the two projection maps from LHS to
\displaystyle Z_{n}
and
\displaystyle B_{n}
respectively. Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{n}
denote the Poincare line bundle, then we can use
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{n}
as the Fourier-Mukai kernel to define

\textnormal{FM}_{n}:=(p_{1})_{*}(p_{2}^{!}(\bullet)\tensor\mathscr{L}_{n}):\textnormal{IndCoh}(B_{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n}),

where the tensor product indicates the action of
QCoh
on
IndCoh
.

The following property of the Fourier-Mukai kernel is the main goal of this section:

Proposition 5.2.1
.

\displaystyle\Upsilon((p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n}))\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})
and
\displaystyle(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n}))\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(B_{n})
are invertible objects in the convolution monoidal structure
\displaystyle\star
given by

\star:\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})\tensor\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n}):=m_{*}(p_{1}^{!}(\bullet)\boxtimes p_{2}^{!}(\bullet))

where
\displaystyle p_{1},p_{2}:Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}\to Z_{n}
are projections and
\displaystyle m:Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}\to Z_{n}
is the multiplication map (and similarly defined for
\displaystyle B_{n}
).

Corollary 5.2.2
.

Each
\displaystyle\textnormal{FM}_{n}
is an equivalence of categories.

Proof.

The proof is standard and can be found in e.g.
[
Lurb
, Section 5.1]
, using Proposition
5.2.1
as the main input. The necessary modifications are as follows:

•

Replace the use of biextensions in 4.2.2 of
loc.cit.
with the bi-multiplicativity of
\displaystyle F_{n}
, which follows from definition;

•

For the inverse Fourier transformation, use
\displaystyle(p_{2})_{!}(p_{1}^{*,\textnormal{IndCoh}}(\bullet)\tensor\mathscr{L}_{n})
instead. (This accounts for the asymmetry of the statement above.) Tracing through the proof one sees that for the reverse direction, one needs the projection formula

f_{*}(\mathcal{E})\tensor\mathcal{F}\simeq f_{*}(\mathcal{E}\tensor f^{*,\textnormal{IndCoh}}(\mathcal{F}))

for
\displaystyle f:Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}\to Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}\in\textnormal{QCoh}(Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n})
, as well as the QCoh base change formula for the next diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}Z_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}}

both of which follow from the fact that
\displaystyle B_{n}
is a QCA stack of bounded Tor dimension.

The rest of the proof proceeds as in
loc.cit.
.
∎

Proof of Proposition
5.2.1
.

First we note that
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{n}
is canonically bi-rigidified, i.e. we have isomorphisms

\mathscr{L}_{n}|_{\{e_{Z}\}\times B_{n}}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{B_{n}}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathscr{L}_{n}|_{Z_{n}\times\{e_{B}\}}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}},

where
\displaystyle e_{Z}:X^{I}\to Z_{n},e_{B}:X^{I}\to B_{n}
are the unit sections. Indeed,
\displaystyle e_{B}
is the trivial
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T
-bundle on
\displaystyle X^{I}
, so the map
\displaystyle Z_{n}\times\{e_{B}\}\to Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}
factors through
\displaystyle\textnormal{pt}\inj\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}
. Likewise, identity for
\displaystyle Z_{n}
is the constant group homomorphism
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T\to\{1\}\to\underline{\mathbb{G}_{m}}
, so the induced bundle is again always trivial.

Now consider the following two Cartesian diagrams:

\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\widetilde{e_{B}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p_{2}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X^{I}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{e_{B}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{B_{n}}

\displaystyle\textstyle{B_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\widetilde{e_{Z}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p_{1}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X^{I}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{e_{Z}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Z_{n}}

We obtain the following from the left diagram:

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})}(\omega_{Z_{n}},\omega_{Z_{n}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})}(\omega_{Z_{n}},\pi^{!}(\omega_{X^{I}}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\omega_{Z_{n}},\omega_{X^{I}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{B}}^{!}(\omega_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}}),\omega_{X^{I}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{B}}^{!}(\Upsilon(\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}})),\omega_{X^{I}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\Upsilon(\widetilde{e_{B}}^{*}(\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}})),\omega_{X^{I}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\Upsilon(\widetilde{e_{B}}^{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n}),\omega_{X^{I}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{B}}^{!}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n})),\omega_{X^{I}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(e_{B}^{!}(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n})),\omega_{X^{I}})\simeq\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(K_{X^{I}/B_{n}}\tensor e_{B}^{*,\textnormal{IndCoh}}(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n})),\omega_{X^{I}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(e_{B}^{*,\textnormal{IndCoh}}(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n})),K_{X^{I}/B_{n}}^{-1}\tensor\omega_{X^{I}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(B_{n})}((p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n})),(e_{B})_{*}(\Upsilon(K_{X^{I}/B_{n}}^{-1})))

where we used the fact that the relative dualizing complex
\displaystyle K_{X^{I}/B_{n}}:=e_{B}^{!}(\mathcal{O}_{B_{n}})
is a line bundle, which is because the morphism
\displaystyle X^{I}\to B_{n}
is smooth. Thus from the identity arrow
\displaystyle\omega_{Z_{n}}\to\omega_{Z_{n}}
we obtain a
root morphism

\rho_{Z}:(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n}))\to(e_{B})_{*}(\Upsilon(K_{X^{I}/B_{n}}^{-1}))

For the other root morphism, note that similarly we have

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{QCoh}(B_{n})}(\mathcal{O}_{B_{n}},\mathcal{O}_{B_{n}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{QCoh}(X^{I})}(\pi^{*}\Upsilon^{-1}(\omega_{X^{I}}),\widetilde{e_{Z}}^{*}(\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{QCoh}(X^{I})}(\Upsilon^{-1}(\omega_{X^{I}}),\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{Z}}^{*}(\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\omega_{X^{I}},\Upsilon(\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{Z}}^{*}(\mathcal{O}_{Z_{n}\times_{X^{I}}B_{n}})))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\omega_{X^{I}},\Upsilon(\pi_{*}\widetilde{e_{Z}}^{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n})))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\omega_{X^{I}},\Upsilon(e_{Z}^{*}(p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n})))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})}(\omega_{X^{I}},e_{Z}^{!}\Upsilon((p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n})))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\Hom_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})}((e_{Z})_{!}(\omega_{X^{I}}),\Upsilon((p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n})))

where in the middle we used QCoh base change for the second diagram above. From the identity of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{B_{n}}
we get our second root morphism

\rho_{B}:(e_{Z})_{!}(\omega_{X^{I}})\to\Upsilon((p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}_{n})).

Observe that
\displaystyle\Upsilon
on the right is symmetric monoidal, and
\displaystyle e_{B}
is symmetric monoidal with respect to the standard monoidal structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(X^{I})
and the convolution monoidal structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(B_{n})
. It follows that if
\displaystyle\rho_{Z}
is an isomorphism, then
\displaystyle(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{n}))
is invertible in the convolution monoidal structure; same goes for
\displaystyle\rho_{B}
.

It is clear that the root morphisms are compatible with base change on
\displaystyle X^{I}
. Using the usual open-closed triangle, it suffices to prove them being isomorphism on each strata of
\displaystyle X^{I}
(where we take the diagonal stratification). Since
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{(n)}T
is étale locally trivial on each strata, all sheaves involved are étale locally constant; hence it suffices to prove the isomorphism after base-changing to each geometric point.

We again reduce to
\displaystyle T=\mathbb{G}_{m}
. Suppose we are at a point
\displaystyle x\in X^{I}
with collision pattern
\displaystyle(i_{1},\ldots,i_{N})
, then

\mathcal{L}^{(n)}|_{x}\simeq\mathbb{G}_{m}^{N}\times\mathbb{G}_{a}^{n|I|-N}\hskip 10.00002ptZ_{n}|_{x}\simeq\mathbb{Z}^{N}\times(\mathbb{A}^{n|I|-N})^{\wedge}_{0};

so we see it suffices to check the root morphisms are isomorphisms for each collision type. The rest of the proof is now explicit computation, which immediately reduces to the case
\displaystyle(\mathbb{G}_{m},\mathbb{Z})
and
\displaystyle(\mathbb{G}_{a},(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{0}^{\wedge})
.

The
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{m}
case is simple: the Poincare bundle places a weight
\displaystyle j
representation on
\displaystyle\{j\}\times\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}
. From this one readily computes that both sides of
\displaystyle\rho_{Z}
are regular representation

\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\in\textnormal{QCoh}(\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m})

and both sides of
\displaystyle\rho_{B}
are

i_{*}(k)\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(\mathbb{Z})\hskip 10.00002pti:\{0\}\inj\mathbb{Z}.

For
\displaystyle\mathbb{G}_{a}
, let
\displaystyle Z:=(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{0}^{\wedge}
and
\displaystyle f:\mathbb{G}_{a}\times Z\to\mathbb{G}_{m}
be the pairing map. On the level of algebras,
\displaystyle f
is given by (truncations) of the map

k[x,x^{-1}]\to k[y][[t]]\hskip 10.00002ptx\mapsto e^{yt};

Our first job is to identify the Poincare bundle. By descent we have

\textnormal{QCoh}(B\mathbb{G}_{a}\times Z)\simeq\textnormal{Tot}(\textnormal{QCoh}(\mathbb{G}_{a}^{\bullet}\times Z)),

unwinding definition, we see that
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}
can understood as
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{Z}\in\textnormal{QCoh}(Z)
equipped with the equivariance given by multiplying by
\displaystyle e^{ty}
.
Thus, as plain vector space,
\displaystyle(p_{2})_{*}(\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}))
is isomorphic to

\pi_{*}(\omega_{Z})\simeq\colimit(k\xrightarrow{t}k[t]/t^{2}\xrightarrow{t}k[t]/t^{3}\ldots)\simeq k[t^{-1}]

where the map
\displaystyle k[t]/t^{r}\to k[t^{-1}]
is by multiplying by
\displaystyle t^{-r+1}
; this is additionally a colimit of cocommutative coalgebras. Each term admits an
\displaystyle k[y]
-coaction by truncations of
\displaystyle e^{ty}
, which are compatible with these transition maps, so
\displaystyle k[t^{-1}]
itself admits a
\displaystyle k[y]
-coaction given by
\displaystyle t^{-r}\mapsto t^{-r}\left(1+\ldots+(yt)^{r}/(r)!\right)
, which is isomorphic to the regular representation of
\displaystyle k[y]
via
\displaystyle t^{-r}\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac{y^{i}}{i!}
.

For the other root morphism
\displaystyle\rho_{B}
, note that
\displaystyle!
-pullback along
\displaystyle e_{Z}
is conservative, so it suffices to compute

e_{Z}^{!}\circ(e_{Z})_{!}(k)\simeq k\oplus k[1]\simeq C^{*}(\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{a})\simeq\Upsilon(\pi_{*}\circ\widetilde{e_{Z}}^{*}(\mathscr{L}))\simeq e_{Z}^{!}\circ\Upsilon\circ(p_{1})_{*}(\mathscr{L}).

This finishes the computation.
∎

Now we move towards factorization.

Recall from Definition
3.3.10
that we have a unital factorization category
\displaystyle\mathcal{R}ep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)
over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}
, defined using renormalized ind-coherent sheaves. On the other hand, by Construction
11.11.13
, the unital structure of
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}
equips the category

\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})

with the structure of a unital factorization category over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}
as well. (The condition from Remark
11.11.14
is easily verifiable.)

Proposition 5.2.3
.

There exists an
unital
equivalence of unital factorization categories over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}

\textnormal{FM}:\mathcal{R}ep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)\simeq\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})

whichi induces a pointwise equivalence

\textnormal{FM}:\Rep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}])

that satisfies the following additional constraint: for each dominant weight
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
, let
\displaystyle k^{\check{\lambda}}\in\Rep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)
be the restriction of
\displaystyle k^{\check{\lambda}}\in\Rep(T)
along
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}T\xrightarrow{t=0}T
, then
\displaystyle\textnormal{FM}(k^{\lambda})
is the
\displaystyle\delta
-sheaf supported at
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
.

Proof.

For simplicity, introduce

[\textnormal{Pair}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}:=[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}T]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}

and let
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Pair}]_{X^{I}}
denote its base change along any
\displaystyle X^{I}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}
. Consider the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{[\textnormal{Pair}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{q}
\displaystyle\textstyle{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}T]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}}

The top space again satisfies the condition from Remark
11.11.14
, so that
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Pair}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})
is a unital factorization category.
Note that the map
\displaystyle p
is
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable and strictly unital,
\displaystyle q
is
\displaystyle*
-pullable and strictly co-unital.

From the pairing map of corr-unital factorization spaces

[\textnormal{Pair}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\to\mathbb{B}\mathbb{G}_{m}\times\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}

we obtain an universal Poincare bundle

\Upsilon(\mathscr{L}_{\textnormal{univ}})\in\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Pair}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})

using which we define the Fourier-Mukai morphism and its left adjoint

\textnormal{FM}:=q_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ(-\tensor\mathscr{L}_{\textnormal{univ}})\circ p^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}:\mathcal{R}ep(\mathcal{L}^{+}T)\to\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}})

here by
\displaystyle\tensor^{!}
we mean the
\displaystyle!
-pullback in the
\displaystyle!
-theory; we note that in the present setting, the
\displaystyle!
-theory and
\displaystyle*
-theory are canonically equivalent.
The general setup in Construction
11.11.15
tells us that
FM
is a
lax
unital map; however, explicit computation performed in the previous Proposition demonstrates that the unital map is actually always an isomorphism.
Thus we obtain a
strictly unital
functor.

To see that it is an equivalence, we note that the restriction functors

\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{un}}\to\textnormal{ShvCat}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}})\to\textnormal{ShvCat}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}})\to\textnormal{ShvCat}(\textnormal{Ran})

are all conservative; indeed, the first two are general categorical facts, and the third one is because we can always use smoothness of
\displaystyle X^{I}
to
non-canonically
lift any
\displaystyle S
-point of
\displaystyle X^{I}_{\textnormal{dR}}
to one of
\displaystyle X^{I}
.
It thus suffices to establish the map is an equivalence on each
\displaystyle X^{I}
. Using result from Section
11.11
we can write

\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{X^{I}})\simeq\colimit_{i,!\textnormal{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(Z_{n})\hskip 10.00002pt\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}([\mathbb{B}T]_{X^{I}})\simeq\colimit_{i,*\textnormal{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(B_{n})

with the stratification given above, and
\displaystyle\textnormal{FM}_{X^{I}}
restricts to the system
\displaystyle\textnormal{FM}_{n}
above; the compatibility of the system is given by base change. In particular, the additional constraint is met since the representations
\displaystyle k^{\check{\lambda}}
are pulled back from
\displaystyle B_{1}
.
∎

5.3
Monad Comparison

Let
\displaystyle[\kappa,E]
be a non-degenerate quantum parameter for the maximal torus
\displaystyle T
, and
\displaystyle[\check{\kappa},\check{E}]
be the Langlands dual parameter. By
[
Zha17
]
, to such data we can attach a unital factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\textnormal{Hecke}}_{T}}
over
\displaystyle[\widehat{\textnormal{Hecke}}_{T}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}
as in Section
3.3
. On the other hand, let

[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{rel}}^{\bullet}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}

denote the Cech nerve of
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}\to[(\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}})_{\textnormal{dR}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}
; this is a cosimplicial object in the category of unital factorization spaces. The data
\displaystyle[\check{\kappa},\check{E}]
also gives rise to a multiplicative factorization line bundle
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{rel}}}
over
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{rel}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}
.

Remark 5.3.1
.

The compatibility between
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T},\textnormal{rel}}}
and
\displaystyle\mathscr{L}_{\widehat{\textnormal{Hecke}}_{T}}
is as follows. Because
\displaystyle\kappa
is non-degenerate, it induces an isomorphism of the Lie algebras

Proposition 5.3.4

(Toric Fundamental Local Equivalence)
.

We have an equivalence of unital factorization categories

Proof.

5.4
Global Compatibility

Let
\displaystyle X

\det\Gamma(X,\mathcal{O})\tensor\det\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}\tensor\mathcal{L}^{\prime})\tensor(\det\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}))^{-1}\tensor(\det\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}^{\prime}))^{-1}.

Set

is an equivalence.

\textnormal{FM}_{\textnormal{IndCoh}}^{-1}\simeq(\pi_{1})_{*}(\pi_{2}^{!}(-)\tensor\mathcal{P}^{\textnormal{inv}}).

Let

Remark 5.4.1
.

Let us explain how to relate the above construction to the classical one. For any three laft prestacks
\displaystyle X,Y,Z
, we have the natural convolution functor

\star:\textnormal{IndCoh}(X\times Y)\tensor\textnormal{IndCoh}(Y\times Z)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(X\times Z);

In the case of
\displaystyle X=\textnormal{Bun}_{\check{T}},Y=\textnormal{Bun}_{T},Z=\textnormal{pt}
, the operation
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}\star(-)
becomes the Fourier-Mukai transform for IndCoh. In the case of
\displaystyle X=Y=\textnormal{Bun}_{T},Z=\textnormal{pt}
, we obtain the usual convolution action of
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(\textnormal{Bun}_{T}\times\textnormal{Bun}_{T})
on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(\textnormal{Bun}_{T})
, and a
\displaystyle[\kappa,0]
-twisted D-module is exactly a module over
\displaystyle(\widehat{\Delta}_{T})_{!}(\mathcal{L}_{\kappa})
under this action. Now, the isomorphism between
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\kappa}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\check{\kappa}}
over
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Bun}_{T})^{\wedge}_{\textnormal{triv}}\simeq(\textnormal{Bun}_{\check{T}})^{\wedge}_{\textnormal{triv}}
gives an identification

\mathcal{P}\star(\widehat{\Delta}_{T})_{!}(\mathcal{L}_{\kappa})\simeq(\widehat{\Delta}_{\check{T}})_{!}(\mathcal{L}_{\check{\kappa}})\star\mathcal{P},

from which it follows that
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}\star(-)
upgrades to a functor

(\widehat{\Delta}_{T})_{!}(\mathcal{L}_{\kappa})\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(\textnormal{Bun}_{T}),\star)\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\mathcal{P}\star(-)}(\widehat{\Delta}_{\check{T}})_{!}(\mathcal{L}_{\check{\kappa}})\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(\textnormal{Bun}_{\check{T}}),\star)

This is the functor constructd in
[
PR01
, Theorem 6.5]
; it tautologically agrees with our construction above.

The compatibility with our construction above is summarized in the following diagram (c.f.

, Section 6.4.2]

\displaystyle\textstyle{U\times[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{[\mathbb{B}\mathcal{L}^{+}T]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{q}
\displaystyle\textstyle{[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{U}

and
\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{glob}}
is the pullback of the global Poincare bundle. On the other hand, the bottom circuit becomes
\displaystyle q_{*}(\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{loc}}\tensor\varphi_{*}\circ p^{!}(-))

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{loc}}

∎

6.1
Constructible Factorization Categories

We first make precise of what “topological factorization category” means. For technical reasons, it is easier to work with a slight variant which we call
constructible
factorization categories.

Let
StratTop
denote the category of conically stratified
\displaystyle D_{\omega}
topological spaces
\displaystyle S\to A
(where
\displaystyle A
is the stratification poset) as described in
[
Lej21
]
. A morphism is a square

\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{A^{\prime}}

i.e. the induced stratification on
\displaystyle S
needs to be coarser than
\displaystyle A
.
\displaystyle(S\to A)\times(S^{\prime}\times A^{\prime}):=(S\times S\to A\times A^{\prime})
gives it a symmetric monoidal structure.

Definition 6.1.1
.

For any
\displaystyle X\to A\in\textnormal{StratTop}
and any symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, we let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})
(resp.
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})
) denote the category of
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-valued
hyper(co)complete

\displaystyle A
-constructible (co)sheaves (a notion defined in
[
Lej21
]
). The functoriality is given by (usual) pushforward and
hyper
pullbacks
30
30

30

that it preserves constructibility is Corollary 2.18 of
loc.cit.
.
. We will abuse language by referring to such objects simply as
\displaystyle A
-constructible (co)sheaves
.

Notation 6.1.2
.

We will let
\displaystyle(f_{\dagger},f^{\dagger})
denote the adjoint pair of cosheaf pushforward / (hyper)pullback.

Remark 6.1.3
.

Since the problem of hypercompleteness only occurs when we consider Ran space itself, we have opted to abuse notation in favor of brevity. We hope this does not cause too much confusion.

Recall that the category of all
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-valued hypercocomplete cosheaves
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}(X;\mathcal{C})
has a symmetric monoidal structure for any symmetric monoidal
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
whose tensor commutes with colimit in each variable: by
[
Lur12
, 2.2.1.9]
, there is an unique such structure such that the cosheafify-then-hypercocomplete functor

\textnormal{coShfycoHyp}:\textnormal{Fun}(\mathcal{U}(X),\mathcal{C})\to\textnormal{cShv}(X;\mathcal{C})

upgrades to a symmetric monoidal functor, where we equip the former with pointwise tensor product.

Remark 6.1.4
.

If
\displaystyle\varphi:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
is a symmetric monoidal functor, then so is the induced map
\displaystyle\tilde{\varphi}:\textnormal{cShv}(X;\mathcal{C})\to\textnormal{cShv}(X;\mathcal{D})
. The category of
\displaystyle A
-constructible cosheaves is stable under this tensor product and
\displaystyle\tilde{\varphi}
restricts to a symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})\to\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{D})
.

Enter-Path Model

Let us introduce a different model for
\displaystyle A
-constructible
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-valued cosheaves. By
[
Lej21
]
(extending
[
Lur12
, A.9.3]
), for
\displaystyle(X\to A)\in\textnormal{StratTop}
, we have

\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{Shv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C}^{\textnormal{op}})^{\textnormal{op}}\simeq\textnormal{Fun}(\textnormal{Exit}_{A}(X),\mathcal{C}^{\textnormal{op}})^{\textnormal{op}}\simeq\textnormal{Fun}(\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X),\mathcal{C})

where
\displaystyle\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X):=\textnormal{Exit}_{A}(X)^{\textnormal{op}}
. For every map
\displaystyle X\to Y
of
\displaystyle A
-stratified space we have an obvious functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)\to\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(Y)
, and precomposition gives the pullback functor; it then follows that
\displaystyle\dagger
-pushforward is given by left Kan extension along
\displaystyle\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)\to\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(Y)
.

A special case is when
\displaystyle A
is trivial. In such case,
\displaystyle\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)\simeq X^{\textnormal{Spc}}
is a Kan complex, so we have

\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{Fun}(X^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},\mathcal{C})\simeq\limit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}\mathcal{C}=:\mathsf{LS}(X;\mathcal{C}).

Note that we also have
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}(X;\mathcal{C})\simeq\colimit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}}\mathcal{C}
.

The assignments

\textnormal{ShvMod}:\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op}}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}\hskip 10.00002pt(S\to A)\mapsto\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(S)\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{DGCat})

is therefore well-defined, sending
\displaystyle f:(S\to A)\to(S^{\prime}\to A^{\prime})
to
\displaystyle M\mapsto M\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(S^{\prime})}\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(S)
. Similarly we have another map

\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op}}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}\hskip 10.00002pt(S\to A)\mapsto\{M\in\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(S)\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{DGCat}),m\in M\}

these two functors give rise to a map of two Cartesian fibrations

\textnormal{ShvModSect}:\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{ShvModSect}}\to\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{ShvMod}}

over
StratTop
. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvMod},\vee}\to\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op}}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvModSect},\vee}\to\textnormal{StratTop}^{\textnormal{op}}
denote the dual coCartesian fibrations.
Taking box product then inducing along

\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(S)\tensor\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(S^{\prime})\xrightarrow{\boxtimes}\textnormal{cShv}_{A\times A^{\prime}}(S\times S^{\prime})

gives both of them symmetric monoidal structures, such that the map (and their maps to
StratTop
) are symmetric monoidal.

Note that the
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}(X)
gives an oplax symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{Betti}}:{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}\to\textnormal{StratTop}
, where the stratification is by number of distinct points; we let
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{Ran}}
denote this stratification.
Similarly, the
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle U_{\textnormal{Ran}}
gives an oplax symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}:\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\textnormal{StratTop}
. We let
\displaystyle A(p)
denote its stratification for
\displaystyle p\in\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

Proposition 6.1.7
.

The two functors above are equivalences of categories.

Proof.

Following the argument of Proposition
10.5.13
it suffices to check that the (co)unit yield identities. By conservativity it suffices to check it on the underlying (plain) categories.
For simplicity, set
\displaystyle C:=\textnormal{cShv}_{A_{\textnormal{Ran}}}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}([1]))
and
\displaystyle C_{J}:=\textnormal{cShv}_{A(J\surj 1)}({U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1))
.

On one hand, we need to check for every
\displaystyle F\in\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr}}
, we have

F(1)\simeq\limit_{J}F(1)\tensor_{C}C_{J};

passing to left adjoints and use the projection formula for closed embeddings, we reduce to showing that
\displaystyle C\to\limit_{J,\dagger\textnormal{-pull}}C_{J}
is an equivalence. Let
\displaystyle C_{\leq n}:=\textnormal{cShv}_{A_{\textnormal{Ran}^{\leq n}}}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\leq n})
, where
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\leq n}
is the topological subspace of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}
consisting of points of cardinality at most
\displaystyle n
, and
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{Ran}^{\leq n}}
is the obvious stratification. It was already proven by devissage in
[
Lej21
, Theorem 2.19]
that
\displaystyle C\simeq\limit_{n,\dagger\textnormal{-pull}}C_{\leq n}
; by passing to left adjoints and combining colimit diagrams we see that it suffices to prove

C_{\leq n}\to\limit_{J,|J|\leq n,\dagger\textnormal{-pull}}C_{J}

(37)

is an equivalence for each
\displaystyle n
. We run induction on
\displaystyle n
, the
\displaystyle n=1
case being evident. Let
\displaystyle C_{=n}:=\mathsf{LS}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{=n})
, where
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{=n}\subseteq\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\leq n}
is the open subspace consisting of points of cardinality exactly
\displaystyle n
. For each
\displaystyle J
, let
\displaystyle C_{J}^{=}:=\mathsf{LS}(U_{{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)}^{=})
where
\displaystyle{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)^{=}
is the open stratum of
\displaystyle U_{{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)}
, and let
\displaystyle{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)^{<}
be the union of all closed proper strata of
\displaystyle{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)
, and set
\displaystyle C_{J}^{<}:=\textnormal{cShv}_{A(J\surj 1)}({U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)^{<})
. Then we have

C_{\leq n}\simeq\textnormal{lax}\limit[C_{=n}\to C_{\leq n-1}]\hskip 10.00002ptC_{J}\simeq\textnormal{lax}\limit[C_{J}^{=}\to C_{J}^{<}]

where both functors are nearby cycles, and lax limits are taken with respect to the diagram
\displaystyle\bullet\to\bullet
. We also have
\displaystyle C_{=n}\simeq\limit_{J,|J|=n}C_{J}^{=}
since
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{=n}
is the colimit of
\displaystyle{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(J\surj 1)^{=}
. Noting that the diagram on the RHS of Equation (
37
) only goes from
\displaystyle|J|=n
to
\displaystyle|J|<n
, we can also rewrite it as

\limit[(\limit_{J,|J|=n}C_{J})\to(\limit_{K,|K|\leq n-1}C_{K})]

Thus we rewrite Equation (
37
), using induction hypothesis, as

\textnormal{lax}\limit[(\limit_{J,|J|=n}C_{J}^{=})\to\limit_{K,|K|\leq n-1}C_{K}]\to\limit\left[\left(\limit_{J,|J|=n}(\textnormal{lax}\limit[C_{J}^{=}\to C_{J}^{<}])\right)\to(\limit_{K,|K|\leq n-1}C_{K})\right]

which can be seen to be an equivalence by unfolding definition.

On the other hand, we need to check for every
\displaystyle G\in\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part}}
and
\displaystyle I
, we have

G(I\surj 1)\simeq(\limit_{J}G(J\surj 1))\tensor_{C}C_{J}

Again by projection formula,
\displaystyle C_{J}
is dualizable as a
\displaystyle C
-module category, so we can swap the tensor inside. Similar to Proposition
10.5.13
, we now claim that the limit stabilizes to a constant as long as
\displaystyle|J|>|I|
. Indeed, since each
\displaystyle C_{J}
fully faithfully embeds into
\displaystyle C
, the tensor product
\displaystyle G(J\surj 1)\tensor_{C}C_{I}
in such range becomes
\displaystyle G(J\surj 1)\tensor_{C_{J}}C_{I}\simeq G(I\surj 1)
.
∎
