6.2
How to Glue Cosheaves

Recall the notion of
lax
limits of categories and
lax
functors between them (Section
9
). Constructible cosheaves constitute an important example of such:

Lemma 6.2.1
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
a symmetric monoidal
\displaystyle\infty
-category,
\displaystyle(X\to A)\in\textnormal{StratTop}
, then
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})
is equivalent to the lax limit corresponding to
\displaystyle\{\mathsf{LS}(X_{a};\mathcal{C})\}_{a\in A}
where the connecting functors are
\displaystyle(j_{b})^{\dagger}\circ(j_{a})_{\dagger}
for
\displaystyle a\to b
.

Proof.

We check the conditions above are satisfied. Fully faithfulness is
[
Knu18
, B.2.4]
. Joint conservativeness is because isomorphism can be checked on costalks (thanks to hypercocompleteness). Assumption on
\displaystyle F_{j}^{R}\circ F_{i}
is
[
Knu18
, B.2.6]
.
It remains to check that
\displaystyle j_{a}^{\dagger}:\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\mathcal{C})\to\mathsf{LS}(X_{a};\mathcal{C})
is continuous. By cosheaf condition, it suffices to compare

\colimit_{\alpha}j_{a}^{\dagger}\mathcal{F}_{\alpha}(W)\to j_{a}^{\dagger}(\colimit_{\alpha}\mathcal{F}_{\alpha})(W)

for each open
\displaystyle F_{\sigma}
set
\displaystyle W\subseteq X_{\alpha}
. By
[
Lur12
, A.5.12]
among all open sets of
\displaystyle X
containing
\displaystyle W
there exists a filtered cofinal subcategory consisting of spaces
\displaystyle\{Q_{\beta}\}
which are homeomorphic to a fixed conical neighborhood
\displaystyle W\times C(L)
of
\displaystyle W
. By homotopy invariance of constructible (co)sheaves
[
Hai20
]
, the map above can then be identified with
\displaystyle\colimit_{\alpha}\mathcal{F}_{\alpha}(Q_{\beta})\xrightarrow{\simeq}(\colimit_{\alpha}\mathcal{F}_{\alpha})(Q_{\beta})
for any such
\displaystyle Q_{\beta}
.
∎

Recall from
[
Lur09
, 5.5.3.3]
the class of
presentable
coCartesian fibrations can be characterized as those whose corresponding functors factor through
\displaystyle\textnormal{Pr}^{L}\subseteq\textnormal{Cat}
.
A morphism between two presentable coCartesian fibrations
\displaystyle p_{1}:E_{1}\to S
and
\displaystyle p_{2}:E_{2}\to S
is a morphism of coCartesian fibrations, such that its induced maps
\displaystyle(E_{1})|_{s}\to(E_{2})|_{s}
are all continuous.

The following curious phenomenon is the basis of our construction:

Proposition 6.2.2
.

Let
\displaystyle p:E\to D
be a presentable coCartesian fibration. Then the canonical functor

\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;E)\to\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;D)

is a presentable coCartesian fibration.

Proof.

We note that a morphism
\displaystyle\widetilde{F}\to\widetilde{G}
upstairs is
\displaystyle\pi
-coCartesian if and only if for every
\displaystyle U\in\mathcal{U}(X)
, the morphism
\displaystyle\widetilde{F}(U)\to\widetilde{G}(U)\in\textnormal{Fun}([1],E)
is a
\displaystyle p
-coCartesian arrow: by
[
Lur09
, 2.4.1.8]
this is evidently true for
\displaystyle\pi^{\prime}
in the above diagram, and thus is true for
\displaystyle\pi
. Now fix
\displaystyle e:(F\to G)\in\textnormal{Fun}([1],\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;D))
and
\displaystyle\widetilde{F}
over
\displaystyle F
. Our goal is to construct a coCartesian lift
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}
above
\displaystyle e
.

First we consider the case when
\displaystyle A
is trivial. Then
\displaystyle\pi
becomes the map
\displaystyle\limit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}E\to\limit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}D
. Then
\displaystyle e
becomes a compatible family
\displaystyle\{e_{x}:F_{x}\to G_{x}\}_{x\in X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}
of objects in
\displaystyle D
, and
\displaystyle\widetilde{F}
becomes
\displaystyle\{\widetilde{F}_{x}\}
a family of objects in
\displaystyle E
. There is an obvious map
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}:\{\widetilde{F}_{x}\}\to\{(e_{x})_{!}(\widetilde{F}_{x})\}
; we now prove this is
\displaystyle\pi
-coCartesian.

Elements in
\displaystyle E
can be expressed as
\displaystyle(x,d)
where
\displaystyle d\in D
and
\displaystyle x\in E|_{d}
. Recall that within
\displaystyle E
(which is a lax limit), colimits are computed as

\colimit_{i}(x_{i},d_{i})\simeq(\colimit_{i}\textnormal{ins}_{i}(x_{i}),\colimit_{i}d_{i})

where
\displaystyle\textnormal{ins}_{i}
is the coCartesian pushforward along
\displaystyle d_{i}\to\colimit_{i}d_{i}
. It follows if
\displaystyle\{(x_{i},d_{i})\}
is a diagram in
\displaystyle E
and
\displaystyle\{\varphi_{i}:d_{i}\to d^{\prime}_{i}\}
is a diagram of arrows in
\displaystyle D
, then the coCartesian lift of
\displaystyle\colimit_{i}\varphi_{i}
above
\displaystyle\colimit_{i}(x_{i},d_{i})
is

(\colimit_{i}\textnormal{ins}^{d}_{i}(x_{i}),\colimit_{i}d_{i})\to(\colimit_{i}\textnormal{ins}^{d^{\prime}}_{i}((\varphi_{i})_{!}(x_{i})),\colimit_{i}d^{\prime}_{i});

It thus follows from cosheaf condition that
\displaystyle\pi
-coCartesian-ness in
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}(X;E)
can be checked just on disks in
\displaystyle X
. Since
\displaystyle\dagger
-fibers can be computed as a constant filtered diagram of sections on such disks, the same condition can be checked on
\displaystyle\dagger
-fibers, whence the claim.

We need to check the fibration is presentable. To check fibers contain filtered colimits, it suffices to check that, if
\displaystyle c_{i}
is a diagram upstairs that map to constant diagram
\displaystyle\underline{c}
downstairs, then
\displaystyle\colimit_{i}c_{i}
maps to the same
\displaystyle\underline{c}
, which follows from the fact that
\displaystyle\pi
is continuous. That the connecting functors are continuous (i.e. coCartesian liftings preserve colimits) follows from the construction of
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}
.

Now we consider general
\displaystyle A
-constructible cosheaves. Let
\displaystyle\Phi
(resp.
\displaystyle\widetilde{\Phi}
) denote the lax-functors encoding
\displaystyle A
-constructible cosheaves valued in
\displaystyle D
(resp.
\displaystyle E
) on
\displaystyle X
. There is an evident lax natural transformation
\displaystyle\mathsf{P}:\widetilde{\Phi}\to\Phi
such that
\displaystyle\pi\simeq\mathsf{Glue}(\mathsf{P})
. Unfolding definition, we see that there is a family of functors

\{\mathsf{P}_{s}:\mathfrak{G}(\widetilde{\Phi})_{s}\to\mathfrak{G}(\Phi)_{s}\}_{s\in\mathsf{sd}(A)}

such that
\displaystyle\mathsf{Glue}(P)\simeq\limit_{s\in\mathsf{sd}(A)}\mathsf{P}_{s}
. Now, each
\displaystyle\mathsf{P}_{s}
is of the form

\textnormal{Fun}(K_{s},\mathsf{LS}(X_{\mathsf{max}(s)};E))\to\textnormal{Fun}(K_{s},\mathsf{LS}(X_{\mathsf{max}(s)};D))

and is component-wise induced by
\displaystyle\pi
from the locally constant case. Given
\displaystyle e:(\{f_{s}\}_{s\in\mathsf{sd}(A)}\to\{g_{s}\}_{s\in\mathsf{sd}(A)})\in\textnormal{Fun}([1],\mathsf{Glue}(\Phi))
and a lift of
\displaystyle\{\tilde{f}_{s}\}

\displaystyle\{f_{s}\}
, then, we have a canonical lift
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}:\{\tilde{f}_{s}\}\to\{\tilde{g}_{s}\}
given by component-wise coCartesian lift, using the locally constant case handled above. We declare this is a
\displaystyle\pi
-coCartesian lift. Replacing disks by the sets
\displaystyle Q_{\beta}
considered in Lemma
6.2.1
, we see that
\displaystyle\pi
-coCartesian-ness can still be checked at
\displaystyle\dagger
-fibers, thus the claim follows from the construction of
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}
and the previous case. That it is a presentable fibration again follows from unwinding the construction of
\displaystyle\widetilde{e}
.
∎

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
denote the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{\textnormal{Vect}/}
, i.e. the pair
\displaystyle(c,C)
where
\displaystyle c\in C\in\textnormal{DGCat}
. The forgetful functor
\displaystyle p:\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}\to\textnormal{DGCat}
is continuous and symmetric monoidal, and is in fact the presentable coCartesian fibration associated with the tautological map
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}\to\textnormal{Pr}^{L}
. We let

\Theta_{X,A}:\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{Pr}^{L}

denote functor corresponding to
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\to\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})
.

Example 6.2.3
.

If
\displaystyle A
is trivial and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\mathsf{LS}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})
is a locally constant cosheaf, then we have
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,\textnormal{triv}}(\mathcal{F})\simeq\Gamma(X,\mathcal{F})\in\textnormal{DGCat}
. Indeed, switching to the LS model, we can identify the fiber as

\limit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}\times_{\limit_{X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}\textnormal{DGCat}}\{x^{\dagger}(\mathcal{F})\}\simeq\limit_{x\in X^{\textnormal{Spc}}}x^{\dagger}(\mathcal{F})\simeq\colimit_{x\in X^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}}x^{\dagger}(\mathcal{F}),

which is by definition the
\displaystyle\dagger
-pushforward to point.

Example 6.2.4
.

In particular, let
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}
denote the cosheafification of the constant copresheaf
\displaystyle\bullet\mapsto\textnormal{Vect}
(it is easy to see that
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}(U)\simeq\textnormal{LS}(U)
, whence the name). Then
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,\textnormal{triv}}(\mathsf{LS})\simeq\textnormal{LS}(X)
.

To describe
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}
in more general cases we need some preparation.

Lemma 6.2.5
.

In the above setting (in fact, for any map
\displaystyle E\to D
of categories), for every
\displaystyle A^{\prime},A^{\prime\prime}\subseteq A
, we have a commutative squares

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X_{A^{\prime}};E)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(\widetilde{j_{A^{\prime}}})_{\dagger}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi_{a}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;E)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(\widetilde{j_{A^{\prime\prime}}})^{\dagger}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime\prime}}(X_{A^{\prime\prime}};E)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\pi_{b}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X_{A^{\prime}};D)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(j_{A^{\prime}})_{\dagger}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{\textnormal{A}}(X;D)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(j_{A^{\prime\prime}})^{\dagger}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime\prime}}(X_{A^{\prime\prime}};D)}

such that the top arrows preserve coCartesian arrows.

Proof.

The first square exists and commutes by definition. Passing to the adjoint horizontally, we have a natural transformation and we reduce to a check on
\displaystyle\dagger
-fibers; the homotopy invariance argument from Lemma
6.2.1
then shows that the diagram actually commutes. The second claim follow similarly.∎

It follows that we have a natural transformation
\displaystyle\eta_{ab}:\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}\Rightarrow\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}\circ(j_{b})^{\dagger}(j_{a})_{\dagger}
(note that
\displaystyle\dagger
-pullback is continuous for constructible sheaves).
Now, let
\displaystyle F=\{F_{a},\varphi_{ab}\}
denote an element of
\displaystyle\mathsf{Glue}(\Phi)\simeq\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;D)
where
\displaystyle F_{i}\in\textnormal{cShv}_{\textnormal{lc}}(X_{a};D)
and
\displaystyle\varphi_{ab}:j_{b}^{\dagger}\circ(j_{a})_{\dagger}(F_{a})\to F_{b}
. We have a continuous functor

\theta_{ab}:=\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(F_{a})\xrightarrow{\eta_{ab}}\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}((j_{b})^{\dagger}(j_{a})_{\dagger}F_{a})\xrightarrow{\varphi_{ab}}\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}(F_{b}).

Proposition 6.2.6
.

\displaystyle\{\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(F_{a}),\theta_{ab}\}
combine into a lax functor
\displaystyle\Xi_{F}:A\dashrightarrow\textnormal{Cat}
such that
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}(F)\simeq\mathsf{Glue}(\Xi_{F})
.

Proof.

By Proposition
9.0.9
, we need to check the following conditions:

1.

There exists fully faithful continuous functors
\displaystyle\phi_{a}:\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(F_{a})\to\Theta_{X,A}(F)
, whose right adjoints are continuous and jointly conservative, and an equivalence
\displaystyle\theta_{ab}\simeq\phi_{b}^{R}\circ\phi_{a}
;

2.

We have
\displaystyle\theta_{ab}(\bullet)\simeq\textnormal{init}_{\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}(F_{b})}
for every
\displaystyle i\not\to j
in
\displaystyle I
.

The second condition is evident because
\displaystyle(\widetilde{j_{b}})^{\dagger}(\widetilde{j_{a}})_{\dagger}
preduces the initial precosheaf. If we consider
\displaystyle F
as an element of
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;D)
, then each
\displaystyle F_{a}\simeq(j_{a})^{\dagger}F
. The first diagram above then gives a functor

\phi_{a}:\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}((j_{a})^{\dagger}F)\xrightarrow{\eta_{\dagger}}\Theta_{X,A}((j_{a})_{\dagger}(j_{a})^{\dagger}F)\xrightarrow{\textnormal{counit}}\Theta_{X,A}(F)

From the second square above, we also obtain a natural transformation
\displaystyle\eta^{\dagger}:\Theta_{X,A}\Rightarrow\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}\circ(j_{a})^{\dagger}
, hence a (continuous) functor

\psi_{a}:=\Theta_{X,A}(F)\xrightarrow{\eta^{\dagger}}\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}((j_{a})^{\dagger}F);

We claim that
\displaystyle\psi_{a}
is the right adjoint of
\displaystyle\phi_{a}
, and
\displaystyle\psi_{a}\circ\phi_{a}\simeq\textnormal{id}
.
This would prove the original claim, since joint conservativity follows from Proposition
9.0.6
, and the equivalence
\displaystyle\theta_{ab}\simeq\varphi_{b}^{R}\circ\varphi_{a}
follows from the functoriality of
\displaystyle\eta^{\dagger}
.

First, note that the composition
\displaystyle\psi_{a}\circ\phi_{a}
is computed by first send an object in the fiber over
\displaystyle F_{a}
along
\displaystyle(\widetilde{j_{a}})_{\dagger}(\widetilde{j_{a}})^{\dagger}
then coCartesian push along the arrow
\displaystyle(j_{a})^{\dagger}\to(j_{a})^{\dagger}(j_{a})_{\dagger}(j_{a})^{\dagger}F
in the base; however, the latter arrow is identity, and the first operation is fully faithful.
To prove adjointness, it remains to exhibit a counit
\displaystyle\phi_{a}\circ\psi_{a}\Rightarrow\textnormal{id}
and check the adjoint axioms. If we denote an object in
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}(F)
by
\displaystyle(F,x)
, then this is a functorial morphism

(F,\textnormal{counit}_{!}((\widetilde{j_{a}})_{\dagger}(\widetilde{j_{a}})^{\dagger}x))\to(F,x)

where
\displaystyle\textnormal{counit}_{!}
is the coCartesian push along
\displaystyle(j_{a})_{\dagger}(j_{a})^{\dagger}F\to F
. By coCartesian-ness this is simply a morphism
\displaystyle(\widetilde{j_{a}})_{\dagger}(\widetilde{j_{a}})^{\dagger}x)\to x
within the total category, which is given by the counit upstairs. The adjoint axioms are checked by unfolding definitions.
∎

Lemma 6.2.7
.

For
\displaystyle(X\to A)\in\textnormal{StratTop}
, the map
\displaystyle\theta_{ab}:\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(\mathsf{LS})\to\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}(\mathsf{LS})
is given by

\mathsf{LS}(X_{a})\xrightarrow{(j_{a})_{\dagger}}\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{Vect})\xrightarrow{(j_{b})^{\dagger}}\mathsf{LS}(X_{b}).

From Proposition
9.0.9
we thus have
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}(\mathsf{LS})\simeq\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{Vect})
.

Proof.

Unfolding definition using the enter-path model, we see that the functor

\mathsf{LS}(X_{a})\xrightarrow{\eta_{ab}}\Theta_{X_{b},\textnormal{triv}}((j_{b})^{\dagger}(j_{a})_{\dagger}(\mathsf{LS}|_{X_{a}}))\xrightarrow{\varphi_{ab}}\mathsf{LS}(X_{b})

identifies with

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}}(X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}\times_{\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{LKE}_{\iota_{a}}\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{a}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
LKE
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X),\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{LKE}_{\iota_{a}}\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{a}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\eta_{a}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}}(X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{a}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X),\textnormal{Un}(C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
res
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/X_{b}^{\textnormal{Spc, {op}}}}(X_{b}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{b}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))}

where
\displaystyle C_{\textnormal{Vect}}:\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)\to\textnormal{DGCat}
is the constant functor mapping everything to
Vect
,
\displaystyle\iota_{a}:X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}}\to\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)
the inclusion,
Un
denotes the corresponding coCartesian fibration, and
\displaystyle\eta_{a}
is given by the universal property of LKE. It suffices to show that the dashed arrow is given by
\displaystyle(j_{a})_{\dagger}
. Flipping the left vertical arrow, it suffices to prove the commutativty of

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{LKE}_{\iota_{a}}\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{a}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
LKE
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\eta_{a}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X),\textnormal{Un}(\textnormal{LKE}_{\iota_{a}}\textnormal{Res}_{\iota_{a}}C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\eta_{a}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(X_{a}^{\textnormal{Spc},\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{Un}(C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
LKE
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{Fun}_{/\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X)}(\textnormal{Entr}_{A}(X),\textnormal{Un}(C_{\textnormal{Vect}}))}

which is because
\displaystyle\eta_{a}
is pointwise colimit-preserving.
∎

6.3
Constructible Action

Recall that a symmetric monoidal coCartesian fibration is a coCartesian fibration that is also a symmetric monoidal functor, and such that the coCartesian arrows are stable under tensor product (
[
GL19a
, 3.3.4.6]
). By
[
GL19a
, 3.3.5.17]
, such a data
\displaystyle p:\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{B}
corresponds to a
lax
symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\mathcal{B}\to\textnormal{Cat}_{\infty}
, where the latter is equipped with the Cartesian monoidal structure. It is easy to see that if
\displaystyle p
is a presentable fibration, then this functor descends to a lax symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\mathcal{B}\to\textnormal{Pr}^{L}
.

The map
\displaystyle p:\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}\to\textnormal{DGCat}
is a symmetric monoidal presentable coCartesian fibration, hence by Proposition
6.2.2
and Remark
6.1.4
the situation above applies. Recall that the unit for
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})
is
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}
, being the cosheafification of the precosheaf unit. Thus we see that for any
\displaystyle F\in\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})
,
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}(F)
has a natural
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{Vect})
-module structure, i.e. we have an enhanced functor

\Theta_{X,A}:\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{DGCat})

which we denote by the same symbol.

In general, the
\displaystyle\dagger
-pullback for
DGCat
-valued constructible cosheaves is
incompatible
with base-change as
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}_{A}
-modules. The following is thus a nontrivial property of this action:

Proposition 6.3.1
.

Let
\displaystyle(X\to A)\in\textnormal{StratTop}
, and let
\displaystyle A^{\prime}\subseteq A
be either upward-closed or an initial element
\displaystyle\{0\}
, then for any
\displaystyle F\in\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})
we have

\Theta_{X,A}(F)\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)}\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X_{A^{\prime}})\simeq\Theta_{X,A^{\prime}}(j_{A^{\prime}}^{\dagger}F).

Proof.

For simplicity let
\displaystyle X^{\prime}:=X_{A^{\prime}}
. First we need a fact:

Lemma 6.3.2
.

\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})
is self-dual as a
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
-module category.

Proof.

Note that
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
is self-dual as a module over itself, so it suffices to demonstrate
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})
as a retract of
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
within
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)\operatorname{-mod}
. If
\displaystyle A^{\prime}
is an upward-closed subposet i.e.
\displaystyle i:X^{\prime}\subseteq X
is a closed embedding, we check that the adjoint pair
\displaystyle i_{\dagger}:\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\adjoint\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X):i^{\dagger}
(where the left adjoint is fully faithful by Proposition
9.0.6
) is
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
-linear, which follows from the explicit description given there. When
\displaystyle A^{\prime}=\{0\}
i.e.
\displaystyle j:X^{\prime}\subseteq X
is an open embedding), since we are in the presentable stable setting, we can instead use the existence of a
right
adjoint
\displaystyle j_{*}
to
\displaystyle j^{\dagger}
(which can be found in
[
AMR21
, Proposition 6.1.6]
), which sets every other component of the lax limit to the zero object; the rest is the same.
∎

By Proposition
6.2.6
we can rewrite the equation as

\mathsf{Glue}_{a\in A}(\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j_{a}^{\dagger}(F)))\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)}\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\xrightarrow{?}\mathsf{Glue}_{a^{\prime}\in A^{\prime}}(\Theta_{X_{a^{\prime}},\textnormal{triv}}(j_{a^{\prime}}^{\dagger}(F)))

Using duality we further expand the left as a cosimplicial limit

\limit_{\bullet}\textnormal{LFun}(\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\tensor\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)^{\tensor\bullet},\mathsf{Glue}_{a\in A}(\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j_{a}^{\dagger}(F))))

Combining Lemma
9.0.8
and Lemma
9.0.4
we rewrite it as

\mathsf{Glue}_{a\in A}(\limit_{\bullet}\textnormal{LFun}(\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\tensor\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)^{\tensor\bullet},\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j_{a}^{\dagger}(F))))

which is

\mathsf{Glue}_{a\in A}(\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})_{\tensor\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)}\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j^{\dagger}_{a}(F))).

Thus we reduce to proving that
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)}\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j^{\dagger}_{a}(F))
is
\displaystyle\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j_{a}^{\dagger}(F))
if
\displaystyle a\in A^{\prime}
, and the empty category otherwise. Note that we can rewrite the expression as

\textnormal{cShv}_{A^{\prime}}(X^{\prime})\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)}\mathsf{LS}(X_{a})\tensor_{\mathsf{LS}(X_{a})}\Theta_{X_{a},\textnormal{triv}}(j^{\dagger}_{a}(F))

thus we reduce to the case of
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}(X_{a})
, which is elementary.
∎

For
\displaystyle p=(I\surj J)\in\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}}
, let
\displaystyle j_{p}:{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(p)\to\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{C})
denote the inclusion. We are now ready to prove

Proposition 6.3.3
.

Given
\displaystyle F\in\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat})
, the assignment

p\in\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}}\mapsto\Theta_{{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(p),A(p)}(j_{p}^{\dagger}F)

is a constructible factorization category over
\displaystyle X(\mathbb{C})
. Combined with
[
Lur12
, 5.5.4.10]
, we obtain a functor

\textnormal{Fact}:\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C}),\textnormal{nu}}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},\textnormal{weak}}.

Proof.

For any symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
and any smooth manifold
\displaystyle M
, we let

\textnormal{Fact}(M)\textnormal{-Alg}^{\textnormal{fact}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\textnormal{Fact}(M)\textnormal{-Alg}(\mathcal{C})

denote the essential image of
\displaystyle\Psi
introduced in
[
Lur12
, 5.5.4.10]
. Elements of this subcategory will be called
factorizable

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-valued
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(M)
-algebra.

We will construct (A) and (B) below

\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C}),\textnormal{nu}}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat})\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\Psi}\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))\textnormal{-Alg}^{\textnormal{fact}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\xrightarrow[\simeq]{(A)}\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{cShvCat},\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{weak}}

\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\textnormal{Conv}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{Ran}\to\textnormal{Part}}}\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{cShvCat},\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},\textnormal{weak}}\xrightarrow{(B)}\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},\textnormal{weak}}.

For (A), let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n\to 1}
denote the full subcategory of coCartesian arrows in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))^{\tensor}
that lie above the active arrow
\displaystyle[n]\to[1]\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
. Consider the functor

\mathscr{P}:{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}\hskip 10.00002pt[n]\mapsto\textnormal{Fun}(\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n\to 1},\textnormal{DGCat})

where for
\displaystyle[n]\to[m]\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}
, the map is given by composing with
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{m\to 1}\to\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n\to 1}
, given by the factorization of coCartesian arrows. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Un}(\mathscr{P})
denote the corresponding coCartesian fibration. Moreover, every
\displaystyle[n_{1}]\sqcup[n_{2}]\simeq[n]
gives rise to a map

\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n\to 1}\to\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n_{1}\to 1}\times\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n_{2}\to 1}

so box product equips
\displaystyle\textnormal{Un}(\mathscr{P})
a symmetric monoidal structure.
We have a naturally defined functor

\eta:\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{Un}(\mathscr{P}))

given by sending a
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))
-algebra
\displaystyle F
and
\displaystyle[n]\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}
to
\displaystyle(n,(p_{0}\to p_{1})\mapsto F(p_{1}))
; the lax symmetric monoidal structure is given by the map
\displaystyle F(U)\tensor F(V)\to F(U\star V)
given by the algebra structure of
\displaystyle F
.
On the other hand, note that
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{cShvCat},\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{weak}}
embeds into the RHS, because each
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))_{n\to 1}
provides a basis for the topology of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}([n])
. It is also clear that its essential image coincides with that of
\displaystyle\eta
: both consists of sections that satisfy cosheaf and factorization conditions. This provides the desired equivalence (A).

For (B), we first need the fact that
\displaystyle\Theta_{X,A}
is
lax
functorial in
\displaystyle(X\to A)
; i.e. for every
\displaystyle f:(X\to A)\to(Y\to B)
we have a map of
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
-modules

\Theta_{Y,B}(-)\tensor_{\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y)}\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)\to\Theta_{X,A}(f^{\dagger}(-)).

(38)

First, we note that the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\times_{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})}\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y;\textnormal{DGCat})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y;\textnormal{DGCat})}

coming from the left square in Lemma
6.2.5
upgrades to a diagram of symmetric monoidal functors, where the left arrow is given by Remark
6.1.4
. (Indeed, pullback of cosheaves is symmetric monoidal, so the right top corner is a limit of symmetric monoidal categories.) It follows that we have a map of
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y)
-module categories
\displaystyle\Theta_{Y,B}(-)\to\Theta_{X,A}(f^{\dagger}(-))
, where
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y)
acts on the right via the map
\displaystyle f^{\dagger}:\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y)\to\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X)
; the claim above then follows by passing to left adjoint.

Thus we have a map
\displaystyle\tilde{\Theta}:\textnormal{StratSpc}^{\textnormal{cShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{StratSpc}^{\textnormal{ShvMod},\vee}
over
\displaystyle\textnormal{StratSpc}^{\textnormal{op}}
. Moreover, for
\displaystyle X\to A,Y\to B
, the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\times\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A\times B}(X\times Y;\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A}(X;\textnormal{DGCat})\times\textnormal{cShv}_{B}(Y;\textnormal{DGCat})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{cShv}_{A\times B}(X\times Y;\textnormal{DGCat})}

is commutative; it follows that
\displaystyle\tilde{\Theta}
is
lax
symmetric monoidal. The existence of (B) now follows Proposition
6.3.1
above.
∎

6.3.4
Variant: Module Categories

The concept of operadic module is defined in
[
Lur12
, Chapter 3.3]
. Fix
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}
-category and
\displaystyle A\in\mathbb{E}_{M}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})
. Fix a point
\displaystyle x\in M
and a particular disk embedding
\displaystyle(D_{x}\subseteq M)\in(\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\tensor})_{\langle 1\rangle}

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{D_{x}}

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\tensor}
consisting of copies of
\displaystyle(D_{x}\subseteq M)
. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{K}^{\prime}

\displaystyle\textstyle{\mathcal{K}^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\mathcal{K}_{\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\tensor}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{e_{0},e_{1}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\mathbb{E}_{D_{x}}\times\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\textnormal{nu},\tensor}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\tensor}\times\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\tensor}}

and let

\textnormal{Mod}_{A,x}^{\mathbb{E}_{M},\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})\subseteq\textnormal{Fun}_{\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\textnormal{nu},\tensor}}(\mathcal{K}^{\prime},\mathcal{C}^{\tensor})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}_{\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\textnormal{nu},\tensor}}(\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\textnormal{nu},\tensor},\mathcal{C}^{\tensor})}\{A\}

be the full subcategory of maps that preserve inert arrows (the map
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\textnormal{nu},\tensor}\inj\mathcal{K}^{\prime}
is the inclusion of null arrows c.f.
[
Lur12
, 3.3.3.2]
). By definition, the category is an operad over
\displaystyle N(\textnormal{Surj}_{*})
, whose fiber over
\displaystyle[k]
consists of all
\displaystyle k
-tuples of non-unital
\displaystyle A
-
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}
-modules inside
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
and
\displaystyle k
-tuples of non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{M}
-module morphisms between them.

Define a category
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}^{\mathsf{Mod}}(M)_{x}^{\tensor}
as follows:

•

Its objects are pairs

(\varphi:I\subseteq[n]\in\mathsf{Comm},(U_{1},\ldots,U_{n}))

where
\displaystyle I
is a (potentially empty) subset, each
\displaystyle U_{j}
such that
\displaystyle j\in\im(\varphi)
is an open subseteq of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}(M)_{x}
, and is otherwise an open subset of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}(M)
;

•

A morphism

(\varphi:I\subseteq[n],(U_{1},\ldots,U_{n}))\to(\psi:J\subseteq[m],(V_{1},\ldots,V_{m}))

only exists when
\displaystyle|I|=|J|
, in which case it is a surjection
\displaystyle\alpha:[n]\surj[m]
that restricts to a bijection
\displaystyle I\simeq J
, and such that for each
\displaystyle j\in J
,
\displaystyle\{U_{i}\}_{\alpha(i)=j}
are pairwise disjoint, and that
\displaystyle\star_{\alpha(i)=j}U_{i}\subseteq V_{j}
.

The category
\displaystyle N(\textnormal{Fact}^{\mathsf{Mod}}(M)_{x}^{\tensor})
is then an
\displaystyle\infty
-operad over
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\tensor}
. A straightforward extension of
[
Lur12
, 5.5.4.10]
(where one uses
[
AF19

to prove the fully faithfulness) allows us to conclude:

Proposition 6.3.5
.

The category
\displaystyle\textnormal{Mod}_{A,x}^{\mathbb{E}_{M},\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})
identifies with the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Alg}_{\textnormal{Fact}^{\mathsf{Mod}}(M)_{x}}(\mathcal{C})\times_{\textnormal{Alg}_{\textnormal{Fact}(M)}(\mathcal{C})}\{\Psi(A)\}

spanned by objects
\displaystyle F
satisfying the following conditions:

1.

the restriction to the objects in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}^{\mathsf{Mod}}(M)_{x,\langle 1\rangle}
containing a marked disk gives a constructible cosheaf on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}(M)_{x}
; and

2.

the map
\displaystyle F(U)\tensor F(V)\to F(U\star V)
is an isomorphism for all
\displaystyle U,V
independent.

The same argument as before then gives that

Corollary 6.3.6
.

For any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
DG category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, There exists a canonically defined functor

\textnormal{Fact}_{\textnormal{ModCat}}:\mathcal{C}\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})},\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{Fact}(\mathcal{C})\textnormal{-FactModCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},\textnormal{weak},x}.

6.3.7
Algebras and Modules

Now we compare internal
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-algebras and modules with the corresponding constructible factorization concepts. Fix an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-DG category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
and let its corresponding factorizable cosheaf of DG categories be
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathcal{C})
. Note that by definition, the category of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-algebras internal to
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
is equivalent to the category

\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))\textnormal{-Alg}^{\textnormal{fact}}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\times_{\textnormal{Fact}(X(\mathbb{C}))\textnormal{-Alg}^{\textnormal{fact}}(\textnormal{DGCat})}\{\Psi(\mathcal{C})\}.

The argument in the proof of Proposition
6.3.3
shows that this is equivalent to a system of objects
\displaystyle\{c_{p}\}
in
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A(p)}({U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(p);\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})
above the elements in
\displaystyle\textnormal{cShv}_{A(p)}({U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(p);\textnormal{DGCat})
corresponding to
\displaystyle j_{p}^{\dagger}(\Psi(\mathcal{C}))
, which are just objects in each
\displaystyle\Theta_{{U_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(p),A(p)}(j^{\dagger}_{p}(\Psi(\mathcal{C})))
. Moreover, that these
\displaystyle c_{p}
correspond to each other under
\displaystyle\dagger
-pullbacks is tautologically equivalent to the statement that they map to each other under the map in Equation
38
. The module case is analogous. We are thus led to the following fact:

Proposition 6.3.8
.

For any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
DG category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, we have an equivalence of categories

\textnormal{Fact}_{\textnormal{Alg}}:\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part}}(\textnormal{Fact}(\mathcal{C}));

for any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
-algebra
\displaystyle A
inside
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, a fixed point
\displaystyle x\in X(\mathbb{C})
and any
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C})}
module category
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
of
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, we have an equivalence of categories

\textnormal{Fact}_{\textnormal{Mod}}:A\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{X(\mathbb{C}),\textnormal{nu}}}(\mathcal{M})\simeq\textnormal{Fact}_{\textnormal{Alg}}(A)\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},x}(\textnormal{Fact}_{\textnormal{ModCat}}(\mathcal{M})).

Remark 6.3.9

(Case of
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
)
.

When our curve is
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
(which is what we use in the main paper), the operad
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}(\mathbb{C})}
is isomorphic to
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
(
[
Lur12
, 5.4.5.3]
), so LHS of Proposition
6.3.8
becomes (non-unital)
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras and
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-modules in the usual sense. However, we avoid utilizing this trivialization until the comparison with Drinfeld center (Proposition
12.1.17
), as it obfuscates the
\displaystyle SO(2)
-equivariance necessary for
combinatorially
constructing the relevant factorization algebras.

7
Quantum Torus

Notation 7.0.1
.

In this subsection, we use the notation
\displaystyle\textbf{K}(G,n)
to denote the homotopy type of the Eilenberg-Maclane space
\displaystyle K(G,n)
.

Let
\displaystyle T
be a torus over
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
with weight lattice
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}
and coweight lattice
\displaystyle\Lambda
; let
\displaystyle\check{T}
be the Langlands dual torus. Consider the mapping space

\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{torus}}:=\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{0}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc})}(B(\check{T}(\mathbb{C}))^{\textnormal{Spc}},\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},4))

This is a strict 2-groupoid classifying braided monoidal 1-categories known as
quantum tori
associated with
\displaystyle T
. It has two homotopy invariants (
[
GL18
, Appendix C]
):

\pi_{0}(\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{torus}})=\textnormal{Quad}(\check{\Lambda}),\pi_{2}(\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{torus}})=\Hom(\check{\Lambda},\mathbb{C}^{\times})

where the former is the set of quadratic forms
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}\times\check{\Lambda}\to\mathbb{C}^{\times}
.

Let us fix a quadratic form
\displaystyle q\in\pi_{0}(\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{torus}})
and let
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
denote the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-DG Category defined in Definition
2.7.2
.
By definition, as an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
DG category,
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
is isomorphic to the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
DG category underlying the symmetric monoidal DG category
\displaystyle\Rep(T)
. It follows from
[
Lur12
, 5.1.3.2]
that the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
operations are
\displaystyle t
-exact with respect to the standard
\displaystyle t
-structure, so that the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
category
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
form a full
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG subcategory. By
[
Lur12
, 5.1.2.4]
, a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure on a Grothendieck abelian category is a (classical) braided monoidal structure on the underlying 1-category (here Convention
6.0.2
is invoked), and the corresponding braided monoidal structure on
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
is the same as what we described above.

Crucially, the above conditions actually uniquely identifies
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
:

Proposition 7.0.2
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}
be an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category. Suppose we are given an equivalence of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
DG categories
\displaystyle\alpha:\mathcal{E}\simeq\Rep(T)
. Then
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}
inherits a
\displaystyle t
-structure from
\displaystyle\Rep(T)
and, by above,
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}^{\heartsuit}
inherits a braided monoidal structure. Suppose we are also given a braided monoidal equivalence
\displaystyle\beta:\mathcal{E}^{\heartsuit}\simeq\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
. Then to
\displaystyle\alpha
and
\displaystyle\beta
we can canonically attach an equivalence of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG categories
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}\simeq\Rep_{q}(T)
.

Proof.

Let us introduce some notations:

•

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}
denote the category of all Grothendieck prestable categories (defined in
[
Lur18
, C.3.0.5]
); it comes with a symmetric monoidal structure by
[
Lur18
, C.4.2.1]
. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{\textnormal{lex}}
denote the 1-full subcategory where we require morphisms to be left exact, and let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{\textnormal{sep},\textnormal{lex}}
denote the full subcategory consisting of separated prestable categories (
[
Lur18
, C.1.2.12]
);

•

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}}
denote the category of Grothendieck abelian categories and exact functors between them;

•

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{+,\textnormal{lex}}
be the category of pairs
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0})
, where
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\in\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{st}}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
is a full subcategory closed under colimits and extensions. A morphism
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0})\to(\mathcal{C}^{\prime},\mathcal{C^{\prime}}_{\geq 0})
is a continuous functor
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C^{\prime}}
that is left
\displaystyle t
-exact, and restricts to a left exact functor
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}\to\mathcal{C}^{\prime}_{\geq 0}
.

By
[
Lur18
, C.5.4.5]
, we have a
fully faithful
map

\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}:\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}}\to\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{\textnormal{sep},\textnormal{lex}},

given by sending an Grothendieck abelian category
\displaystyle\mathcal{H}
to
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})_{\geq 0}
defined in
[
Lur18
, C.1.4.5]
. Moreover, the essential image consists of those prestable categories which are separated and 0-complicial (
[
Lur18
, C.5.3.1]
). By
[
Lur18
, C.3.1.4 and C.3.2.1]
, the stabilization functor

\textnormal{Sp}:\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{\textnormal{lex}}\to\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{+,\textnormal{lex}}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathcal{C}\mapsto(\textnormal{Sp}(\mathcal{C}),\textnormal{Sp}(\mathcal{C})_{\geq 0})

is a fully faithful embedding; here
\displaystyle\textnormal{Sp}(\mathcal{C})_{\geq 0}
is the essential image of
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\subseteq\textnormal{Sp}(\mathcal{C})
. By
[
Lur12
, 1.3.5.21]
, the combination
\displaystyle\textnormal{Sp}\circ\mathcal{D}_{\geq 0}
is the functor of derived category
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(-)
, so we have a fully faithful embedding

\mathcal{D}:\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}}\to\textnormal{Groth}_{\infty}^{+,\textnormal{lex}}.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}}
denote the essential image. By
[
Lur18
, C.3.1.5]
, this category is the category of stable presentable categories
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
equipped with an accessible
\displaystyle t
-structure
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0},\mathcal{C}_{\leq 0})
that is right complete and compatible with filtered colimits, and such that
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}
is separated and 0-complicial. Morphisms in this category are the
\displaystyle t
-exact continuous functors. In other words, we obtain an equivalence

\mathcal{D}:\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}}\simeq\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}}:\textnormal{Heart}

Both sides of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
admit finite products, given by product of
\displaystyle\infty
-categories and
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}^{\prime})_{\geq 0}:=\mathcal{C}_{\geq 0}\times\mathcal{C}^{\prime}_{\geq 0}
. We claim
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
commutes with finite products. It suffices to check this on the underlying pair of
\displaystyle\infty
-categories, i.e. that for any
\displaystyle A,B\in\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}}
we have

\mathcal{D}(A\times B)\simeq\mathcal{D}(A)\times\mathcal{D}(B)\hskip 10.00002pt\mathcal{D}(A\times B)_{\geq 0}\simeq\mathcal{D}(A)_{\geq 0}\times\mathcal{D}(B)_{\geq 0};

which is immediate from the description of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(-)
as a localization via the injective model structure.
Let
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}})^{\times}
and
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}})^{\times}
denote the Cartesian symmetric monoidal structures on them (defined in
[
Lur12
, Chapter 2.4.1]
), then
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(-)
is symmetric monoidal functor between them.

Let
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}
denote the
\displaystyle\infty
-operad encoding a symmetric monoidal algebra along with its left module. The data of an
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Pr}^{L}
, whose underlying
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2}\simeq\mathbb{E}_{\infty}
-algebra is
Vect
, is precisely an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category; likewise, a morphism of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG categories is a map of such
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras that restricts to identity on the algebra part.
We have a pair of equivalence functors

\mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{enh}}:(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}((\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}})^{\times})\simeq(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}((\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}})^{\times}):\textnormal{Heart}^{\textnormal{enh}}

both computed by the underlying functors. The symmetric monoidal forgetful functor
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}})^{\times}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}^{\times}
then gives a functor
\displaystyle\oblv_{t}:(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}((\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}})^{\times})\to(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}(1\textnormal{-Cat}^{\times})
. On the other hand, by
[
Lur12
, 4.8.1.9 and 4.8.1.15]
, there is a
fully faithful
embedding

\oblv_{\textnormal{Pr}}:(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Pr}^{L})\subseteq(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}(1\textnormal{-Cat}^{\times}),

whose image consists of those algebras whose underlying categories are presentable, and whose action maps are colimit-preserving.

Let
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Vect},\Rep_{q}(T))
be the
\displaystyle(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})
-algebra in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Pr}^{L}
observing the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG category structure of
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
. On the other hand, let
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Vect}^{\heartsuit},\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit})\in(\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2})\textnormal{-Alg}((\textnormal{Groth}_{\textnormal{ab}}^{\textnormal{ex}})^{\times})
denote the algebra encoding the
\displaystyle k
-linear braided monoidal category structure of
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}
. It follows from unfolding definition that we have

\oblv_{t}\circ\mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{enh}}((\textnormal{Vect}^{\heartsuit},\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit}))\simeq\oblv_{\textnormal{Pr}}((\textnormal{Vect},\Rep_{q}(T))).

Recall the category
\displaystyle\mathcal{E}
assumed in the statement of the lemma. It now suffices to lift it to an element
\displaystyle(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}_{\geq 0})
of
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Pr}^{\textnormal{t-ex}})^{\times}
and provide an isomorphism of
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}\tensor\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras
\displaystyle\textnormal{Heart}^{\textnormal{enh}}((\mathcal{E},\mathcal{E}_{\geq 0}))\simeq(\textnormal{Vect}^{\heartsuit},\Rep_{q}(T)^{\heartsuit})
that is identity on the algebra part. This is precisely the data of
\displaystyle\alpha
and
\displaystyle\beta
.
∎

7.1
Geometric Construction

Notation 7.1.1
.

Because
\displaystyle\check{T}(\mathbb{C})
is commutative,
\displaystyle B\check{T}(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}
is an infinite loop space. For notational simplicity, let us introduce

\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}}:=\Omega^{2}(B\check{T}(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}})\in\mathbb{E}_{\infty}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc});

this notation is justified because there is indeed an identification of both sides as
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}
-spaces, when the lattice is understood as a discrete topological group. We make this distinction so that
\displaystyle\check{\Lambda}
by itself always denotes the lattice.

Start with a fixed
31
31

31

The ambiguity in
\displaystyle\pi_{2}
does not pose a problem, since the homotopy coherence can be checked by hand.
factorizable Betti gerbe
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}

Since

As a map between

By discussion above,

at

which is by construction the value

\displaystyle q_{g}
denote the image of
\displaystyle g
under

\pi_{0}(\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc})}(\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}},\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},2))\xrightarrow[\textnormal{delooping}]{\simeq}\pi_{0}(\mathcal{P}_{\textnormal{torus}})\simeq\textnormal{Quad}(\check{\Lambda}),

i.e. the quadratic form inside
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
. By Proposition
7.0.2
, this gives us an identification of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
DG categories

\pi_{\dagger}g^{\dagger}(\mathsf{LS}_{\textnormal{univ}}^{\textnormal{tw}})\simeq\Rep_{q_{g}}(T).

We now obtain a more explicit description of
\displaystyle\Psi(\Rep_{q_{g}}(T))
as a factorizable cosheaf of spaces.

In general, let
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
be a non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-category, and
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
a
symmetric monoidal
category. Suppose we are given a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}^{\textnormal{nu}}
-functor
\displaystyle F:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
, then by
[
Lur12
, 5.5.4.10]
we obtain a morphism of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})
-algebras in
\displaystyle 1\textnormal{-Cat}

\displaystyle\Psi(F):\Psi(\mathcal{C})\to\Psi(\mathcal{D})
, which is (
[
Lur12
, 2.4.2.4]
) equivalent to a map
\displaystyle\Psi(F)^{\tensor}:\Psi(\mathcal{C})^{\tensor}\to\Psi(\mathcal{D})^{\tensor}
of coCartesian fibrations over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}
. Now,
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
being symmetric monoidal means we have a well-defined map

\Psi(\mathcal{D})^{\tensor}\to\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}\times_{\mathsf{Comm}}\mathcal{D}^{\tensor}

of coCartesian fibrations over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}
, given by the
unique
push along each
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathcal{D})(U)\to\Psi(\mathcal{D})(\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{R}^{2}))\simeq\mathcal{D}
. Precomposing with
\displaystyle\Psi(F)
we obtain a map
\displaystyle\Psi(F)_{\Gamma}:\Psi(\mathcal{C})^{\tensor}\to\mathcal{D}^{\tensor}
of coCartesian fibrations over
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
that preserve inert maps. Taking relative left Kan extension along
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathcal{C})^{\tensor}\to\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}
with respect to
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
, we arrive at a map

\textnormal{LKE}(\Psi(F)_{\Gamma}):\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}\to\mathcal{D}^{\tensor}

over
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
. On the other hand
\displaystyle\textnormal{LKE}(F):=\colimit F\in\textnormal{Fun}(\textnormal{pt},\mathcal{D})\simeq\mathcal{D}
is a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}^{\textnormal{nu}}
-algebra within
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
, then we can attach to it an object
\displaystyle\Psi_{\mathcal{D}}(\textnormal{LKE}(F))
.
Then we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{LKE}(\Psi(F)_{\Gamma})\simeq\Psi_{\mathcal{D}}(\textnormal{LKE}(F))
: indeed it is easy to see that LHS is a factorizable cosheaf, thus it suffices to produce an equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{LKE}(\Psi(F)_{\Gamma})|_{\textnormal{Disk}(M)}\simeq\textnormal{LKE}(F)
, which now follows from definition.

Apply the above paradigm to
\displaystyle u\circ g:\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}}\to\textnormal{DGCat}
, we obtain an identification

\Psi(\Rep_{q_{g}}(T))\simeq\textnormal{LKE}(\Psi(u\circ g)_{\Gamma}).

On the other hand, from
\displaystyle g:\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}}\to\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},2)
we can obtain a map over
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
given by

\Psi(\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}})^{\tensor}\xrightarrow{\Psi(g)_{\Gamma}}\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},2)^{\tensor}\xrightarrow{u^{\tensor}}\textnormal{DGCat}^{\tensor}

Again taking relative LKE we obtain

\textnormal{LKE}(u^{\tensor}\circ\Psi(g)_{\Gamma}):\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})^{\tensor}\to\textnormal{DGCat}^{\tensor};

Note that
\displaystyle\Psi(u\circ g)_{\Gamma}\simeq u^{\tensor}\circ\Psi(g)_{\Gamma}
, so we have

\Psi(\Rep_{q_{g}}(T))\simeq\textnormal{LKE}(\Psi(u\circ g)_{\Gamma})\simeq\textnormal{LKE}(u^{\tensor}\circ\Psi(g)_{\Gamma}).

The RHS can be understood as assignment to each
\displaystyle U\subseteq\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{R}^{2})
the DG category of
\displaystyle q
-twisted local systems on
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}})(U)
; the extra structure here is the factorization property of this assignment, which we shall discuss after a small digression.

7.1.3
Comparison with Affine Grassmannian

The factorization space
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}})
admits another description as follows.
Recall the non-unital factorization space
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}
, whose
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points give a map of topological spaces

\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}(\mathbb{C})\to\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{C})\simeq\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{R}^{2}).

Consider the copresheaf of spaces over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{R}^{2})
given by

\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}}(U):=[U\times_{\textnormal{Ran}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}(\mathbb{C})]^{\textnormal{Spc}}\in\textnormal{Spc};

The natural inclusion of subspaces then upgrades it to a
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})
-algebra. We claim that it is a
Spc
-valued factorizable cosheaf: indeed, before passing through
\displaystyle\textnormal{Top}\to\textnormal{Spc}
this claim was verified in
[
Noc21
, Section 4]
; since the colimits in the cosheaf condition in this case are homotopy colimits (the relevant maps being monomorphisms of topological spaces), the cosheaf condition still holds as a
Spc
-valued cosheaf.

It then follows that
\displaystyle\Psi^{-1}(\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}})
is a well-defined
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
Spc
. Since we have an identification of weak homotopy types
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}\simeq\Omega^{2}(B\check{T}(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}})
, one is naturally led to believe that
\displaystyle\Psi^{-1}(\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}})
carries the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure from being a double loop space. However, this is not immediate from the factorization perspective.

Remark 7.1.4
.

For a general reductive
\displaystyle G
, the identification of homotopy types
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{G}(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}\simeq\Omega^{2}(BG(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}})
associates to the former an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure. By looking at sections, one expects that the corresponding cosheaf of spaces
\displaystyle\Psi(\textnormal{Gr}_{G}(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}})
is the
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of the Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{G}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}
. We do not need, nor do we prove, this identification for general
\displaystyle G
.

Luckily, we know a bit more about this space, namely that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}
is a
commutative
factorization space under the fiber product symmetric monoidal structure on non-unital factorization spaces. This structure induces an upgrade of
\displaystyle\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}}
as an element of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Fact}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc}))
with respect to the section-wise fiber product (recall that in
Spc
colimits distributes over fiber products). Because
\displaystyle\Psi
is symmetric monoidal (this follows from unwinding construction), we end up producing an element

\Psi^{-1}(\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}})\in\mathbb{E}_{\infty}\textnormal{-Alg}(\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc}))\simeq\mathbb{E}_{\infty}\textnormal{-Alg}(\textnormal{Spc}).

We claim that we have an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}
equivalence
\displaystyle\Psi^{-1}(\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}})\simeq\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}}
, where the latter is given the evident symmetric monoidal structure: indeed, by recognition principle
[
Lur12
, 5.2.6.26]
it suffices to compute the connective spectrum corresponding to
\displaystyle\Psi^{-1}(\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}})
. The underlying space has discrete homotopy type, and the abelian group structure is forced by the additional
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}
structure mentioned above, so the claim follows from
[
Lur12
, 1.4.3.6]
. It follows that

Corollary 7.1.5
.

There is an unique identification of
Spc
-valued factorizable cosheaves
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathbf{\check{\Lambda}})\simeq\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}}
.

Remark 7.1.6
.

In the main proof, it is not
\displaystyle\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}}
, but
\displaystyle\mathsf{Gr}\check{\mathsf{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}
, the
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of the
\displaystyle\check{\rho}
-shifted Grassmannian (c.f. Definition
2.5.1
) that we want to compare with
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
. However, we note that over
\displaystyle\mathbb{A}^{1}
their analytifications are canonically isomorphic.

7.1.7
Ind-Lisse Sheaves

We begin with a basic fact relating local systems as defined above and
ind-lisse
constructible sheaves. Let
\displaystyle Z
be an aft scheme over
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
and let
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}\in\textnormal{Maps}(Z,\textnormal{{Ge}}_{\textnormal{an}})
be an analytic gerbe. Let
\displaystyle g_{0}:Z(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}\to\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},2)
be the map induced by
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}
. Let us define

\mathsf{LS}_{g_{0}}(Z):=\mathsf{LS}_{g_{0}}(Z(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}):=\limit_{Z(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}}\left(Z(\mathbb{C})^{\textnormal{Spc}}\xrightarrow{g_{0}}\textbf{K}(\mathbb{C}^{\times},2)\xrightarrow{u}\textnormal{DGCat}\right);

(39)

The same argument in
[
Gai+20
, Section 1.4]
still gives us the
\displaystyle\dagger
-pull and
\displaystyle\dagger
-push functors. On the other hand, let

consisting of objects whose value lands in the ind-lisse subcategory (i.e. filtered colimits of lisse objects) when pulled back to each

\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}

and
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}
-twisted ind-lisse sheaves
respectively.

The following is an immediate generalization of
[
Gai+20
, Lemma A.4.2]
:

Lemma 7.1.8
.

\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}_{g_{0}}(Z)\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse},\mathscr{G}_{0}}(Z)

For future use, we remark that, if
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}
admits an
étale
trivialization, we can equip both sides of the above lemma with
\displaystyle t
-structures such that the equivalence is
\displaystyle t
-exact:

•

First, being an ind-category,
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(Z):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(Z))
admits a unique
\displaystyle t
-structure (
[
Lur18
, C.2.4.3]
) specified by
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(Z)^{\leq 0}:=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(Z)^{\textnormal{perv}\leq 0})
. It guarantees, by design, that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(Z)\subseteq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(Z)
is
\displaystyle t
-exact;

•

Because the lisse condition is defined on each cohomology sheaf, the lisse subcategory is closed under extensions. It follows (
[
Lur12
, 1.4.4.1]
) that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse}}(Z)^{\leq 0}:=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(Z)^{\textnormal{perv}\leq 0}\cap\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{lisse}}(Z))
generates a
\displaystyle t
-structure for
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse}}(Z)
. Moreover, since
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{lisse}}(Z)
is closed under truncation
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq 0}
, it follows that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse}}(Z)\subseteq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(Z)
is
\displaystyle t
-exact;

•

By assumption, there exists an étale covering
\displaystyle V/Z
such that

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse},\mathscr{G}_{0}}(Z)\simeq\textnormal{Tot}_{!\textnormal{-pull}}\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{ind-lisse},\mathscr{G}_{0}}(V^{\bullet}/Z);

each entry on the RHS has a
\displaystyle t
-structure such that the connecting morphisms are
\displaystyle t
-exact, so it equips LHS with an unique
\displaystyle t
-structure such that
\displaystyle!
-pulling back to each
\displaystyle V^{\bullet}
is
\displaystyle t
-exact;

•

On the other hand,
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}(Z)
, being a limit of categories, has an unique
\displaystyle t
-structure such that each
\displaystyle\dagger
-fiber map is
\displaystyle t
-exact. We also have a descent isomorphism
\displaystyle\mathsf{LS}_{g_{0}}(Z)\simeq\textnormal{Tot}_{\dagger\textnormal{-pull}}\mathsf{LS}_{g_{0}}(V^{\bullet}/Z)
, in which each evaluation is
\displaystyle t
-exact, so we can equip it with a
\displaystyle t
-structure such that the previous lemma is
\displaystyle t
-exact.

7.2
Comparison with Constructible Sheaves

We now return to the question of understanding
\displaystyle\Psi(\Rep_{q_{g}}(T))
explicitly.

Notation 7.2.1
.

During this subsection we will set
\displaystyle\mathsf{GR}_{p}:=\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{U(p)}
for simplicity of notation.

From recollement it is easy to see that, for any analytic factorizable gerbe
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}_{0}
, the system of categories

Proposition 7.2.2
.

We have an identification of weak constructible factorization categories

\textnormal{Fact}(\textnormal{LKE}(u^{\tensor}\circ\Psi(g)_{\Gamma}))\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}}(\mathsf{GR}_{\bullet});

here

Proof.

For each

We slightly abuse notation and let

Combined with discussion from the previous section, we finally arrive at:

Corollary 7.2.3
.

We have an identification of weak constructible factorization categories

\textnormal{Fact}(\Psi(\Rep_{q_{g}}(T)))\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}(\mathbb{A}^{1})_{\textnormal{Ran}}),

Remark 7.2.4
.

We emphasize that the parameter

7.3
Koszul/Verdier Duality

Recall the notion of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-Koszul duality described in Section
2.7.3
. The geometric incarnation of Koszul duality is that of
Verdier duality on the Ran space
. For technical simplicity, we will restrict ourselves to consider Verdier duality on the configuration space instead; algebraically, this corresponds to considering negatively-weighted non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras.

Definition 7.3.1
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
be an analytic gerbe on
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}
and let
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}^{-1}
be the inverse gerbe (i.e. the gerbe corresponding to the inverse bilinear form). For
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf})
, the
Verdier dual
of
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
, to be denoted
\displaystyle\mathbb{D}^{\textnormal{Verdier}}(\mathcal{F})
, is the object in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf})
representing the functor

\mathcal{G}\in\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf})\mapsto\textnormal{Maps}_{\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}\times\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}}\textnormal{Conf})}(\mathcal{F}\boxtimes\mathcal{G},\Delta_{*}(\omega_{\textnormal{Conf}}))\in\textnormal{Spc}

Here
\displaystyle\omega_{\textnormal{Conf}}
is the dualizing sheaf (i.e. the
\displaystyle!
-pullback of
\displaystyle k\in\textnormal{Vect}
) on the configuration space.

Suppose now that
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
is a
factorizable gerbe
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is a factorizable algebra on the configuration space; then it is immediate that the Verdier dual of
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
underlies another factorization algebra (with respect to the dual gerbe), and we will again denote it by
\displaystyle\mathbb{D}^{\textnormal{Verdier}}(\mathcal{F})
. On compact objects, we therefore have a well-defined functor

\mathbb{D}^{\textnormal{Verdier}}:\textnormal{FactAlg}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}))\to\textnormal{FactAlg}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf}))^{\textnormal{op}}.

The enhanced Verdier duality functor has the following universal property, which is easy to verify by unfolding definition: suppose
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is a
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
-twisted factorizable algebra on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}(\mathbb{A}^{1})
whose underlying sheaf object is compact, and
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}
is any
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}^{-1}
-twisted factorization algebra on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Conf}(\mathbb{A}^{1})
. Then we have

\textnormal{Maps}_{\textnormal{FactAlg}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf}))}(\mathcal{G},\mathbb{D}^{\textnormal{Verdier}}(\mathcal{F}))\simeq\textnormal{Maps}_{\textnormal{FactAlg}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}\times\mathscr{G}^{-1}}(\textnormal{Conf}\times_{\textnormal{Ran}}\textnormal{Conf}))}(\mathcal{F}\boxtimes\mathcal{G},\Delta_{*}(\omega_{\textnormal{Conf}}))

here we note that both
\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(\omega_{\textnormal{Conf}})
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}
have evident upgrades to factorization algebras.

We can now state the following compatibility result, first claimed in
[
Gai21a
, 3.4.5]
:

Proposition 7.3.2
.

Let
\displaystyle q
be the quadratic form corresponding to a factorization gerbe
\displaystyle\mathscr{G}
on
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}
. Suppose
\displaystyle A
is a non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
concentrated in negative weights which is weight-wise finite dimensional (i.e.
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}(A)
lands in the compact subcategory
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf})
). Then we have

\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{op}}\circ\textnormal{inv}^{\textnormal{op}}\circ\textnormal{KD}^{\textnormal{nu}}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(A)\simeq\mathbb{D}^{\textnormal{Verdier}}\circ\textnormal{FactAlg}(A),

where
\displaystyle\textnormal{inv}:\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)\to\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)
is the automorphism induced by the Cartan involution of
\displaystyle T
(i.e. one which sends each
\displaystyle{\check{\lambda}}
-weight space to
\displaystyle-{\check{\lambda}}
).

Proof.

We start by giving alternative description of Koszul pairing for
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
.
Note that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))
admits a monoidal structure, and the functor

\textnormal{biact}:[\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))\times\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))]\times\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))\to\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))

given by two-sided multiplication, observes the structure of
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}:=\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))
as being left tensored over the monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{A}:=\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T))\times\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))
. Fix
\displaystyle A\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T)),B\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))
.
Consider the category

\mathcal{C}:=\{a\in\mathcal{A},\varphi:\textnormal{biact}(a,k)\to k\in\mathcal{M}\};

as in
[
Lur12
, 4.7.1]
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
has the structure of a monoidal category, and an
\displaystyle(A,B)
-bimodule structure on
\displaystyle k
is precisely an element of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{C})
lifting
\displaystyle(A,B)\in\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{A})
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}:\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)\to\Rep_{q}(T)
be the monoidal functor of tensor product of graded vector spaces; it induces a plain functor

\textnormal{prod}:\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))\to\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q}(T));

Define

\mathcal{A}^{\prime}:=\textnormal{Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))\hskip 10.00002pt\mathcal{C}^{\prime}:=\{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime},\varphi:\textnormal{prod}(a^{\prime})\to k\in\mathcal{M}\}.

Note that we have a box product
\displaystyle\boxtimes:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
which is monoidal; also note that, as a plain functor,
\displaystyle\textnormal{biact}(-,k):\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{M}
factors as

\mathcal{A}\xrightarrow{\boxtimes}\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\xrightarrow{\textnormal{prod}}\mathcal{M};

It follows that an
\displaystyle(A,B)
-bimodule structure on
\displaystyle k
is the same as an element of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
lifting
\displaystyle A\boxtimes B\in\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})
. Next note that the plain functor
prod
admits a right adjoint
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}^{R}
, and thus we have an induced adjoint pair

\textnormal{prod}:\mathcal{A}^{\prime}\adjoint\mathcal{M}:\textnormal{prod}^{R};

As in
[
Lur12
, 4.7.1.41]
,
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}^{R}(k)\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}
equipped with the obvious map
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}\circ\textnormal{prod}^{R}(k)\to k
is the final object in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}^{\prime}
, and thus admits an unique lifting to an element in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})
; furthermore, an
\displaystyle(A,B)
-bimodule structure on
\displaystyle k
is the same as a map

A\boxtimes B\to\textnormal{prod}^{R}(k)\in\textnormal{Alg}(\mathcal{A}^{\prime})\simeq\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)).

We shall explicitly identify
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}^{R}(k)
. Consider the following
group homomorphism

\textnormal{inv-mult}:T\times T\xrightarrow{\textnormal{id}\times(-)^{-1}}T\times T\xrightarrow{\textnormal{mult}}T

We observe that restriction along
inv-mult
gives a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-map

\textnormal{res}_{\textnormal{inv-mult}}:\Rep(T)\to\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T);

indeed, this claim can be checked on the level of braided monoidal abelian categories. Consider the
QCoh
-adjunction

(p_{T})^{*}:\textnormal{Vect}\adjoint\Rep(T):(p_{T})_{*}

the left adjoint is a fortiori
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
, thus the right adjoint
\displaystyle(p_{T})_{*}
lifts to a lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-map, so that
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{T}:=(p_{T})_{*}(k)
obtains an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra structure, and we set

\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}:=\textnormal{res}_{\textnormal{inv-mult}}(\mathcal{O}_{T})\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)).

Because the object lies in the heart, it is easy to see that
\displaystyle\textnormal{prod}^{R}(k)\simeq\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}
as
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras.

If
\displaystyle A
is an augmented algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, then we have a naturally defined map of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras

\epsilon_{A}:=A\boxtimes k\to k\boxtimes k\simeq k\to(p_{T})_{*}(p_{T})^{*}(k)\simeq\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}.

The discussion above can be summarized as

Corollary 7.3.3
.

For every augmented
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra
\displaystyle A
, its
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
Koszul dual is the universal augmented
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)
representing the functor

B\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{aug}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))\mapsto\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes B,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})

\times_{\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes k,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})\times\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(k\boxtimes B,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})}\{\epsilon_{A},\epsilon_{B}\}.

We observe that when we restricts to negatively-weighted non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras, the pairing admits a simpler description:

Lemma 7.3.4
.

For every non-unital negatively-weighted
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra
\displaystyle A\in\Rep_{q}(T)
, its
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-Koszul dual is the universal positively-weighted non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T)
representing the functor

B\in\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))^{>0}\mapsto\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes\textnormal{inv}(B),\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}_{\Delta}^{<0})

where

•

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q^{-1}}(T))^{>0}
denotes the full subcategory of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras whose underlying object lies in the subcategory of positively-weighted objects (same for
\displaystyle(-)^{>0}
);

•

\displaystyle\textnormal{inv}(B)
is the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-functor of inverting the weight lattice;

•

Let
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}_{\Delta}
be the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra whose underlying object is the restriction of
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{T}
along
mult
, then
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}_{\Delta}^{<0}
is the image of
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}_{\Delta}
under the lax (non-unital)
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
functor

\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)\to\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)^{<0,<0}\to\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)

where the first (lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
) map is projection and second (
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
) map is inclusion.

Proof.

The explicit description of the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-Koszul dual via double Bar construction guarantees that it is positively-weighted, so by Yoneda, it suffices to specify how other positively-weighted non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras map to it. The map
\displaystyle\textnormal{id}\times\textnormal{inv}
is a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-functor on
\displaystyle\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)
, so the space in the statement is the same as

\mathcal{S}_{\textnormal{red}}:=\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes B,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}^{<0,>0})

where
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}^{<0,>0}
is the non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra obtained from
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}
as
\displaystyle\textnormal{inc}_{<0,>0}\circ\textnormal{proj}_{<0,>0}
, where

\textnormal{inc}_{<0,>0}:\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)^{<0,>0})\adjoint\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T)):\textnormal{proj}_{<0,>0}

is the adjoint pair on non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras induced by the inclusion-projection adjoint pair. Set

\mathcal{S}:=\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}((A\oplus k)\boxtimes(B\oplus k),\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})

\times_{\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}((A\oplus k)\boxtimes k,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})\times\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(k\boxtimes(B\oplus k),\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})}\{\epsilon_{A\oplus k},\epsilon_{B\oplus k}\};

Since
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
is stable,
\displaystyle(A\oplus k)\boxtimes(B\oplus k)\simeq A\boxtimes B\oplus A\boxtimes k\oplus k\boxtimes B\oplus k
is the product of its summands (as
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras), so we see that
\displaystyle\mathcal{S}
is isomorphic to
\displaystyle\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes B\oplus k,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})
, which is
\displaystyle\textnormal{Maps}_{\mathbb{E}_{2}\textnormal{-Alg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\Rep_{q\times q^{-1}}(T\times T))}(A\boxtimes B,\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}})
since
\displaystyle(-)\oplus k
is the left adjoint of the functor of forgetting the unital structure. Thus the adjunction
\displaystyle(\textnormal{inc}_{<0,>0},\textnormal{proj}_{<0,>0})
gives an isomorphism
\displaystyle\mathcal{S}_{\textnormal{red}}\simeq\mathcal{S}
.
∎

Under the correspondence between factorizable sheaves and non-unital
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebras, box product matches with box product, and
\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(\omega_{\textnormal{Conf}})
matches with
\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{O}_{T}}_{\Delta}^{<0}
(it is easy to see the underlying object matches; to upgrade to
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure, use the fact that the latter lies in the heart). The original claim follows.
∎
