\displaystyle D_{\varphi}
and
\displaystyle D_{\psi}
are the corresponding prestacks for
\displaystyle G
. The condition of being strictly unital (resp. strictly co-unital, strictly bi-unital) then corresponds to the condition of the left square (resp. right square, both squares) being Cartesian.

Example 10.3.13
.

Any map between unital (resp. co-unital) factorization spaces, considered as one between corr-unital factorization spaces, is automatically strictly unital (resp. counital). A strictly
co-unital
map between
unital
factorization spaces (or vice versa) forces the non-dgenerate square in the above diagram to be Cartesian. Lax-(co)unital maps between (co)unital factorization spaces are not allowed when considering them as corr-unital factorization spaces.

Remark 10.3.14
.

In the correspondence framework of
[
Ras15
]
one can also write down a definition of corr-unital factorization spaces, namely as a
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}_{\textnormal{corr}}
-valued lax prestack. To compare this with our definition one needs to compare the category of categories over
\displaystyle[1]
fibered in spaces with the category of spans in spaces, which is part of Problem 0.17 of
[
AF20
]
. We will not need such comparison here.

Remark 10.3.15
.

Using the lax colimit description one can formulate a description of the category of unital factorization spaces with partition data similar to Proposition
10.2.10
, but the description is more complicated. We leave it to the interested reader.

Convention 10.3.16
.

From now on, we will only introduce the construction of factorization structures for the non-unital version, with the implicit understanding that the corresponding unital version can be defined similarly. There are a few places where complications do occur, at which point we address them separately.

10.4
Factorization Module Spaces

The CM Operad

We have the colored operad
\displaystyle\textnormal{CMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}
, which consists of two colors
\displaystyle\mathfrak{a}
and
\displaystyle\mathfrak{m}
, and such that

\textnormal{Mul}(\{X_{i}\},Y)=\begin{cases}*&\textnormal{if}~Y=X_{i}=\mathfrak{a}\textnormal{ for all }i\\
*&\textnormal{if}~Y=\mathfrak{m}\textnormal{ and }X_{i}=\mathfrak{m}\textnormal{ for exactly one }i\\
\emptyset&\textnormal{otherwise}\end{cases}

Let
\displaystyle{\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\tensor}
be the associated
\displaystyle\infty
-operad. Unwinding definitions we find that it is given by the following category:

•

Its objects are pairs
\displaystyle(I,M)
where
\displaystyle I
is a nonempty finite set and
\displaystyle M\subseteq I
is a (potentially empty) subset;

•

A morphism from
\displaystyle(I,M)
to
\displaystyle(J,N)
only exists when
\displaystyle|M|=|N|
, in which case it is a surjection
\displaystyle p:I\surj J
that restricts to a bijection
\displaystyle M\simeq N
. We will often only write
\displaystyle M\subseteq I\surj J
for the morphism when no confusion is likely to occur.

Variant 10.4.1
.

We also have the
unital
CM operad
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}^{\tensor}
, where we replace “surjective map” with “arbitrary map” in the definition above.

Remark 10.4.2
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Mod}^{\textnormal{Comm}}(\mathcal{C})
be the
\displaystyle\infty
-operad of
\displaystyle E_{\infty}
-algebras and its
\displaystyle E_{\infty}
-modules (defined in
[
Lur12
, 3.3.3.8]
), and let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Mod}^{\textnormal{Comm}}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C}):=\textnormal{Mod}^{\textnormal{Comm}}(\mathcal{C})\times_{\mathsf{Comm}}N_{*}(\textnormal{Surj})
be the base change such that we only allow surjective morphisms in
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
. By
[
Lur12
, 4.5.1.4]
(and its non-unital variant) we have an equivalence of categories
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}_{{\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}}}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{Mod}^{\textnormal{Comm}}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}_{\mathsf{CM}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\textnormal{Mod}^{\textnormal{Comm}}(\mathcal{C})
.

Definition 10.4.3
.

Taking opposite category over each arity,
\displaystyle(\mathsf{CM}^{\textnormal{op}})^{\tensor}
is again a
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}^{\tensor}
-monoidal operad. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Env}((\mathsf{CM}^{\textnormal{op}})^{\tensor})
denote its
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}
-monoidal envelope of
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}^{\textnormal{op}}
, and set

\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}:=\textnormal{Env}((\mathsf{CM}^{\textnormal{op}})^{\tensor})_{\langle 1\rangle}.

This category can be explicitly described as follows:

•

Its objects are pairs
\displaystyle(Z\subseteq I)
, where
\displaystyle I
is a finite (potentially empty) set and
\displaystyle Z
is a subset of size at most 1;

•

Those objects with
\displaystyle Z\simeq\emptyset
are of color
\displaystyle\mathfrak{a}
, and others are of color
\displaystyle\mathfrak{m}
;

•

A morphism
\displaystyle(Z_{1}\subseteq I_{1})\to(Z_{2}\subseteq I_{2})
only exists when
\displaystyle|Z_{1}|\simeq|Z_{2}|
, in which case it is a map
\displaystyle I_{1}\leftarrow I_{2}
in
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
that maps
\displaystyle Z_{2}
to
\displaystyle Z_{1}
isomorphically;

•

For
\displaystyle I\in\mathsf{Comm}^{\textnormal{op}}
, we will use
\displaystyle I_{\mathfrak{a}}
to denote
\displaystyle(\emptyset\subseteq I)\in\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}
, and
\displaystyle I_{\mathfrak{m}}
to denote
\displaystyle(\{*\}\subseteq I)\in\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

Variant 10.4.4
.

The non-unital version
\displaystyle\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}_{\textnormal{nu}}
is defined analogously, by replacing
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
with
\displaystyle{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
everywhere, and disallowing empty sets for
\displaystyle I
.

Remark 10.4.5
.

By definition, a
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}
-monoidal functor from
\displaystyle\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}
to another
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}
-monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
is precisely a
lax

\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}
-monoidal functor
\displaystyle\mathsf{CM}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\mathcal{C}
.

Now we are ready to define factorization module spaces:

Definition 10.4.6
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{RanModMonoid}_{\textnormal{nu}}
denote the category

\textnormal{Fun}^{\mathsf{CM}\textnormal{-lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}_{\textnormal{nu}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{op}}\}

We refer to this category as category of Ran-module monoids. If
\displaystyle Z
is the image of
\displaystyle[1]_{\mathfrak{m}}
, we will denote the corresponding element by
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}},Z)
.

Example 10.4.7
.

\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}
is itself a Ran-module monoid.

Definition 10.4.8
.

For a fixed Ran-module monoid
\displaystyle Z
, let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactModSpace}_{\textnormal{nu}}(Z)
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\mathsf{CM}\textnormal{-lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}_{\textnormal{nu}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})_{(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}},Z)/}

satisfying condition L (i.e. the natural transformations from the lax structure are Cartesian). We refer to this category as the category of non-unital factorization module spaces of type
\displaystyle Z
.

Variant 10.4.9
.

The unital versions
\displaystyle\textnormal{RanModMonoid}_{\textnormal{un}}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactModSpace}_{\textnormal{un}}(Z)
are defined analogously using
\displaystyle\mathsf{ECM}^{\textnormal{op}}
instead.

Example 10.4.10
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Arr}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}})
denote the arrow lax prestack, given by
\displaystyle S\mapsto\textnormal{Fun}([1],\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}(S))
. It admits two maps
\displaystyle\pi_{s}
and
\displaystyle\pi_{t}
to
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
, by mapping to the source and target respectively.

For any
\displaystyle\epsilon_{R}:R\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
, we define

\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\epsilon_{R}}:=R_{\epsilon_{R}/}:=R\times_{\epsilon_{R},\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}},\pi_{s}}\textnormal{Arr}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}).

For any map
\displaystyle\eta:R\to\textnormal{Ran}
to the non-unital Ran space, we define
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\eta}
as

\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu},\eta}:=\left(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},(\textnormal{Ran}\inj\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}})\circ\eta}\right)\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu},\eta}:=\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\eta}^{\textnormal{PreStk}}.

We sometimes also the notation
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{R}
to denote this space, when the map is clear from the context. Explicitly, on the object-level it is given by

\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu},R}(S)=\{\alpha\in R(S),\beta\in\textnormal{Ran}(S)\mid\epsilon_{R}\circ\alpha\subseteq\beta\}

We have evident maps

\textnormal{pr}_{R}:(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto\alpha\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{pr}_{\textnormal{Ran}}:(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto\beta;

and the action of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},R}
is by union with
\displaystyle\beta
.

Cases that we will need include (all for the unital version):

•

\displaystyle R=\emptyset
, so we get
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
, the unmarked Ran space itself;

•

For
\displaystyle S
affine and a fixed subgroupoid
\displaystyle\overrightarrow{x}=\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\}\subset X(S)
, we let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\overrightarrow{x}}
denote the lax prestack
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{S}
for the map
\displaystyle S\xrightarrow{\overrightarrow{x}}X^{n}\to\textnormal{Ran}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
;

•

\displaystyle R=X^{I}\to\textnormal{Ran}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
, in which case we denote the resulting lax prestack simply by
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},X^{I}}
;

•

Recursively, we can let
\displaystyle R=\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},R^{\prime}}
via
\displaystyle\textnormal{pr}_{\textnormal{Ran}}
for any
\displaystyle R^{\prime}
, so on and so forth.

10.5
Factorization Categories and Algebras

The functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{ShvCat}(-):\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}
corresponds to a Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
. Similarly, the functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{ShvCatSect}(-):\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}\to 1\textnormal{-Cat}
which sends
\displaystyle S
to the category of pairs
\displaystyle(\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{ShvCat}(S),f\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal{F}))
also gives rise to a Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCatSect}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
. The natural forgetful functor then gives a tower of maps

\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCatSect}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}}\to\textnormal{PreStk};

Note that the first map is not a (co)Cartesian fibration.
Box product then equips each level with a symmetric monoidal structure, such that all maps above are symmetric monoidal.

Definition 10.5.1
.

Let
\displaystyle Z
be a non-unital factorization space. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu},Z}
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk})}\{Z\}

consisting of those maps
\displaystyle F
satisfying the following conditions:

(Condition R)

For every
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(I)\to F(J)
is Cartesian with respect to the Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
;

(Condition L)

For every
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(I)\to\bigotimes_{j}F(I_{j})
is Cartesian with respect to the Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
.

An element of this category is called a non-unital factorization category over
\displaystyle Z
.

Convention 10.5.2
.

Our
default
choice is
\displaystyle Z=\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
(in the non-unital case) and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}
(in the unital case); in such case, we omit the
\displaystyle Z
subscript. When we work over other factorization spaces (e.g.
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}
itself), we will explicit warn our readers.

Definition 10.5.3
.

Let
\displaystyle Z
be a non-unital factorization space and
\displaystyle C\in\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}(Z)
. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(C)
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCatSect}})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}})}\{C\}

satisfying the corresponding conditions L and R with respect to the Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCatSect}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
. An element of this category is called a non-unital factorization algebra within
\displaystyle C
.

Variant 10.5.4
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
denote the dual
coCartesian
fibration associated with
ShvCat
. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{dual}}(Z)
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{o}p,\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{Z^{\textnormal{op}}\}

satisfying the following conditions:

(Condition R)

For every
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(J)\to F(I)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
;

(Condition L)

For every
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle\bigotimes_{j}F(I_{j})\to F(I)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

The category
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{dual}}(Z)
can be defined analogously.

Remark 10.5.5
.

Obviously we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{dual}}(Z)\simeq\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}(Z)
.

10.5.6
Partition Description

In alignment with the choices made above, we make the following definition:

Definition 10.5.7
.

We define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{weak}}
as the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk})}\{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}\}

such that

(Condition L)

For every
\displaystyle I\to J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(I)\to\bigotimes_{j}F(I_{j})
is Cartesian with respect to the Cartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCat}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}
.

Similar we define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{weak}}(C)
for any factorization category
\displaystyle C
.

For technical purposes, however, we will exclusively work with the dual version:

Variant 10.5.8
.

We define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}
as the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}^{\textnormal{op}}\}

such that

(Condition R)

For every
\displaystyle I\to J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(J)\to F(I)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

We can similarly define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}(C)
for any factorization category
\displaystyle C
.

Remark 10.5.9
.

We note that the notion definition of a (strong) factorization algebra / module only requires a
weak
factorization category as background.

Remark 10.5.10
.

There exists an equivalence of categories
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{weak}}\simeq\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}
compatible with the embeddings from
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}(Z)\simeq\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{dual}}(Z)
. The analogous statement holds for factorization algebras.

Remark 10.5.11
.

Note that, in
[
Ras15
]
, a weak factorization category (resp. algebra) is defined as a commutative algebra in a certain correspondence category of Grothendieck fibrations; such notion coincides with our
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}
. The comparison follows easily from
[
Lur12
, 2.2.4.9]
and Lemma
10.1.1
.
45
45

45

Note that our condition L is hidden in
[
Ras15
, 5.14]
, and that composability condition in Lemma
10.1.1
is vacuous in this case as remarked in
[
Ras15
, 8.12]
.
The algebra case follows by comparing the category
\displaystyle(\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{ShvCatSect}})_{\textnormal{corr}}
with the category
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}
in

Ras15
, 5.26]
.

Now we introduce the partition description:

Definition 10.5.12
.

We let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Dbl},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Dbl},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{U_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}^{\textnormal{op}}\}

consisting of maps
\displaystyle F
such that:

(Condition R’)

For every
\displaystyle(I\to J)\to(I^{\prime}\to J^{\prime})\in\mathsf{Dbl}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(I\to J)\to F(I^{\prime}\to J^{\prime})
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

We let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{Part}}
denote the full subcategory of
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}
where additionally,

(Condition L’)

For every
\displaystyle I\to J\to K\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle\bigotimes_{k}F(I_{k}\to J_{k})\to F(I\to J)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}

The category
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C)
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C)
for a fixed factorization category

Proposition 10.5.13
.

There is a natural equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}\simeq\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}
which restricts to an equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{Part}}\simeq\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu}}
. The analogous statement holds for factorization algebras in a factorization category
\displaystyle C
.

Proof.

We treat the category case by essentially copying the proof from
[
Ras15
, 8.4.1]
with added details; the algebra case is completely analogous.
Let
\displaystyle\pi:\mathsf{Tpl}\to\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}}
denote the map
\displaystyle(I\to J\to K)\mapsto(J\to K)
.
Passing to the monoidal envelope we obtain an adjunction

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\simeq\textnormal{Fun}^{\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Dbl},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\simeq\textnormal{Fun}^{\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Tpl},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})

We hope to use monoidal right Kan extension along
\displaystyle\pi
to relate the RHS categories. In general, however, box product of sheaves of categories do not distribute over limits, so RKE along
\displaystyle\pi
only yields a map between lax-monoidal functor categories. Nevertheless, we claim that for any
\displaystyle F,G\in\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{Dbl},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})
satisfying condition (R’),

(\limit_{I\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}}(\pi_{I})_{*}(F(I)))\boxtimes(\limit_{J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}}(\pi_{J})_{*}(G(J)))\to\limit_{I,J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}}(\pi_{I})_{*}(F(I))\boxtimes(\pi_{J})_{*}(G(J))

(where
\displaystyle\pi_{I}:X^{I}_{\textnormal{dR}}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
is the structure map) is an isomorphism. Indeed, condition (R’) guarantees that for any affine
\displaystyle S
and any
\displaystyle I_{1}\surj I_{2}
, the section
\displaystyle(\pi_{I_{2}})_{*}(F(I_{2}))(S)\to(\pi_{I_{1}})_{*}(F(I_{1}))(S)
admits a left adjoint, so we can turn the limits above to colimits and commute with box product. It follows that when restricting to this subcategory, RKE (and
Res
) preserve the strictly symmetric monoidal functors. Moreover, for the same reason the resulting right Kan extension will satisfying condition (R). Thus monoidal right Kan extension induces an adjunction

\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Ran}\to\textnormal{Part}}:\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}\adjoint\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{Part},\textnormal{L-weak}}:\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Part}\to\textnormal{Ran}};

explicitly, the right adjoint sends
\displaystyle F:{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}
to

p=(I\surj J)\mapsto\pi_{p}^{*}(F(J))\in\textnormal{ShvCat}(U_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}(p))\hskip 10.00002pt\pi_{p}:U_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}(p)\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}(J);

and the left adjoint sends
\displaystyle T:\mathsf{Dbl}\to\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}
to

J\mapsto\limit_{p=(J^{\prime}\surj J)}(\pi_{p})_{*}(T(p))\in\textnormal{ShvCat}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}(J)).

It is easy to check that the full subcategories of factorization objects are preserved by this adjunction, and it remains to check the unit and counit of this adjunction are isomorphisms.
Condition R and R’ guarantee that forgetful functors
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}\to\textnormal{ShvCat}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}})
and

\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}\to\textnormal{Fun}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{I\mapsto X^{I}_{\textnormal{dR}}\}

are both conservative. Unfolding definition, we see that we need to check

F\simeq\limit_{I\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}}(\pi_{I})_{*}(\pi_{I})^{*}F\hskip 10.00002pt\hskip 10.00002ptT(J)\simeq\pi_{J}^{*}(\limit_{I}(\pi_{I})_{*}T(I))\forall J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}^{\textnormal{op}}

for every
\displaystyle F
which is the restriction of an element in
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}
(resp.
\displaystyle T
a restriction of an element in
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}
). The unit follows from the fact that
ShvCat
is a right Kan extension.

Set
\displaystyle T_{J}:=\Gamma(X^{J}_{\textnormal{dR}},T(J))
.
For
\displaystyle S
affine mapping to
\displaystyle X^{J}_{\textnormal{dR}}
, the two sides of the counit evaluates to

\textnormal{QCoh}(S)\tensor_{\textnormal{DMod}(X^{J})}T_{J}\to\limit_{I}\limit_{R\in\mathcal{D}_{I,J}^{\textnormal{op}}}\textnormal{QCoh}(R)\tensor_{\textnormal{DMod}(X^{I})}T_{I}

where

10.5.14
The Unital Case

First note that
ShvCat
can be defined for all lax prestacks (
[
Ras15
, 4.19]
). Explicitly, if
\displaystyle S
is affine and
\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}
is a lax prestack, a sheaf of categories
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
over
\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}
attaches to each
\displaystyle\varphi\Rightarrow\psi\in\mathcal{Y}(S)
an
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
-linear map
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{\varphi}\to\mathcal{F}_{\psi}
.
We now define unital factorization categories and algebras.

Definition 10.5.15
.

Let
\displaystyle Z
be a unital factorization space.
We define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{L-weak},Z}
as the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}(\mathsf{Comm}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee})\times_{\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{lax},\tensor}(\mathsf{Comm}^{\textnormal{op}},\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op}})}\{Z^{\textnormal{op}}\}

consisting of maps
\displaystyle F
such that

(Condition R)

For every surjective
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(J)\to F(I)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
;

(Condition Z)

For every map
\displaystyle[0]\to I\in\mathsf{Comm}
, the arrow
\displaystyle F(I)\to F([0])
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
;

(Condition C)

For every composable pair of morphisms
\displaystyle I\to J\to K
in
\displaystyle\mathsf{Comm}
, the commutative square

\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{j=1}^{J}F([1])\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{k=1}^{K}F(J_{k})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{j=1}^{J}F(I_{j})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{k=1}^{K}F(I_{k})}

is coCartesian within
\displaystyle\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}
;

we define
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{un},Z}
as the full subcategory consisting of objects that additionally satisfy

(Condition L)

For every surjective
\displaystyle I\surj J\in{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the arrow
\displaystyle\bigotimes_{j}F(I_{j})\to F(I)
is coCartesian with respect to the coCartesian fibration
\displaystyle\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op},\textnormal{ShvCat},\vee}\to\textnormal{LaxPreStk}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

Remark 10.5.16

Again, in the non-unital case condition C was subsumed.

Variant 10.5.17

In accordance with previous notations, we let
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactCat}_{\textnormal{un},Z}

Variant 10.5.18

For a given unital factorization category

can be defined analogously.

10.6
Restriction of Modules

We shall adopt the following notations:

•

\displaystyle\epsilon:R\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}}
for
\displaystyle R

Let

The main fact we establish in this section is:

Proposition 10.6.1
.

In the above setting, there exists an a well-defined continuous functor

\textnormal{res}_{f}:B\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(C_{M})\to A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(C_{M});

This functor has the following properties:

1.

It is functorial in
\displaystyle f
;

2.

\displaystyle\epsilon_{\textnormal{dR}}^{!}\circ\textnormal{res}_{f}\simeq\epsilon_{\textnormal{dR}}
for every
\displaystyle f
.

An analogous non-unital version also exists.

Example 10.6.2
.

Let
\displaystyle B
be a unital factorization algebra within
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un}})
and let
\displaystyle M_{0}
denote a unital
\displaystyle B
-factorizable module within
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},X})

be a map of unital factorization algebras. Then

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{res}_{f}(M_{0})|_{X^{2}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

\displaystyle\textstyle{j_{*}j^{*}(A|_{X}\boxtimes M_{0}|_{X})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

where

is the inclusion of the complement of the diagonal. The unital structure at this level amounts to two maps

Remark 10.6.3

In the

Here we use the fact that

The idea of the construction is simple: we first forget the data
\displaystyle(B,M)
to a
weak

\displaystyle B
-factorization module, which then allows us to restrict to a
weak

\displaystyle A
-factorization module
\displaystyle(A,M)
. We then apply the right adjoint to the forgetful functor from factorization modules to weak factorization modules to rebuild a factorization module. The work then lies in giving a homotopically coherent definition of this “rebuilding” procedure—for which we use the partition description of factorization algebras/modules and the theory of operadic Kan extension.
The rest of the proof is pure combinatorics.

We first treat the non-unital case.

Convention 10.6.6

\displaystyle\textstyle{J\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

Since we work in the stable setting, that the necessary

\displaystyle\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}
-monoidal functor
\displaystyle\bar{F}:=\textnormal{RKE}_{\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}}(\widetilde{F})
. Evidently
\displaystyle F\mapsto\bar{F}
is the right adjoint to the forgetful functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{Fun}^{\tensor}(\mathsf{Dbl},\mathscr{C})\to\textnormal{Fun}^{\tensor,\textnormal{lax}}(\mathsf{Dbl},\mathscr{C})
.

Lemma 10.6.10
.

If
\displaystyle F
sends all arrows to coCartesian arrows, then so does
\displaystyle\bar{F}
.

We demonstrate the case for
\displaystyle{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
; the
\displaystyle{\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
case is completely analogous.

Proof.

For
\displaystyle p_{1}\to p_{2}\in\mathsf{Dbl}
, let
\displaystyle\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}:\Gamma(U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p_{1}),\mathcal{C})\to\Gamma(U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p_{2}),\mathcal{C})
be the structural morphism. Let
\displaystyle\pi:\mathsf{Tpl}\to\mathsf{Dbl}
be the projection. Concretely, we want the statement that for any
\displaystyle p_{1}\to p_{2}\in\mathsf{Dbl}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
an
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}
-weak factorization algebra, the natural morphism

\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}(\limit_{q_{1}\in\mathsf{Tpl}_{p_{1}/}}\varphi_{p_{1}\to\pi(q_{1})}^{R}(\mathcal{F}(q_{1})))\to\limit_{q_{2}\in\mathsf{Tpl}_{p_{2}/}}\varphi_{p_{2}\to\pi(q_{2})}^{R}(\mathcal{F}(q_{2}))

is an isomorphism. Using assumption on
\displaystyle\varphi
we can rewrite the morphism as

\limit_{q_{1}\in\mathsf{Tpl}_{p_{1}/}}\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}\circ\varphi_{p_{1}\to\pi(q_{1})}^{R}(\mathcal{F}(q_{1}))\to\limit_{q_{2}\in\mathsf{Tpl}_{p_{2}/}}\varphi_{p_{2}\to\pi(q_{2})}^{R}(\mathcal{F}(q_{2}))

and the map is restriction to a subdiagram
\displaystyle Q
of those
\displaystyle q
such that
\displaystyle p_{1}\to q
factors as
\displaystyle p_{1}\to p_{2}\to q
, followed by the morphism obtained via

[\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}\circ\varphi^{R}_{p_{1}\to\pi(q)}]\simeq[\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}\circ\varphi^{R}_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}\circ\varphi^{R}_{p_{2}\to\pi(q)}]\xrightarrow{\textnormal{counit}}[\varphi^{R}_{p_{2}\to\pi(q)}]

Write
\displaystyle p_{1}=I_{1}\surj J_{1}
,
\displaystyle p_{2}=I_{2}\surj J_{2}
, and running induction on
\displaystyle|I_{1}-I_{2}|+|J_{2}-J_{1}|
we reduce to the following two cases:

Case 1

\displaystyle I_{1}=I_{2}=:I,|J_{2}|=|J_{1}|+1
: this is the open embedding case. We can replace
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}
with
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}
on both sides. Without loss of generality, we can assume the map
\displaystyle p_{1}\to p_{2}
is induced by the map
\displaystyle J_{2}\surj J_{1}:\{1,2\}\mapsto 1,\ldots,|J_{1}|\mapsto|J_{1}|-1,|J_{1}|+1\mapsto|J_{1}|
.
For any term
\displaystyle I\to J\to K
included in the subdiagram
\displaystyle Q
, the map is given by (we omit the
\displaystyle I
-part)

[\varphi_{(J_{1})\to(J_{2})}\circ\varphi_{(J_{1})\to(J_{2})}^{R}\circ\varphi_{(J_{2})\to(J)}^{R}]\to[\varphi_{(J_{2})\to(J)}^{R}]

which is an isomorphism by assumption. It remains to check that restriction to the smaller diagram does nothing. Note that
\displaystyle\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/}
as an under-category admits a coproduct structure
\displaystyle\sqcap
, such that

U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p\sqcap(I\to J_{2}))\simeq U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)\cap U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(I\to J_{2});

we define
\displaystyle\Psi(I\to J)=(I\to J)\sqcap(I\to J_{2})
and extend it to
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/}
via identity. By base change, it suffices to show that
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{2}/}
is left cofinal within
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/})
, but this is clear: after inverting isomorphisms,
\displaystyle\Psi(\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/})
indeed retracts onto
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{2}/}
.

Case 2

\displaystyle|I_{1}|=|I_{2}|+1,J_{1}=J_{2}=:J
: this is the diagonal embedding case. To avoid considering non-continuous functors we again replace
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}
with
\displaystyle\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}
on both sides. Without loss of generality we assume the mapping on
\displaystyle I
is
\displaystyle\{1,2\}\mapsto 1,\ldots,|I_{2}|+1\mapsto|I_{2}|
; in other words, the corresponding closed subscheme is
\displaystyle\{x_{1}=x_{2}\}
; let
\displaystyle\Delta
denote this closed embedding.
We claim that, upon taking
\displaystyle\varphi_{p_{1}\to p_{2}}
, those nodes in
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}(\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/})
that do not become zero form a diagram isomorphic to
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}(\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{2}/})
. By (weak) factorization, it suffices to note that the full subcategory of arrows
\displaystyle I_{1}\to J^{\prime}
in
\displaystyle\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{1}/}
that admit a dotted arrow (which is by definition unique) like follows:

\displaystyle\textstyle{I_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{I_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{J}
\displaystyle\textstyle{J^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

is isomorphic to
\displaystyle\mathsf{Dbl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p_{2}/}
(the map is by sending it to the dotted arrow).
∎

To summarize, the forgetful functor

\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}\textnormal{-FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}\textnormal{-FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{L-weak}}(\mathcal{C})

admits a right adjoint
\displaystyle\mathsf{strc}_{\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}}
, which can be explicitly computed as

\mathsf{strc}_{\mathcal{O}^{\tensor}}(\mathcal{F})(p)=\limit_{q\in\mathsf{Tpl}^{\textnormal{top}}_{p/}}\varphi_{p\to\pi(q)}^{R}\left(\mathcal{F}(q)\right)

for each
\displaystyle p\in\mathsf{Dbl}
, where
\displaystyle\pi:\mathsf{Tpl}\to\mathsf{Dbl}
is the projection,
\displaystyle\varphi_{p\to\pi(q)}^{R}
is right adjoint to the structure morphism
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}(p)\to\mathcal{C}(\pi(q))
.

Proof of Proposition
10.6.1
.

The following discussion applies to both the unital and the non-unital case. Consider the tautological inclusion

\oblv_{\textnormal{mod}}^{s\to w}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})\to A\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})

By considerations above, this functor admits a right adjoint, which we denote by
\displaystyle\oblv_{\textnormal{mod}}^{s\to w,R}
and is computed by
\displaystyle\mathsf{strc}_{\mathsf{CM}}
. Since weak modules are actual modules in the correspondence category (see Remark
10.5.11
, or use the interpretation of lax monoidal functors as algebra objects under Day convolution), by
[
Lur12
, 4.2.3.1]
, for any morphism
\displaystyle f:A\to B
in
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C)
, we have a functor

\textnormal{res}^{w}_{f}:B\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})\to A\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})

which commutes with all small limits and colimits.

Definition 10.6.14
.

We
define
the restriction functor of (strong) factorization modules as

\textnormal{res}_{f}:=B\textnormal{-FactMod}(C_{M})\xrightarrow{\oblv_{\textnormal{mod}}^{s\to w}}B\textnormal{-FactMod}\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})

\xrightarrow{\textnormal{res}^{w}_{f}}A\textnormal{-FactMod}\textnormal{-FactMod}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{L-weak},\textnormal{Part}}(C_{M})\xrightarrow{\oblv_{\textnormal{mod}}^{s\to w,R}}A\textnormal{-FactMod}(C_{M}).

Using the description obtained in previous section, we get an explicit expression

\textnormal{res}_{f}(M)(p)=\limit_{q\in\textnormal{Env}_{\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\tensor}}(\textnormal{Tw}(\mathsf{CM}_{\textnormal{nu}})^{\textnormal{op}})^{\textnormal{top}}_{p/}}\varphi_{p\to\pi(q)}^{R}(A\boxtimes M)(q),

from which the second property is also evident.
∎

10.7
Commutative Case

We now consider the counterpart of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\infty}
-objects in the factorization world.

On the space level, we have the notion of
commutative
factorization spaces. Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{comm}}
denote the oplax functor corresponding to
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{comm}}
described above. There is then a natural transformation
\displaystyle\eta:\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}\Rightarrow\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{comm}}
. It is easy to see that pullback along
\displaystyle\eta

\eta^{*}:\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk})_{/\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{comm}}}\to\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk})_{/\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}}.

Definition 10.7.1
.

Let
\displaystyle\textnormal{CommFactSpace}_{\textnormal{nu}}
denote the full subcategory of

\textnormal{Fun}^{\textnormal{oplax},\tensor}_{\textnormal{nu}}({\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}},\textnormal{PreStk})_{/\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{nu}}^{\textnormal{comm}}}

consisting of object
\displaystyle F
satisfying condition L and

(Condition C)

For every composable pair of morphisms
\displaystyle I\to J\to K
in
\displaystyle{\mathsf{Comm}_{\textnormal{nu}}}
, the commutative square

\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{k=1}^{K}F(I_{k})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{k=1}^{K}F(J_{k})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{j=1}^{J}F(I_{j})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\bigotimes_{j=1}^{J}F(j)}

is Cartesian;

but such that
\displaystyle\eta^{*}(F)
satisfies both condition L and R. An element of this category is called a non-unital
commutative
factorization space.

Variant 10.7.2
.

The category
\displaystyle\textnormal{CommFactSpace}_{\textnormal{un}}
of unital commutative factorization spaces can be analogously defined.

[
Ras15
]
introduced a functor which attaches to every symmetric monoidal category a commutative factorization category. This can be written, in our notation, as

\textnormal{Loc}:\textnormal{CAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{CommFactCat}_{\textnormal{nu}}

\textnormal{Loc}:\textnormal{CAlg}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\textnormal{CommFactCat}_{\textnormal{un}}

A key feature is that the restriction of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Loc}(\mathsf{C})
to
\displaystyle X_{\textnormal{dR}}
is canonically isomorphic to
\displaystyle\mathsf{C}\tensor\textnormal{DMod}(X)
. The following is well-known (see
[
Ras16
, 8.10.1]

[
GL19a
, 5.6.4]
):

Proposition 10.7.3
.

For each
\displaystyle\mathsf{C}\in\textnormal{CAlg}(\textnormal{DGCat})
, the diagonal restriction upgrades to an equivalence

\textnormal{Fact}:\textnormal{CAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\mathsf{C}\tensor\textnormal{DMod}(X))\simeq\textnormal{CommFactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{Loc}(\mathsf{C})):\textnormal{res}

which further restricts to an equivalence of full subcategories

\textnormal{Fact}:\textnormal{CAlg}(\mathsf{C}\tensor\textnormal{DMod}(X))\simeq\textnormal{CommFactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{Loc}(\mathsf{C})):\textnormal{res}

In particular, being a unital
commutative
factorization algebra is not extra data.

Taking

then pushforward will then give rise to an equivalence of categories

\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\textnormal{Alg}}:\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}))\simeq\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}))

and, for every factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
on the configuration space, an equivalence of categories

\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{A}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}))\simeq\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\textnormal{Alg}}(A)\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0,\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}}))

\simeq\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\textnormal{Alg}}(A)\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}})),

which immediately follows from factorization. We likewise have a fully faithful embedding

\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}))\subseteq\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}))

whose essential image consisting of those unital factorization algebras whose underlying sheaf is suppported on the sublocus; for a fixed unital factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
that lies in the former, we have an equivalence of categories

A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0,\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}}))\simeq A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}})).

By pulling back along

[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}

we have a functor

\textnormal{Red}:\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}))\to\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}))

and for every unital factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
in the former, a functor

\textnormal{Red}_{A}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}}))\simeq A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0,\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}}))

\xrightarrow{!\textnormal{-pull}}\textnormal{Red}(A)\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},<0,\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}})).

Let us set
\displaystyle A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}:=(\textnormal{Conv}_{\textnormal{Conf}}^{\textnormal{Alg}})^{-1}\circ\textnormal{Red}(A)
, so that for every unital factorization algebra
\displaystyle A
that lies in
\displaystyle\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}},\leq 0}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{un},\textnormal{dR}}}))
, we have a well-defined functor
48
48

48

We note (without proving) that for
\displaystyle A\simeq\Omega^{\textnormal{Lus}}_{\textnormal{KM},\kappa}
, this is actually an equivalence of categories.

\textnormal{Red}_{\textnormal{Conf}}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{un}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}^{\omega^{\check{\rho}}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR},\overrightarrow{x}}}))\to A_{\textnormal{red},\textnormal{Conf}}\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}}(\textnormal{Conf}_{\infty\cdot\overrightarrow{x}})).

11
Appendix C: Ind-coherent Sheaves

Convention 11.0.1
.

In this chapter, all occurrences of
PreStk
and the term “prestack” should be understood as
convergent prestack
. For a prestack
\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}
to be convergent means that, for every affine
\displaystyle S
, we require the natural map

\mathcal{Y}(S)\to\limit_{n}\mathcal{Y}(\tau^{\leq n}(S))

(where
\displaystyle\tau^{\leq n}
denotes the Postnikov truncation of
\displaystyle S
) to be an isomorphism.

We note that being convergent is a condition that is satisfied by almost all “geometric” objects (e.g. all Artin stacks). In particular, all prestacks we consider in this paper are convergent.

11.1
Ind-coherent sheaves on qcqs schemes

In this subsection, we study the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on eventually coconnective qcqs schemes.

Definition 11.1.1
.

Following
[
Ras20a
,
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign
6.4]
, for
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{{\operatorname{qcqs}}}
, define
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
to be the full subcategory of bounded
almost perfect
object, i.e., those objects
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{+}
such that for any integer
\displaystyle N
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{\geq-N}
implies
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is a compact object in
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{\geq-N}
. Define

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S):=\operatorname{Ind}(\textnormal{Coh}(S)).

Let

\Psi:=\Psi_{S}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(S)

be the continuous functor obtained by ind-extending from
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
.

Remark 11.1.2
.

In
[
Ras20a
]
,
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is denoted by
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{*}(S)
.

Remark 11.1.3
.

In the above definition, we can replace “any integer
\displaystyle N
” by “any large enough integer
\displaystyle N
”.

Remark 11.1.4
.

It is easy to see
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)
is Karoubi complete, hence
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)
is the category of compact objects in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
.

Remark 11.1.5
.

It is easy to see
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
is closed under finite colimits. Hence
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is a cocomplete DG-category.

Remark 11.1.6
.

If
\displaystyle S
is almost finite type, i.e.,
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
(which is equivalent to
\displaystyle S\in\,^{\geq-m}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{ft}}
for some
\displaystyle m
), the above definition of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)
coincides with that in
[
Gai13
]
. Hence we write
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
in this case.

Construction 11.1.7
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
, there exists a compactly generated t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
such that
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\leq 0}
is generated under colimits and extensions by
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh(S)}\cap\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{\leq 0}
.

Remark 11.1.8
.

In particular, the above t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is right separated and compatible with filtered colimits.

Remark 11.1.9
.

In the above definition, we can replace “generated under colimits and extensions” by “generated under filtered colimits”.

Lemma 11.1.10
.

(
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 6.4.1]
)
For
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
, the functor
\displaystyle\Psi:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
is t-exact and induces an equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)^{+}\simeq\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{+}
.

Construction 11.1.11
.

For
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}

\displaystyle f_{*}:\textnormal{QCoh}(S)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(T)
is left t-exact. Consider the functor

\textnormal{Coh}(S)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(S)^{+}\xrightarrow{f_{*}}\textnormal{QCoh}(T)^{+}\xrightarrow{\Psi^{-1}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T)^{+}\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(T).

By ind-extending, we obtain a functor

The functor below was denoted by

in

f_{*}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)

and a commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

Warning 11.1.12

Lemma 11.1.13
.

For
\displaystyle f:S\to T

{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}

∎
