11.2
“Apaisant” schemes: when ind-coherent sheaves are well-behaved

Let
\displaystyle S
be any eventually coconnective qcqs scheme. One can show that
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)\subset\operatorname{QCoh}(S)
is closed under truncations if and only if
\displaystyle S
is
coherent
, i.e., locally of the form
\displaystyle\operatorname{Spec}(A)
such that
\displaystyle A
is (left)
coherent
(see
[
Lur12
, Definition 7.2.4.16]
). By the previous discussions, we want to restrict our study to locally coherent schemes. However, the notion of locally coherence is not preserved by standard geometric constructions
52
52

52

For example,
\displaystyle A
being coherent does not imply
\displaystyle A[t]
being coherent.
. Hence we want to restrict to a smaller class of schemes, which we call
apaisant schemes
53
53

53

The relation between apaisant schemes and coherent schemes is similar to that between finite type schemes and Noetherian schemes.
.

Definition 11.2.1
.

\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
is said to be
apaisant
, or
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
if it can be written as a (co)filtered limit
\displaystyle S=\lim_{i}S_{i}
under faithfully flat affine structure maps with
\displaystyle S_{i}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
.

Lemma 11.2.2
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 6.36.3]
)
Suppose
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
can be written as a filtered limit
\displaystyle S=\lim_{i}S_{i}
under flat affine structure maps with
\displaystyle S_{i}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. Then
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors induce an equivalence

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).

In particular,
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i}).

Warning 11.2.3
.

If we do not have finiteness assumption on
\displaystyle S_{i}
, the above lemma might be false. Under this additional assumption, the proof in
[
Ras20a
]
is correct.

Remark 11.2.4
.

In the definition of apaisant schemes, we required the connecting maps
\displaystyle S_{i}\to S_{j}
to be surjective. It is possible to develop the theory without it, but this requirement simplifies many discussions (e.g. the statement and proof of Lemma
11.2.12
below).

Remark 11.2.5
.

Let
\displaystyle\operatorname{Pro}^{\operatorname{aff,ff}}(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})
be the full subcategory of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Pro}(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})
containing those filtered systems connected by faithfully flat affine maps. Using Noetherian approximation (see
[
Lur18
,
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign
4.4]
), one can show the functor

\operatorname{Pro}^{\operatorname{aff,ff}}(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})\to\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}

obtained by right Kan extension along
{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}\to\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
is fully faithful. By definition, the image of this functor is
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Hence by Lemma
11.2.2
, the functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}
that encodes the
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors is the right Kan extension of
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}:\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}
.

Corollary 11.2.6
.

Suppose
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
is apaisant, then
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{QCoh}(S)
is closed under truncations.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
11.2.2
and the fact that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S_{i})
are closed under truncations.

∎

Remark 11.2.7
.

Let
\displaystyle S=\lim_{i}S_{i}
be an apaisant presentation. By Lemma
11.1.13
and Lemma
11.1.14
, the equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})
induces equivalences

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq 0}\xrightarrow{\simeq}\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})^{\geq 0},\;\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\leq 0}\xrightarrow{\simeq}\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})^{\leq 0}

Proposition 11.2.8
.

Let
\displaystyle S_{1}\to S
and
\displaystyle S_{2}\to S
be two open embeddings in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
such that
\displaystyle S_{1}\sqcup S_{2}\to S
is surjective. Then
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{2}).

(49)

Proof.

This functor has a right adjoint defined as follows. Let
\displaystyle u_{i}:S_{i}\to S
,
\displaystyle v_{i}:S_{1}\cap S_{2}\to S_{i}
and
\displaystyle v:S_{1}\cap S_{2}\to S
be the schematic open embeddings. For an object

(\mathcal{F}_{1},\mathcal{F}_{2},\mathcal{F}_{12},(v_{i})^{*}(\mathcal{F}_{i})\simeq\mathcal{F}_{12})\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{2}),

consider the object

(u_{1})_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{1})\times_{v_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{12})}(u_{2})_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{2})\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).

This defines a functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{2})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S),

which is right adjoint to (
49
). It remains to show these adjoint functors are inverse to each other. We need to check the following:

(i)

For any
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
, the morphism

\mathcal{F}\to(u_{1})_{*}\circ(u_{1})^{*}(\mathcal{F})\times_{v_{*}\circ(v)^{*}(\mathcal{F})}(u_{2})_{*}\circ(u_{2})^{*}(\mathcal{F})

is an equivalence.

(ii)

For any
\displaystyle(\mathcal{F}_{1},\mathcal{F}_{2},\mathcal{F}_{12},(v_{i})^{*}(\mathcal{F}_{i})\simeq\mathcal{F}_{12})
as before, the morphism

(u_{i})^{*}[(u_{1})_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{1})\times_{v_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{12})}(u_{2})_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{2})]\to\mathcal{F}_{i}

is an equivalence.

(ii) follows from the base-change isomorphisms. To prove (i), note that both sides commute with taking filtered colimits for
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
. Hence we can assume
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S)
. This allows us to replace
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
by
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}^{*}(S)
, where the claim is well-known.

∎

Corollary
11.2.6
implies
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on apaisant schemes is well-behaved. For example, we always have base-change isomorphisms. Note that the full subcategory
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{apsi}\subset\operatorname{Sch}
is not stable under fiber products. However, we have the following results.

Lemma 11.2.9
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp (i.e., almost of finite presentation) map in
{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
. If
\displaystyle T
is apaisant, then
\displaystyle S
is apaisant.

Proof.

Let
\displaystyle T=\lim_{i\in I^{\textnormal{op}}}T_{i}
be an apaisant presentation, where
\displaystyle I
is filtered. By assumption, there exists an integer
\displaystyle m
such that
\displaystyle S
,
\displaystyle T
and
\displaystyle T_{i}
are contained in
{}^{\geq-m}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{qcqs}}
. Note that
\displaystyle f:S\to T
is finitely
\displaystyle m
-presented (see
[
Lur18
, Definition 4.2.3.1]
). Hence by Noetherian approximation (see
[
Lur18
, Proposition 4.4.4.1]
), there exist an index
\displaystyle j
and a finitely
\displaystyle m
-presented map
\displaystyle S_{j}\to T_{j}
such that
\displaystyle S\simeq\tau^{>-m}(T\times_{T_{j}}S_{j})
. Since
\displaystyle T\to T_{j}
is flat, the truncation
\displaystyle\tau^{>-m}
is superfluous, i.e.,
\displaystyle S\simeq T\times_{T_{j}}S_{j}
. Now it is easy to see
\displaystyle S\simeq\lim_{i\in(I_{j/})^{\textnormal{op}}}(T_{i}\times_{T_{j}}S_{j})
is an apaisant presentation for
\displaystyle S
.

∎

Definition 11.2.10
.

A map
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}
is called
relatively apaisant
if it is qcqs, schematic, of Tor dimension
\displaystyle\leq n
for some integer
\displaystyle n
, and for any apaisant scheme
\displaystyle T^{\prime}
over
\displaystyle T
, the fiber product
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}
is apaisant.

Lemma 11.2.11
.

Suppose
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}
is qcqs, schematic, afp and of Tor dimensinon
\displaystyle\leq n
for some integer
\displaystyle n
. Then
\displaystyle f
is relatively apaisant.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
11.2.9
.

∎

Lemma 11.2.12
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}
. Suppose
\displaystyle S
can be written as a limit
\displaystyle S=\lim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}S_{n}
under faithfully flat affine afp structure maps with
\displaystyle S_{i}\to T
being relatively apaisant. Then
\displaystyle f
is relatively apaisant.

Proof.

We only need to show
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant scheme when each
\displaystyle S_{i}
is assumed to be an apaisant sheme. Let
\displaystyle S_{0}\simeq\lim_{\alpha\in J^{\textnormal{op}}}S_{0}^{\alpha}
be an apaisant presentation. As in the proof of Lemma
11.2.9
, using induction, there exists a chain
\displaystyle\alpha_{1}\to\alpha_{2}\to\cdots
in
\displaystyle J
and apaisant presentations
\displaystyle S_{n}\simeq\lim_{\alpha\in(J_{\alpha_{n}/})^{\textnormal{op}}}S_{n}^{\alpha}
such that
\displaystyle S_{n+1}^{\alpha}\simeq S_{n}^{\alpha}\times_{S_{n}^{\alpha_{n+1}}}S_{n+1}^{\alpha_{n+1}}
. Now it is easy to see
\displaystyle S\simeq\lim_{n\in\mathbb{N},\alpha\in(J_{\alpha_{n}/})^{\textnormal{op}}}S_{n}^{\alpha}
is an apaisant presentation for
\displaystyle S
.

∎

Example 11.2.13
.

Let
\displaystyle H=\lim_{n}H_{n}
be an apaisant presentation for an apaisant affine flat group scheme over a base
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. Then
\displaystyle B\to\mathbb{B}H
is relatively apaisant. Indeed, for any apaisant scheme
\displaystyle S
over
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}H
, we only need to show the corresponding
\displaystyle H
-torsor
\displaystyle P_{H}
over
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant scheme. Let
\displaystyle P_{H_{n}}
be the induced
\displaystyle H_{n}
-torsor, which is apaisant by Lemma
11.2.9
. Therefore
\displaystyle P_{H}\simeq\lim_{n}P_{H_{n}}
is apaisant by Lemma
11.2.12
.

Construction 11.2.14
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Choose an apaisant presentation
\displaystyle T=\lim_{i\in I^{\textnormal{op}}}T_{i}
. As in the proof of Lemma
11.2.9
, there exists an index
\displaystyle j
and
\displaystyle S_{j}\in(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{/T_{j}}
such that
\displaystyle S\simeq T\times_{T_{j}}S_{j}
, and
\displaystyle S\simeq\lim_{i\in(I_{j/})^{\textnormal{op}}}(T_{i}\times_{T_{j}}S_{j})
is an apaisant presentation for
\displaystyle S
. By Remark
11.2.5
, we have the following functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\simeq\lim_{i\in(I_{j/})^{\textnormal{op}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{j})\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\lim_{i\in(I_{j/})^{\textnormal{op}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{j})\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S),

where the middle functor is defined using the base-change isomorphisms between
\displaystyle!
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors (for the
IndCoh
-theory on
{}^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{ft}}
). Alternatively, it can be defined as

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i\in I_{j/}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{j})\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i\in I_{j/}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{j})\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S),

where the middle functor is defined using the commutativity between
\displaystyle!
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors (see
[
Gai13
, Proposition 7.1.6]
). Note that the obatined functor

f^{!}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)

does not depend on the choice of the apaisant presentation.

Construction 11.2.15
.

Let

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

be a Cartesian diagram contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
such that
\displaystyle f
is afp (hence so is
\displaystyle\varphi
). Then we have a canonical isomorphism (for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory):

\displaystyle\displaystyle\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\simeq f^{!}\circ g_{*}

induced via right Kan extensions from the similar isomorphisms for
IndCoh
-theory on aft schemes.

If
\displaystyle g
is further assumed to be of bounded Tor dimension (hence so is
\displaystyle\phi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\displaystyle\displaystyle\phi^{*}\circ f^{!}\to\varphi^{!}\circ g^{*}

induced by the above isomorphism is also an isomorphism.

Construction 11.2.16
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp open immersion in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, by
[
Lur18
, Corollary 4.6.2.2]
, the map
\displaystyle S_{j}\to T_{j}
in Contruction
11.2.14
can be chosen to be an open immersion. It follows that there is a canonical isomorphism
\displaystyle f^{!}\simeq f^{*}
.

Construction 11.2.17
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp proper map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Then the map
\displaystyle S_{j}\to T_{j}
in Contruction
11.2.14
is also proper (because
\displaystyle T\to T_{j}
is
faithfully
flat). It follows that there is a canonical adjoint pair
\displaystyle(f_{*}f^{!})
.

Lemma 11.2.18
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. The functor
\displaystyle f^{!}
is left t-exact up to a shift.

Proof.

Follows from Remark
11.2.7
and
[
Gai13
, Lemma 7.1.7]
.

∎

We also need the following sharper result:

Lemma 11.2.19
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Then there exists a natural number
\displaystyle n
such that for any Cartesian square

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the functor
\displaystyle[-n]\circ\varphi^{!}
is left t-exact.

Proof.

We can replace
\displaystyle S\to T
by
\displaystyle S_{j}\to T_{j}
in Contruction
11.2.14
. Hence we can assume
\displaystyle S,T\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. Similar, using Remark
11.2.7
, we can also assume
\displaystyle S^{\prime},T^{\prime}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. As in the proof of
[
Gai13
, Lemma 7.1.7]
54
54

54

Warning: the derived Nagata compactification, which this proof depends on, currently has a gap.
, we can reduce to the case when
\displaystyle f
is proper. Hence we only need to show
\displaystyle[n]\circ\varphi_{*}
is right t-exact, where
\displaystyle n
is an integer that depends only on
\displaystyle f
.

The remaining argument is standard . If
\displaystyle f
is affine, we can take
\displaystyle n:=0
.

If
\displaystyle f
is separated, we can find finite many open subschemes
\displaystyle\{S_{i}\}_{i\in I}
of
\displaystyle S
that covers
\displaystyle S
such that each composition
\displaystyle S_{i}\to S\to T
is affine. Note that for any
\displaystyle J\subset I
, the intersection
\displaystyle\cap_{j\in J}S_{j}
is affine over
\displaystyle T
(because
\displaystyle f
is separated). Then we can take
\displaystyle n:=|I|
.

For general map
\displaystyle f
, note that
\displaystyle f
is quasi-separated. We can find finite many open subschemes
\displaystyle\{S_{i}\}_{i\in I}
of
\displaystyle S
that covers
\displaystyle S
such that each composition
\displaystyle S_{i}\to S\to T
is separated. Note that for any
\displaystyle J\subset I
, the intersection
\displaystyle\cap_{j\in J}S_{j}
is separated over
\displaystyle T
(because
\displaystyle f
is quasi-separated). Let
\displaystyle n_{J}
be the natural number constructed in the last paragraph for the map
\displaystyle\cap_{j\in J}S_{j}\to T
. Then we can take
\displaystyle n:=|I|+\operatorname{max}_{J}\{n_{J}\}
.

∎

11.3
Ind-coherent sheaves on indschemes

In this subsection, we study the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on (apaisant) indschemes. However, we postpone the study of
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors to the next subsection.

Definition 11.3.1
.

A
convergent
prestack
\displaystyle S
is an
apaisant indscheme
, or
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, if it can be written as a filtered colimit
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}S_{i}
such that

•

\displaystyle S_{i}\in\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
,

•

\displaystyle S_{i}\to S_{j}
are afp closed embeddings.

Remark 11.3.2
.

Any apaisant indscheme is
reasonable
in the sense of
[
Ras20a
,
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign 6.8
]
.

Construction 11.3.3
.

We define

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

by left Kan extension along
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}\subset\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Explicitly, we have

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{i})\simeq\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{i})

Remark 11.3.4
.

Note that the
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{i})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{j})
sends
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S_{i})
into
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S_{j})
. In particular,
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is compactly generated by

\textnormal{Coh}(S):=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{Coh}(S_{i}),

where the colimit is taken in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Cat}
.

Remark 11.3.5
.

If
\displaystyle S
is locally almost finite type, i.e.,
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{laft}
, the obtained
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
coincides with
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
defined in
[
Gai13
]
. Hence we write
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
in this case.

Construction 11.3.6
.

By Lemma
11.1.14
, for
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}S_{i}\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, there exists a t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
such that

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq 0}\simeq\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{i})^{\geq 0}.

This t-structure does not depend on the choice of the presentation
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}S_{i}
.

It is not hard to show the above t-structure is compactly generated and

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\leq 0}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{i})^{\leq 0},

where the colimit is taken in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Pr}^{L}
.

Corollary 11.3.7
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
,
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is closed under truncations.

Proof.

Follows from Corollary
11.2.6
.

∎

Lemma 11.3.8
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 6.11.2]
)

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is coherent if and only if
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is bounded and almost perfect, i.e.,
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}
and for any integer
\displaystyle N
with
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq-N}
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is compact in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq-N}
.

Lemma 11.3.9
.

For
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the functor
\displaystyle f_{*}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)
is left t-exact. If
\displaystyle f
is a closed immersion
55
55

55

This means for some apaisant presentations
\displaystyle S=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\,}S_{i}
and
\displaystyle T=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\,}T_{j}
, and any index
\displaystyle i\in\mathcal{I}
, there exists
\displaystyle j\in\mathcal{J}
such that
\displaystyle S_{i}\to S\to T
factors through a closed immersion
\displaystyle S_{i}\to T_{j}
.
, then
\displaystyle f_{*}
is t-exact.

Proof.

If
\displaystyle f
is a closed immersion,
\displaystyle f_{*}
is right t-exact by definition. Hence it remains to prove the first claim.

Let
\displaystyle T=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}T_{i}
be an apaisant presentation. We first prove in the case
\displaystyle S=T_{j}
for some index
\displaystyle j
. We only need to show

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{j})\xrightarrow{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{i})

is left t-exact for any
\displaystyle i
. Since the
\displaystyle*
-pushforward and
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors along any
\displaystyle T_{i_{1}}\to T_{i_{2}}
is left t-exact, we only need to prove in the case
\displaystyle i=j
. Then the above composition is the filtered colimit of the following functors

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{j})\xrightarrow{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{k})\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{j}),

where the colimit is taken for all arrows
\displaystyle j\to k
. Then we are done because the t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{j})
is compatible with filtered colimits.

We then prove in the case when
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Note that
\displaystyle f:S\to T
factors through some
\displaystyle T_{i}
. This reduces the problem to the previous case.

Finally, for general
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, let
\displaystyle S=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}S_{\alpha}
be an apaisant presentation. Note that the identity functor on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is the filtered colimit of the following left t-exact functors

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{\alpha})\xrightarrow{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).

Hence the previous case (applied to each
\displaystyle S_{\alpha}\to T
) implies
\displaystyle f_{*}
is left t-exact.

∎

Lemma 11.3.10
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 6.16.1, Corollary 6.16.2]
)

Suppose
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
is relatively apaisant. Then:

•

\displaystyle f_{*}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)
has a right t-exact left adjoint
\displaystyle f^{*}
.

•

If
\displaystyle f
is of Tor dimension
\displaystyle\leq n
, then
\displaystyle[-n]\circ f^{*}
is left t-exact.

•

For a Cartesian diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, if
\displaystyle f
is relatively apaisant (hence so is
\displaystyle\varphi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation (for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory)

f^{*}\circ g_{*}\to\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{*}

is an isomorphism.

Proof.

When
\displaystyle f
is flat, the proof in
[
Ras20a
]
is correct when restricted to apaisant indschemes. The proof can be generalized to maps of bounded Tor dimensions.

∎

Lemma 11.3.11
.

Suppose
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{Sch}_{qcqs}
can be written as a filtered limit
\displaystyle S=\lim_{i\in I^{\textnormal{op}}}S_{i}
under faithful flat affine structure maps with
\displaystyle S_{i}
being finite type. Then
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant
indscheme
and
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors induce an equivalence

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).

In particular,
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i}).

Proof.

Note that
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\textnormal{op}}}\tau^{\geq-n}(S_{i})
. Therefore
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S)
is an apaisant scheme. Moreover, for
\displaystyle m\geq n
, the map
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S)\to\tau^{\geq-m}(S)
is an afp closed embedding because it is the base-change of a closed embedding
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S_{i})\to\tau^{\geq-m}(S_{i})
contained in
{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{ft}
. Hence
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n}\,}\tau^{\geq-n}(S)
is an apaisant indscheme. Now we have

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S_{i})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n,*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(\tau^{\geq-n}(S_{i}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n,*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(\tau^{\geq-n}(S_{i}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n,*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(\tau^{\geq-n}(S))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)

where the first equivalence is due to
[
Gai13
, Proposition 4.3.4]
, the second is due to the base-change isomorphisms, the third is by Lemma
11.2.2
, and the last is by definition.

∎

11.4
Ind-coherent sheaves on indschemes:
\displaystyle!
-pullbacks

In this subsection, we study the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-thoery on apaisant indschemes.

Definition 11.4.1
.

A map
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
is called
ind-afp
if for some apaisant presentations
\displaystyle S=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\,}S_{i}
and
\displaystyle T=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\,}T_{j}
, and any index
\displaystyle i\in\mathcal{I}
, there exists
\displaystyle j\in\mathcal{J}
such that
\displaystyle S_{i}\to S\to T
factors through an afp map
\displaystyle S_{i}\to T_{j}
.

We say
\displaystyle f:S\to T
is ind-afp and
ind-proper
(resp. an
ind-afp closed embedding
) if the above maps
\displaystyle S_{i}\to T_{j}
are afp and proper (resp. afp closed embeddings).

Remark 11.4.2
.

By
[
Ras20a
, Proposition 6.12.1]
(whose proof is correct for apaisant indschemes), we see that in the above definition, we can replace “some apaisant presentations” by “any apaisant presentations”.

Remark 11.4.3
.

A filtered colimit of apaisant indschemes connected by ind-afp closed embeddings is an apaisant indscheme.

Construction 11.4.4
.

Let
\displaystyle(\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{afp}}
(resp.
\displaystyle(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{ind-afp}}
) be the 1-full subcategory of
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
(resp.
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
) containing afp (resp. ind-afp) morphisms. Let

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:(\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{afp}}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

be the functor that encodes
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors for the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on apaisant schemes. By right Kan extension, we obtain a functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{ind-afp}}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

which encodes
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors for the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on apaisant indschemes. Note that for any apaisant indscheme
\displaystyle S
, the obtained category
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is equivalent to that in Construction
11.3.3
.

For any ind-proper map
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, we have a canonical adjoint pair
\displaystyle(f_{*},f^{!})
.

For any schematic open embedding map
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, we have a canonical adjoint pair
\displaystyle(f^{!},f_{*})
.

We are going to discuss the base-change isomorphisms between
\displaystyle!
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward (resp.
\displaystyle*
-pullback) functors. As a preparation, we have:

Lemma 11.4.5
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an ind-afp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
and
\displaystyle g:T^{\prime}\to T
be any map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Then the fiber product
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}
(in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{conv}}
) is an apaisant indscheme, and the map
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
is ind-afp.

If
\displaystyle f
is further assumed to be ind-proper (resp. an ind-afp closed embedding), then so is
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
.

Proof.

We first assume
\displaystyle S,T,T^{\prime}
are apaisant schemes. Let
\displaystyle S_{j}\to T_{j}
be as in the proof of Lemma
11.2.9
. Let
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\textnormal{op}}}T^{\prime}_{k}
be an apaisant presentation of
\displaystyle T^{\prime}
defined over
\displaystyle T_{j}
. Then
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\textnormal{op}}}S_{j}\times_{T_{j}}T^{\prime}_{k}
is an apaisant indscheme by Lemma
11.3.11
. Moreover, each map
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S\times_{T}T^{\prime})\to T^{\prime}
is afp (resp. afp and proper, an afp closed embedding) because it is the base-change of
\displaystyle\tau^{\geq-n}(S_{j}\times_{T_{j}}T^{\prime}_{k})\to T^{\prime}_{k}
.

Then we only assume
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T^{\prime}
are apaisant schemes. Let
\displaystyle T\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}T_{\alpha}
be as in the definition of apaisant indschemes. We can assume this filtered diagram has an initial object
\displaystyle T_{\alpha_{0}}
and the maps
\displaystyle S\to T
and
\displaystyle S\to T^{\prime}
factor through
\displaystyle T_{\alpha_{0}}
. By the previous case and Remark
11.4.3
, we only need to show
\displaystyle S\times_{T_{\alpha}}T^{\prime}\to S\times_{T_{\beta}}T^{\prime}
is an afp closed embedding. However, this follows from the fact that it is the base-change of
\displaystyle T_{\alpha}\to T_{\alpha}\times_{T_{\beta}}T_{\alpha}
, which is an afp closed embedding because the maps from both sides to
\displaystyle T_{\beta}
are afp.

Finally, the general case follows from Remark
11.4.3
.

∎

Lemma 11.4.6
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Lemma 6.17.1, Lemma 6.17.2]
)

Let

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

be a Cartesian diagram in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
such that
\displaystyle f
is ind-afp and ind-proper (hence so is
\displaystyle\varphi
). Then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\to f^{!}\circ g_{*}.

is an isomorphism. If moreover
\displaystyle g
is relatively apaisant (hence so is
\displaystyle\phi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi^{*}\circ f^{!}\to\varphi^{!}\circ g^{*}

obtained from the above isomorphism is also an isomorphism.

Proof.

We first assume
\displaystyle S,T,T^{\prime}
are apaisant schemes. Using Lemma
11.3.11
, as in the proof of Lemma
11.4.5
, the desired isomorphisms can be induced from the base-change isomorphisms for
IndCoh
-theory on
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{ft}
.

Then we only assume
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T^{\prime}
are apaisant schemes. Let
\displaystyle T\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}T_{\alpha}
be as in the definition of apaisant indschemes. We can assume this filtered diagram has an initial object
\displaystyle T_{\alpha_{0}}
and the maps
\displaystyle S\to T
and
\displaystyle S\to T^{\prime}
factor through
\displaystyle T_{\alpha_{0}}
. Consider the Cartesian diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}_{\alpha}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi_{\alpha}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi_{\alpha}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g_{\alpha}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f_{\alpha}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T_{\alpha}}

and the ind-afp closed embeddings
\displaystyle\iota_{\alpha}:T_{\alpha}\to T
and
\displaystyle\iota_{\alpha}^{\prime}:S_{\alpha}^{\prime}\to S
. We have

\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}\phi_{*}\circ(\iota_{\alpha}^{\prime})_{*}\circ(\iota_{\alpha}^{\prime})^{!}\circ\varphi^{!}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}\phi_{\alpha,*}\circ\varphi_{\alpha}^{!}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}f_{\alpha}^{!}\circ g_{\alpha,*}\simeq f^{!}\circ g_{*}.

(50)

In the general case, let
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}T^{\prime}_{\beta}
and
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}S_{\gamma}
be as in the definition of apaisant indschemes. Then the base-change isomorphisms between
\displaystyle!
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors for the Cartesian squares

\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{\gamma}\times_{T}T^{\prime}_{\beta}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}_{\beta}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{\gamma}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

imply the desired isomorphism
\displaystyle\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\to f^{!}\circ g_{*}
.

To prove
\displaystyle\phi^{*}\circ f^{!}\simeq\varphi^{!}\circ g^{*}
when
\displaystyle g
is assumed to be relatively apaisant, we can first reduce to the case when
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant scheme, then reduce to the case when
\displaystyle T
is an apaisant scheme (hence so is
\displaystyle T^{\prime}
), and finally using Noetherian approximation to reduce to the finite type case.

∎

Proposition 11.4.7
.

Let
\displaystyle S_{1}\to S
and
\displaystyle S_{2}\to S
be two schematic open embeddings in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
such that
\displaystyle S_{1}\sqcup S_{2}\to S
is surjective. Then
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{2}).

Proof.

Follows from Proposition
11.2.8
and Lemma
11.4.6
.

∎

Proposition 11.4.8
.

Let
\displaystyle f:T\to S
be a faithfully flat and relatively apaisant map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, then
\displaystyle*
-pullback induces an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}(\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)})).

Proof.

Follows from Proposition
11.1.21
and Lemma
11.4.6
.

∎

.

(C.f.

Remark 11.4.10
.

It is very possible that for any ind-afp map
\displaystyle f
, there are isomorphisms
\displaystyle\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\simeq f^{!}\circ g_{*}
and
\displaystyle\phi^{*}\circ f^{!}\simeq\varphi^{!}\circ g^{*}
and higher compatibilities for them. In fact, the proof of Lemma
11.4.6
can be generalized to all ind-afp map
\displaystyle f
as long as the isomorphisms
\displaystyle\phi_{\alpha,*}\circ\varphi_{\alpha}^{!}\simeq f_{\alpha}^{!}\circ g_{\alpha,*}
in (
50
) can be shown to be compatible with the colimits, which we do
not
know how to prove homotopy-coherently. However, for the purpose of this paper, we only need the following special case.

Definition 11.4.11
.

A morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
is
uniformly afp
, or
uafp
, if there exists a presentation
\displaystyle T=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}T_{i}
of
\displaystyle T
as an apaisant indscheme such that each
\displaystyle T_{i}\times_{T}S
is an apaisant
scheme
and each map
\displaystyle T_{i}\times_{T}S\to T_{i}
is afp.

Remark 11.4.12
.

By Lemma
11.2.9
,
\displaystyle f
is uafp iff

•

\displaystyle f:S\to T
is a schematic and afp morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{afp}}
;

•

there exists a presentation
\displaystyle T=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}T_{i}
of
\displaystyle T
as an apaisant indscheme such that each
\displaystyle T_{i}\times_{T}S
is eventually coconnective.

Remark 11.4.13
.

If
\displaystyle f
is uafp and ind-proper, then
\displaystyle f
is proper.

Remark 11.4.14
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a uafp morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{afp}}
, and
\displaystyle g:T^{\prime}\to T
be a relatively apaisant morphism. Then
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}
is an apaisant indscheme and
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
is uafp.

Warning 11.4.15
.

The composition of two uafp morphisms might
not
be uafp.

Construction 11.4.16
.

Let

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

be a Cartesian diagram in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
such that both
\displaystyle f
and
\displaystyle\varphi
are uafp. Then we have a canonical isomorphism (for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory):

\displaystyle\displaystyle\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{!}\simeq f^{!}\circ g_{*}

induced via left Kan extensions from the similar isomorphisms for apaisant schemes. In Remark
11.4.19
we will explain how to construct the higher compatibilities for these base-change isomoprhisms.

It follows from construction that:

•

if
\displaystyle f
is ind-proper (hence so is
\displaystyle\varphi
), then the above isomorphism can be identified with the Beck-Chevalley isomorphism in Lemma
11.4.6

•

if
\displaystyle g
is relatively apaisant (hence so is
\displaystyle\phi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi^{*}\circ f^{!}\to\varphi^{!}\circ g^{*}

obtained from the above isomorphism is also an isomorphism.

Lemma 11.4.17
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an afp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
. Then there exists a natural number
\displaystyle n
such that for any Cartesian square

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}

contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
with
\displaystyle\varphi
being uafp, the functor
\displaystyle[-n]\circ\varphi^{!}
is left t-exact.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
11.2.19
.

∎

The above right-lax symmetric monoidal structure means the following. For another similar diagram

there is a canonical functor, i.e., the

, from

11.5
Ind-coherent sheaves on renormalizable prestacks: definitions

In the following subsections, we study the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on nice enough prestacks such as the double quotient
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
.

Definition 11.5.1
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
,
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign
6.21-6.22]
) A convergent prestack
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{conv}}
is
weakly renormalizable
, or
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, if there exists a faithfully flat and relatively apaisant map
\displaystyle T\to S
with
\displaystyle T
being an apaisant indscheme. We refer such a map
\displaystyle T\to S
as an
flat apaisant cover
for
\displaystyle S
.

Example 11.5.2
.

The (fppf) double quotient
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
is a weakly renormalizable prestack.

Remark 11.5.3
.

Consider the category
\displaystyle\operatorname{Cov}(S)
of flat apaisant covers of
\displaystyle S
, where a morphism from a cover
\displaystyle S_{0}\to S
to
\displaystyle S_{0}^{\prime}\to S
is a faithfully flat and relatively apaisant map
\displaystyle S_{0}\to S_{0}^{\prime}
defined over
\displaystyle S
. Note that the fiber product of two flat apaisant covers is also a flat apaisant cover. Hence
\displaystyle\operatorname{Cov}(S)
is weakly contractible.

Definition 11.5.4
.

A map
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
is
apaisant indschematic
if for any relatively apaisant map
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\to T
with
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the fiber product
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}
is contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
.

Remark 11.5.5
.

If
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, then
\displaystyle f
is apaisant indschematic.

Remark 11.5.6
.

If
\displaystyle f
is relatively apaisant, then
\displaystyle f
is apaisant indschematic.

Remark 11.5.7
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an apaisant indschematic morphism and
\displaystyle g:T^{\prime}\to T
be a relatively apaisant morphism. Then
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}
is weakly renormalizable and
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
is apaisant indschematic.

Warning 11.5.8
.

We do
not
know if the class of apaisant indschematic maps is stable under general base-changes.

Construction 11.5.9
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Definition 6.24.1]
)

Recall we have a symmetric monoidal functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:\operatorname{Corr}(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{all,rel.apai}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

that encodes the
\displaystyle*
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors for the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on apaisant indschemes. Using right Kan extension along the fully faithful functor

\operatorname{Corr}(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{all,rel.apai}}\to\operatorname{Corr}(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})_{\operatorname{apai.indsch,rel.apai}},

we obtain a right-lax symmetric monoidal functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}:\operatorname{Corr}(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})_{\operatorname{apai.indsch,rel.apai}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}.

In other words, we extended the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory to weakly renormalizable prestacks such that

•

we have
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors along relatively apaisant morphisms,

•

we have
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors along apaisant indschematic morphisms,

•

we have base-change isomorphisms between the above
\displaystyle*
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors.

•

we have external tensor product functors compatible with the
\displaystyle*
-pullback and
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors.

By
[
GR17
, Chapter 8, Theorem 6.1.5]
, when restricted to horizontal morphisms, the obtained functor

[(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})_{\operatorname{rel.apai}}]^{\textnormal{op}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

is also the right Kan extension of the functor

[(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{rel.apai}}]^{\textnormal{op}}\to\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}}

that only encodes the
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors. In other words, for a weakly renormalizable prestack
\displaystyle S
, we have

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\simeq\lim_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(U),

where the limit is taken for all relatively apaisant morphisms
\displaystyle U\to S
with
\displaystyle U\in(\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}})_{\operatorname{rel.apai}}^{\textnormal{op}}
.

By construction, for any relatively apaisant morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, the functor
\displaystyle f^{*}
is left adjoint to
\displaystyle f_{*}
. Also, for a Cartesian diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, if
\displaystyle f
is relatively apaisant (hence so is
\displaystyle\varphi
) and
\displaystyle g
is apaisant indschematic (hence so is
\displaystyle\phi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

f^{*}\circ g_{*}\to\phi_{*}\circ\varphi^{*}

is an isomorphism.

Remark 11.5.10
.

When
\displaystyle S
is a QCA stack, by Theorem
11.6.1
below, the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
coincides with
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
defined in
[
DG13
]
. Hence we write
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
in this case.

Warning 11.5.11
.

For general
\displaystyle S
, the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is not as well-behaved as in the case when
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant indscheme. For instance, it is not compactly generated. Also, we do not have a
continuous

\displaystyle*
-pushforward functor along maps like
\displaystyle\mathbb{B}G(O)\to\operatorname{pt}
. We will use the
renormalization
precedure to obatin a more robust
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\operatorname{ren}}
-theory later.

Construction 11.5.12
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, there exists a unique t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
such that for any flat and relatively apaisant morphism
\displaystyle f:U\to S
with
\displaystyle U\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the functor
\displaystyle f^{*}
is t-exact. Equivalently, it is the unique t-exact such that for a given flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle f:U\to S
, the functor
\displaystyle f^{*}
is t-exact.

Remark 11.5.13
.

It is easy to see the above t-structure is compatible with filtered colimits and right separated.

Lemma 11.5.14
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an apaisant indschematic map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, then
\displaystyle f_{*}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)
is left t-exact. If
\displaystyle f
is further assumed to be relatively apaisant, then
\displaystyle f^{*}
is right t-exact, and is left t-exact up to a cohomological shift.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
11.3.9
and Lemma
11.3.10
.

∎

Lemma 11.5.15
.

Let
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T
be in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
. For
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq 0}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)^{\geq 0}
, the external tensor product
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}
is contained in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S\times T)
.

Proof.

By Construction
11.5.12
, Construction
11.3.6
and Remark
11.2.7
, we can reduce to the case when
\displaystyle S,T\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, and then reduce to a similar obvious claim about
\displaystyle\operatorname{QCoh}
.

∎

11.6
Ind-coherent sheaves on renormalizable prestacks: descent

In this subsection, we show that the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}
-theory on weakly renormalizable prestacks satisfies descents for flat apaisant covers.

Theorem 11.6.1
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Theorem 6.25.1]
)
Let
\displaystyle f:T\to S
be a relatively apaisant and faithfully flat map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, then
\displaystyle*
-pullback induces an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}(\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)})).

Proof.

The proof in
[
Ras20a
]
is correct as long as we replace
Step 1
of that proof by Proposition
11.4.8
. In general, under mild assumptions, a functor satisfying certain descents formally implies its right Kan extension satisfies similar descents. See Proposition
11.6.2
below for a precise statement.

∎

Proposition 11.6.2
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
be any category and
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}
be a full subcategory. Let (P) be a property on morphisms in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
that is stable under compositions and contains all isomorphisms. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{P}
(resp.
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{P}
) be the corresponding 1-full subcategory of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
(resp.
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
). Let (Q) be a property on morphisms in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
such that

(a)

it is stronger than (P), i.e., any (Q)-morphism is a (P)-morphism,

(b)

it is stable under compositions and contains all isomorphisms,

(c)

it is stable under base-changes, i.e., if
\displaystyle T\to S
is a (Q)-morphism and
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
is any morphism, then the fiber prodcut
\displaystyle T\times_{S}S^{\prime}
is well-defined in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
and
\displaystyle T\times_{S}S^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}
is a (Q)-morphism,

(d)

if
\displaystyle T\to S
is a (Q)-morphism and
\displaystyle S
is contained in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, then so is
\displaystyle T
,

(e)

if
\displaystyle T\to S
is a (P)-morphism with
\displaystyle T\in\mathcal{C}
and
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
is a (Q)-morphism in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
, then the fiber prodcut
\displaystyle T\times_{S}S^{\prime}
is well-defined in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
and
\displaystyle T\times_{S}S^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}
is a (P)-morphism,

(f)

for any
\displaystyle S\in\mathcal{D}
, there is a (Q)-morphism
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
with
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}
.

Now suppose
\displaystyle I:\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\mathcal{E}
is any functor satisfying (Q)-descent, i.e., such that for any (Q)-morphism
\displaystyle T\to S
in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, the canonical morphism
62
62

62

The fiber product
\displaystyle T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}
is taken in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
. By assumption (d), it is actually contained in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
. However, it is
not
the fiber product in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{P}
or
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{Q}
.

I(S)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}(I(T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}))

is an isomorphism. Suppose the right Kan extension
\displaystyle\operatorname{RKE}(I):\mathcal{D}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\mathcal{E}
of
\displaystyle I
along
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}}\to\mathcal{D}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}}
exists. Then
\displaystyle\operatorname{RKE}(I)
also satisfies (Q)-descent.

Proof.

Our argument is essentially borrowed from
Step 2
of the proof of
[
Ras20a
, Theorem 6.25.1]
.

We abuse notation by writing
\displaystyle I
for
\displaystyle\operatorname{RKE}(I)
. For any (Q)-morphism
\displaystyle T\to S
in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
, we need to prove

F:I(S)\to\lim_{[m]\in\Delta_{inj}}I(T^{\times_{S}(m+1)})

is an isomorphism. By (b) and (c), the semi-cosimplicial diagram
\displaystyle T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}
is contained in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{Q}
. Recall

I(S)\simeq\lim J,

where
\displaystyle J:(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/}\to\mathcal{E}
sends a (P)-morphisms
\displaystyle U\to S
to
\displaystyle I(U)
.

We first prove in the case when
\displaystyle T\in\mathcal{C}
. By assumption (d), the semi-cosimplicial diagram
\displaystyle T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}
is contained in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{Q}
. Hence by assumption (e), we have canonical functors

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{B}:(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/}\times\Delta_{inj}\to(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/},

\displaystyle\displaystyle(U,[m])\mapsto U\times_{S}T^{\times_{S}(m+1)},

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{T}:\Delta_{inj}\to(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/},

\displaystyle\displaystyle[m]\mapsto T^{\times_{S}(m+1)},

and natural transformations
\displaystyle\alpha:\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{2}\to\mathbf{B}
,
\displaystyle\beta:\operatorname{pr}_{1}\to\mathbf{B}
. Note that the morphism
\displaystyle F
can be identified with the canonical morphism

\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}}:\lim J\to\lim J\circ\mathbf{T}

induced by restricting the limit diagrams along the functor
\displaystyle\mathbf{T}
. Since
\displaystyle I
satisfies (Q)-descent on
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, for any
\displaystyle U\in(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/}
, we have

J(U)\simeq\lim_{[m]\in\Delta_{inj}}J(\mathbf{B}(U,[m])).

(52)

Hence an isomorphism

\lim J\to\lim J\circ\mathbf{B}.

(53)

Consider the following composition

\displaystyle\displaystyle G:\lim_{[m]\in\Delta_{inj}}J\circ\mathbf{T}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim J\circ\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{2}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim J\circ\mathbf{B}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim J,

where

•

the first morphism is restricting the limit diagrams along
\displaystyle\operatorname{pr}_{2}:(\mathcal{C}_{P}^{\textnormal{op}})_{S/}\times\Delta_{inj}\to\Delta_{inj}
,

•

the second morphism is induced by the natural transformation
\displaystyle\alpha:\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{2}\to\mathbf{B}
,

•

the third morphism is the inverse of (
53
).

We claim
\displaystyle F
and
\displaystyle G
are inverse to each other, and in particular, they are isomorphism. Note that

\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}\circ F\simeq\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}}\simeq\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{2}}\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{B}}.

Also note that (
53
) is just
\displaystyle\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\beta)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{1}}
, which is also isomorphic to
\displaystyle\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{B}}
. Combining these, we get
\displaystyle G\circ F\simeq\operatorname{Id}
. Now we show
\displaystyle F\circ G\simeq\operatorname{Id}
. By above, we have

F\circ G\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}}\circ\res_{\mathbf{B}}^{-1}\circ\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}.

Note that (
52
) also induces an isomorphism

J\circ\mathbf{T}([n])\simeq\lim_{[m]\in\Delta_{inj}}J(\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{T}([n]),[m])),

hence an isomorphism

\lim J\circ\mathbf{T}\to\lim J\circ\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{join}

(54)

where

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{join}:\Delta_{inj}\times\Delta_{inj}\to\Delta_{inj},

\displaystyle\displaystyle([n],[m])\mapsto[m+n+1]

is the concatenation functor, and we are using the fact

\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{join}\simeq\mathbf{B}\circ(\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}).

As before, we can show (
54
) is equivalent to
\displaystyle\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}
.

Hence

\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}}\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}\circ\res_{\mathbf{B}}

and therefore

\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}}\circ\res_{\mathbf{B}}^{-1}\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}^{-1}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}.

Hence

F\circ G\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}^{-1}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}\circ\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha)\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}^{-1}\circ\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha\bigstar\mathbf{Id}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}})\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}.

Note that
\displaystyle\operatorname{pr}_{2}\circ(\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id})
is the second projection map

p_{2}:\Delta_{inj}\times\Delta_{inj}\to\Delta_{inj},

and the natural transformation

\alpha\star\mathbf{Id}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}:\mathbf{T}\circ p_{2}\to\mathbf{T}\circ\operatorname{join}

is induced by a natural transformation
\displaystyle\beta:p_{2}\to\operatorname{join}
. Hence

\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J}\bigstar\alpha\bigstar\mathbf{Id}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}})\circ\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf{T}\times\mathbf{Id}}\circ\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{pr}_{2}}\simeq\lim(\mathbf{Id}_{J\circ\mathbf{T}}\bigstar\beta)\circ\operatorname{res}_{p_{2}}\simeq\operatorname{res}_{\operatorname{join}}.

This shows
\displaystyle F\circ G\simeq\operatorname{Id}
and finishes the proof in the case
\displaystyle T\in\mathcal{C}
.

For the general case, let
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
be as in assumption (f). We have already proved
\displaystyle I
satisfies descent along
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
,
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\times_{S}T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}\to T^{\times_{S}(\bullet+1)}
and
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\times_{S}T\to S^{\prime}
. These formally imply
\displaystyle I
satisfies descent along
\displaystyle T\to S
.

∎

Proposition 11.6.3
.

Let
\displaystyle S_{1}\to S
and
\displaystyle S_{2}\to S
be two schematic open embeddings in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
such that
\displaystyle S_{1}\sqcup S_{2}\to S
is surjective. Then
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{2}).

Proof.

Follows from Proposition
11.4.7
and Theorem
11.6.1
.

∎

The statement (2) follows from construction.

The proof of (3) is again similar to that of (iii). Namely, we want to show certain filtered colimits commute with certain semi-totalizations in

Definition 11.7.2

A map

-pullable.

11.8
Ind-coherent sheaves on renormalizable prestacks:

Definition 11.8.1
.

An apaisant indschematic morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
is
uafp
if for any relatively apaisant map
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\to T
with
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\in\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the map
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
is a uafp morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
.

A uafp morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
is
proper
(resp. a
closed immersion
) if the uafp map
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
as above is proper (resp. a closed immersion)
65
65

65

Recall that a uafp map in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
is schematic. Hence the notion of proper maps (resp. closed immersions) is well-defined.
.

Remark 11.8.2
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a uafp morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, and
\displaystyle g:T^{\prime}\to T
be a relatively apaisant morphism. Then by Remark
11.4.14
,
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
is uafp.

Warning 11.8.3
.

The composition of two uafp morphisms might
not
be uafp.

Construction 11.8.4
.

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a uafp morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
. For any flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle T_{0}\in\operatorname{Cov}(T)

. Let
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}
and
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}

\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\to T_{\bullet}

\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}

, the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors induce a functor

\displaystyle T_{0}
, i.e., we have a functor
\displaystyle\operatorname{Cov}(T)^{\textnormal{op}}\to\operatorname{Arrow}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}})

to the above arrow in

and Remark

It follows from contruction that:

•

If
\displaystyle f
is proper, we have a canonical adjoint pair
\displaystyle(f_{*},f^{!})
.

•

If
\displaystyle f
is an open immersion, we have a canonical adjoint pair
\displaystyle(f^{!},f_{*})
.

•

The bi-simplicial symmetric monoidal functor

in Remark
11.4.19
can be extended to a right-lax symmetric monoidal functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(-):\operatorname{Cart}^{m,n}_{\operatorname{apai.indsch,uafp}}(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})\to\operatorname{Funct}([m]^{\textnormal{op}}\times[n],\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}})

satisfying similar properties.

Now we restrict to those
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors that send bounded-below objects to bounded-below ones.

Let

\displaystyle\phi
), the Bech-Chevalley natural transformation

(\phi^{*})^{+}\circ(f^{!})^{+}\to(\varphi^{!})^{+}\circ(g^{*})^{+}

obtained from the above isomorphism is also an isomorphism.

Proof.

The first claim can be proved by using the same trick as in the proof of Proposition
11.7.1
. To prove the second claim, we can use Theorem
11.6.1
to reduce to the case when
\displaystyle g
is relatively apaisant, which has already been treated in Construction
11.8.4
.

∎

Construction 11.8.8
.

By Lemma
11.8.7
and Remark
11.4.19
, we have a bi-simplicial right-lax symmetric monoidal functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(-)^{+}:\operatorname{Cart}^{m,n}_{\operatorname{all,vafp}}(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})\to\operatorname{Funct}([m]^{\textnormal{op}}\times[n],\operatorname{Vect}^{+}\operatorname{-mod})

that encodes all the previous constructions. Namely, for a diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{0,0}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{1,0}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\cdots\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{m,0}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{0,1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{1,1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\cdots\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S_{m,1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}

where all the squares are Cartesian and all the horizontal maps are vafp, it is sent to

where all horizontal functors are
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors and all vertical functors are
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functors. Moreover, if each

is
