-pullable, then all the squares in the above diagram are left adjointable along the vertical direction.

11.9
Renormalization

Construction 11.9.1
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, let
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
be the full subcategory of objects
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
such that its
\displaystyle*
-pullback along any flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
is contained in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S^{\prime})\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\prime})
.

Remark 11.9.2
.

By Lemma
11.3.8
,
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{b}
.

Lemma 11.9.3
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
, the following are equivalent:

(i)

\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S)
;

(ii)

there exists a flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
such that the
\displaystyle*
-pullback of
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is contained in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S^{\prime})\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\prime})
;

(iii)

for any
\displaystyle*
-pullable morphism
\displaystyle T\to S
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, the
\displaystyle*
-pullback of
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is contained in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(T)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)
.

Proof.

Follows from Lemma
11.4.9
.

∎

Lemma 11.9.4
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
,
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)
is contained in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}
and is closed under truncations.

Proof.

Follows from Corollary
11.3.7
.

∎

Construction 11.9.5
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, define

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Coh}(S)).

There is an obvious functor
\displaystyle{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{*}(S)
defined by ind-extending.

Remark 11.9.6
.

When
\displaystyle S
is an apaisant indscheme, recall that
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is compactly generated by
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)
. Hence
\displaystyle{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{*}(S)
is an equivalence. Therefore we omit the subscript
ren
in this case.

Remark 11.9.7
.

When
\displaystyle S
is a QCA stack, via the identification in Remark
11.5.10
, the subcategory
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)
coincides with the same-named category in
[
DG13
]
. Hence by
[
DG13
, Theorem 3.3.5]
, the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
coincides with
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
. Hence we write
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)
for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
in this case.

Remark 11.9.8
.

It is easy to see
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is Karoubi complete and closed under finite colimits, hence
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)^{c}\simeq\textnormal{Coh}(S)
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
is a cocomplete DG-category.

Construction 11.9.9
.

There exists a compactly generated t-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
such that
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)^{\leq 0}
is generated under colimits and extensions by
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh(S)}\cap\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\leq 0}
.

Proposition 11.9.10
.

(C.f.
[
Ras20a
, Proposition 6.28.5]
) For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, the functor
\displaystyle\operatorname{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is t-exact and induces an equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)^{+}\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}
.

Proof.

If
\displaystyle S
is
renormalizable
, i.e., it has a flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle S^{\prime}\to S
that is laft, the proof in
[
Ras20a
]
is correct (after adding the word “apaisant” at suitable places). However, the proof there only uses the
laft
assumption on
\displaystyle S^{\prime}
to guarantee
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)
is closed under truncations, which we have already proved in Lemma
11.9.4
.

∎

Construction 11.9.11
.

For any morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{{\operatorname{w.ren}}}
, the left t-exact functor
\displaystyle(f_{*})^{+}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)^{+}
induces the following functor:

\textnormal{Coh}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)^{+}\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)^{+}\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)

By ind-extending, we obtain the
renormalized
\displaystyle*
-pushforward
functor

f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T).

Since
\displaystyle\textnormal{Coh}(S)\subset\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
is closed under truncations, the functor
\displaystyle f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
is left t-exact. Since the retriction of
\displaystyle f_{*}^{+}
on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{\geq 0}
preserves filtered colimits, we have a commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)^{+}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(f_{*,\textnormal{ren}})^{+}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)^{+}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{(f_{*})^{+}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)^{+}.}

Also, if
\displaystyle f
is apaisant indschematic, then the above commutative diagram can be extended to the unbounded categories.

Construction 11.9.12
.

Similarly, we can use the above
renormalization
procedure to construct the
renormalized
\displaystyle*
-pullback functors
(along any
\displaystyle*
-pullback morphisms) and the
renormalized
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors
(along any vafp morphisms). By Construction
11.8.8
, these functors can be encoded a bi-simplicial right-lax symmetric monoidal functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(-):\operatorname{Cart}^{m,n}_{\operatorname{all,vafp}}(\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}})\to\operatorname{Funct}([m]^{\textnormal{op}}\times[n],\operatorname{DGCat}_{\operatorname{cont}})

satisfying similar properties as in Construction
11.8.8
.

Warning 11.9.13
.

The
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
-theory does
not
satisfy flat descent. For example, the
\displaystyle*
-pullback functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(G(O))\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\operatorname{pt})
is not conservative.

Proposition 11.9.14
.

Let
\displaystyle S_{1}\to S
and
\displaystyle S_{2}\to S
be two schematic open embeddings in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
such that
\displaystyle S_{1}\sqcup S_{2}\to S
is surjective. Then
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks induce an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1})\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1}\cap S_{2})}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{2}).

Proof.

The proof is similar to that of Proposition
11.2.8
. Using the notations of that proof, we only need to check

(i)

For any
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
, the morphism

\mathcal{F}\to(u_{1})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ(u_{1})^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F})\times_{v_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ(v)^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F})}(u_{2})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ(u_{2})^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F})

is an equivalence.

(ii)

For any
\displaystyle(\mathcal{F}_{1},\mathcal{F}_{2},\mathcal{F}_{12},(v_{i})^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}_{i})\simeq\mathcal{F}_{12})
as before, the morphism

(u_{i})^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}[(u_{1})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}_{1})\times_{v_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}_{12})}(u_{2})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}_{2})]\to\mathcal{F}_{i}

is an equivalence.

As before, (ii) follows from the base-change isomorphisms. To prove (i), we can reduce to the case when
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{Coh}(S)
. Then the claim follows from Proposition
11.6.3
.

∎

Proposition 11.9.15
.

For any
\displaystyle S,T\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, the external product functor

-\boxtimes-:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S\times T)

is fully faithful and preserves compact objects. If
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T
are apaisant indschemes, it is an equivalence.

Proof.

When
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T
are apaisant indschemes, there is nothing new to prove (see the last paragraph of Remark
11.4.19
).

In the general case, we first show the external product functor sends compact objects to compact objects. Recall
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)
is compactly generated by the image of

\operatorname{Coh}(S)\times\operatorname{Coh}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\times\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T).

(56)

Hence we only need to show

\operatorname{Coh}(S)\times\operatorname{Coh}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\times\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S\times T)

factors through
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S\times T)
. Using Lemma
11.9.3
, we can reduce to the case when
\displaystyle S
and
\displaystyle T
are apaisant indschemes. Then the claim is obvious because

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S\times T)

is an equivalence hence sends compact objects to compact objects.

We then show the external product functor is fully faithful. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{i}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S)
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}^{i}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T)
. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}^{i}
be the image of
\displaystyle(\mathcal{F}^{i},\mathcal{G}^{i})
under (
56
). Recall we have

\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{M}^{1},\mathcal{M}^{2})\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}^{1},\mathcal{F}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}^{1},\mathcal{G}^{2}),

where
\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(-,-)\in\operatorname{Vect}
is the
mapping object
. Hence we only need to show

\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}^{1},\mathcal{F}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}^{1},\mathcal{G}^{2})\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}^{1}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}^{1},\mathcal{F}^{2}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}^{2})

is an equivalence. Let
\displaystyle S_{0}\to S
and
\displaystyle T_{0}\to T
be flat apaisant covers. Consider the Cech nerves
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\to S
and
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}\to T
. Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{i}_{\bullet}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S_{\bullet})
be the
\displaystyle*
-pullback of
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{i}
, and similarly define
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}^{i}_{\bullet}
. By Theorem
11.6.1
, the above morphism is equivalent to the following composition:

\displaystyle\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}^{1},\mathcal{F}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}^{1},\mathcal{G}^{2})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\underset{m}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{m}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{m}^{2})]\otimes\underset{n}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{n}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{n}^{2})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\underset{m}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\underset{n}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{m}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{m}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{n}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{n}^{2})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{2})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{1}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{2}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{2})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}^{1}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}^{1},\mathcal{F}^{2}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}^{2}).

Note that each

\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{2})\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{1}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{2}\boxtimes\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{2})

is an isomorphism because
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}
and
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}
are apaisant indschemes. Hence we only need to show

\underset{m}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{m}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{m}^{2})]\otimes\underset{n}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{n}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{n}^{2})]\to\underset{m}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\underset{n}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}[\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_{m}^{1},\mathcal{F}_{m}^{2})\otimes\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{G}_{n}^{1},\mathcal{G}_{n}^{2})]

is an isomorphism. By Remark
11.9.2
, we can assume
\displaystyle F^{i},G^{i}
are concentrated in degrees
\displaystyle[0,d]
for some integer
\displaystyle d
, and so are
\displaystyle F^{i}_{\bullet},G^{i}_{\bullet}
. Hence each
\displaystyle\operatorname{Hom}(-,-)
as above is contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Vect}^{\geq-d}
. Therefore we only need to show the above morphism induces isomorphisms on
\displaystyle H^{j}
for
\displaystyle j\geq-2d
. For each fixed
\displaystyle j
, we can replace the semi-totalization by a truncated one. Then we are done because tensor products in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Vect}
commutes with finite limits.

∎

So far we only allow
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors along vafp morphisms, which does not include
ind
-proper morphisms. These functors can be supplied easily as follows.

Definition 11.9.16
.

A morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
is
ind-afp and ind-proper
(resp.
an ind-afp closed immersion
) if there exists a flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle T_{0}\in\operatorname{Cov}(T)
such that
\displaystyle S\times_{T}T_{0}\to T_{0}
is an ind-afp and ind-proper map (resp. an ind-afp closed immersion) in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
.

An ind-afp and ind-proper morphism
\displaystyle f:S\to T
is
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable
if
\displaystyle f_{*}
is left t-exact up to a shift (hence so is
\displaystyle f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
).

Remark 11.9.17
.

We do
not
require ind-afp and ind-proper map to be apaisant indschematic.

Lemma 11.9.18
.

(1)

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be an ind-afp and ind-proper morphism in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, then the functor
\displaystyle f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
has a
continuous
right adjoints.

(2)

Let
\displaystyle f:S\to T
be a
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable map. Then the right adjoints
\displaystyle f^{?}
and
\displaystyle f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}
of
\displaystyle f_{*}
and
\displaystyle f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
are left t-exact up to shifts, and
\displaystyle f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}
can be obtained from
\displaystyle f^{?}
via renormalization. I.e., it can be identified with the ind-extension of

\operatorname{Coh}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)^{+}\xrightarrow{f^{?}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)^{+}\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)^{+}\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)

such that we have a canonical commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}}
ren
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
ren
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f^{?}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).}

(3)

Let

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\varphi}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\phi}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\textstyle{S\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T}

be a Cartesian diagram in
\displaystyle\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
such that
\displaystyle f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}
and
\displaystyle\varphi^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}
are well-defined. Then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ\varphi^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\to f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ g_{*,\textnormal{ren}}.

is an isomorphism. If
\displaystyle g
is
\displaystyle*
-pullable (hence so is
\displaystyle\phi
), then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\to\varphi^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ g^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}.

is also an isomorphism. If
\displaystyle g
and
\displaystyle\phi
are vafp, then the Beck-Chevalley natural transformation

\phi^{!}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ f^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\to\varphi^{?}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ g^{!}_{\textnormal{ren}}

is also an equivalence.

Proof.

To prove (1), we only need to show
\displaystyle(f_{*})^{+}
sends
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(S)
to
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T)
, which follows from Lemma
11.4.9
.

Note that
\displaystyle S_{0}:S\times_{T}T_{0}
is a flat apaisant cover of
\displaystyle S
. Let
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}\to T
and
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\to S
be the Cech nerves. By Theorem
11.6.1
and the base-change isomorphisms,
\displaystyle f_{*}
can be identified with

\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{\bullet})\xrightarrow{*\operatorname{-push}}\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{\bullet}).

By Lemma
11.4.6
, this functor has a continuous right adjoint

\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{\bullet})\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{\bullet}).

This proves the existence of
\displaystyle f^{?}
. The remaining claims of (2) follows from definitions.

(3) can be deduced from the non-renormalized version.

∎

Remark 11.9.19
.

Using Proposition
11.10.1
below, Lemma
11.9.18
(3) can be generalized to the case when
\displaystyle S
can be written as a nice enough filtered colimit
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}S_{\alpha}
such that
\displaystyle S_{\alpha}\to T
and
\displaystyle S_{\alpha}\times_{S}T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}
are
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable. For example, this means for the map
\displaystyle f:\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G\to\operatorname{pt}/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
, the right adjoint of
\displaystyle f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
is well-behaved although it can
not
be obtained via a renormalization procedure. However, for the purpose of this paper, Lemma
11.9.18
(3) is enough (because we use the
forma
stack
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\widehat{\mathcal{L}G}/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
instead of the
ind
-stack
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
).

Variant 11.9.20
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
is compactly generated hence dualizable. We define

\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S):=\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)^{\vee}\simeq\operatorname{Ind}(\operatorname{Coh}(S)^{\textnormal{op}}).

For
\displaystyle f:S\to T
, we define the following functors:

•

The
renormalized
\displaystyle!
-pullback functor for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}
-theory

f^{!,\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S)

is defined as the dual of

f_{*,\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T).

•

When
\displaystyle f
is
\displaystyle*
-pullable, the
renormalized
\displaystyle?
-pushforward functor for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}
-theory

f_{?}^{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(T),

is defined as the dual of

f_{\textnormal{ren}}^{*}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S),

or equivalently as the
continuous
right adjoint of
\displaystyle f^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
.

We use
\displaystyle?
-pushable
as a synonym for
\displaystyle*
-pullable
.

•

When
\displaystyle f
is vafp, the
renormalized
\displaystyle*
-pushforward functor for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}
-theory

f_{*}^{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(T)

is defined as the dual of

f_{\textnormal{ren}}^{!}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S).

•

When
\displaystyle f
is
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable, the
renormalized
\displaystyle!
-pushforward functor for
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!}
-theory

f_{!}^{\textnormal{ren}}:\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(T),

is defined as the dual of

f_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}:\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S),

or equivalently as the left adjoint of
\displaystyle f^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
.

We use
\displaystyle(!,\textnormal{ren})
-pushable
as a synonym for
\displaystyle(?,\textnormal{ren})
-pullable.

For
\displaystyle S_{1},S_{2}
such that the external tensor product functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1})\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{2})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1}\times S_{2})

is an equivalence, we also have an equivalence

\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1})\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{2})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S_{1}\times S_{2})

obtained by taking conjugation.

Notation 11.9.21
.

For
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
, let

\omega_{S}\in\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(S)

be the image of the unit object in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(\operatorname{pt})\simeq\operatorname{Vect}
under the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functor. We often omit the subscript
\displaystyle S
from
\displaystyle\omega_{S}
if there is no danger of ambiguity.

11.10
Ind-coherent sheaves on quotient stacks

In this subsection, we compare Raskin’s definition of
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)
with the definition sketched in
[
Gai14
]
for quotient prestacks such as
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G
.

Proposition 11.10.1
.

Suppose
\displaystyle S\in\operatorname{PreStk}_{\operatorname{w.ren}}
can be written as a filtered colimit
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha\in I}\,}S^{\alpha}
such that:

•

The connecting maps
\displaystyle\iota_{\alpha\to\beta}:S^{\alpha}\to S^{\beta}
and
\displaystyle\iota_{\alpha}:S^{\alpha}\to S
are apaisant indschematic;

•

There exists a flat apaisant cover
\displaystyle S_{0}\to S
such that the map
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}\times_{S}S_{0}\to S^{\beta}\times_{S}S_{0}
is an ind-afp closed immersion in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
.

Then the functors

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)

are equivalences.

Proof.

Let
\displaystyle S_{0}^{\alpha}:=S^{\alpha}\times_{S}S_{0}
. Note that
\displaystyle S_{0}^{\alpha}\to S^{\alpha}
is also an apaisant cover. Let
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\to S
be the Cech nerve for
\displaystyle S_{0}\to S
and
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}^{\alpha}\to S^{\alpha}
be defined similarly. Note that we also have
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}S_{\bullet}^{\alpha}
. By assumption, each
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}_{0}\to S_{0}
is ind-afp and ind-proper. Hence
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}_{0}\to S^{\beta}_{0}
and the base-changes
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}_{\bullet}\to S_{\bullet}
,
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}_{\bullet}\to S^{\beta}_{\bullet}
are also ind-afp and ind-proper (Lemma
11.4.5
).

We first prove the non-renormalized version. Using the base-change isomorphisms and Theorem
11.6.1
, we have the following commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S_{\bullet})}

Since
\displaystyle S_{\bullet}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}S_{\bullet}^{\alpha}
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{IndSch}_{\operatorname{apai}}
, the right vertical functor is an equivalence. Hence it remains to show

\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet})\to\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet})

is an equivalence. By Lemma
11.4.6
, this functor is equivalent to

\underset{!\operatorname{-pull}}{\lim}\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet})\to\underset{*\operatorname{-pull}}{\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}}\underset{!\operatorname{-pull}}{\lim}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha}_{\bullet}),

which is an equivalence because taking limits commute with taking limits.

Now we prove the renormalized version. We first show the functor is fully faithful. By Lemma
11.9.18
(1),
\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})
is compactly generated by the images of

\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha,\textnormal{ren}}:\operatorname{Coh}(S^{\alpha})\to\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})

and the functor

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)

preserves compact objects. Hence we only need to show for fixed
\displaystyle\alpha
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S^{\alpha})
, the morphism

\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}),\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{G}))\to\operatorname{Maps}((\iota_{\alpha})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}),(\iota_{\alpha})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{G}))

is an isomorphism. Note that we have a commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
ren
\displaystyle\textstyle{\underset{*\operatorname{-push}}{\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
ren
\displaystyle\textstyle{\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S)}

which induces

\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}),\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{G}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Maps}(\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{F}),\operatorname{ins}_{\alpha}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{G}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\simeq}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Maps}((\iota_{\alpha})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}),(\iota_{\alpha})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{G}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Maps}((\iota_{\alpha})_{*}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{F}),(\iota_{\alpha})_{*}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{G})).}

By definition, the bottom morphism is an isomorphism. Hence we only need to show the top morphism is an isomorphism. By Lemma
11.3.9
, the functor
\displaystyle(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{*}
is t-exact. Hence by Lemma
11.9.18
, the t-exact connecting functors
\displaystyle(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
and
\displaystyle(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{*}
have continuous right adjoints. Moreover
\displaystyle(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}
and
\displaystyle(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})^{?}
are compatible with the functor
ren
. This implies the top morphism is an equivalence because formally it can be written as

\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F},\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\beta\in I_{\alpha/}}\,}(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}\circ(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{F}))\to\operatorname{Maps}(\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{F}),\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\beta\in I_{\alpha/}}\,}(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})^{?}\circ(\iota_{\alpha\to\beta})_{*}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{F})).

This finishes the proof that

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S^{\alpha})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(S)

is fully faithful. It remains to show it is surjective. We only need to show any
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}\in\operatorname{Coh}(S)
,

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}(\iota_{\alpha})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ(\iota_{\alpha})_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}(\mathcal{M})\to\mathcal{M}

is an equivalence. Note that both sides are bounded below, hence we only need to show it is sent to an equivalence by
ren
. Using Lemma
11.3.9
again,
ren
sends it to

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}(\iota_{\alpha})_{*}\circ(\iota_{\alpha})^{?}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{M})\to\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{M}),

which is indeed an equivalence because

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S^{\alpha})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(S).

∎

Proposition 11.10.2
.

Let
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
be a base scheme,
\displaystyle T=\lim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}T^{n}
be an apaisant presentation for an apaisant scheme over
\displaystyle B
, and
\displaystyle H=\lim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}H^{n}
be an apaisant presentation for an apaisant affine flat group scheme over
\displaystyle B
. Suppose we have compatible actions of
\displaystyle H^{n}
on
\displaystyle T^{n}
relative to
\displaystyle B
. Then:

(0)

The fppf quotient stack
\displaystyle T^{n}/H^{n}
is a QCA stack.

(1)

The fppf quotient stack
\displaystyle T/H
is weakly renormalizable and
\displaystyle T\to T/H
is a flat apaisant cover.

(2)

The maps
\displaystyle T/H\to T^{n}/H^{n}
and
\displaystyle T^{n}/H^{n}\to T^{m}/H^{m}
are
\displaystyle*
-pullable.

(3)

The functor

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{n}/H^{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T/H)

is an equivalence. In particular, the functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T/H)\to\lim_{*\operatorname{-push}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{n}/H^{n})

is also an equivalence.

Proof.

(0) is well-known because
\displaystyle T^{n},H^{n}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
and
\displaystyle H^{n}
is affine.

To prove (1), we only need to prove
\displaystyle T\to T/H
is relatively apaisant. But this follows from Example
11.2.13
.

To prove (2), we only need to check
\displaystyle T\to T^{n}
and
\displaystyle T^{n}\to T_{j}
are relatively apaisant. But both claims are obvious.

We now prove (3). We first prove

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{n}/H^{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T/H)

is fully faithful. Note that it preserves compact objects. Hence we only need to check full-faithfulness on compact objects. Consider the Cech nerve
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}\to T/H
for the cover
\displaystyle T\to T/H
and the similar Cech nerves
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}^{n}\to T^{n}/H^{n}
. For fixed
\displaystyle n
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{n},\mathcal{G}^{n}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T^{n}/H^{n})
, let
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H^{m})
be the
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks (for
\displaystyle m\geq n
) and similarly define
\displaystyle\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}
. Also consider the
\displaystyle*
-pullbacks
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{m},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}^{m}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}_{\bullet})
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{\bullet},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T_{\bullet})
. We only need to show

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m\geq n}\,}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m})\to\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})

is an equivalence. Note that
\displaystyle T_{\bullet}\simeq\lim_{n}T_{\bullet}^{n}
is an apaisant presentation. Hence we have

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\bullet}^{n})\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T_{\bullet})

and therefore

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m\geq n}\,}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}^{m}_{\bullet},\mathcal{G}^{m}_{\bullet})\to\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}).

By Theorem
11.6.1
, we have

\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet},\mathcal{G}_{\bullet}),\;\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m})\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m}_{\bullet}).

Hence we only need to show

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m\geq n}\,}\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m}_{\bullet})\to\operatorname{Tot}_{\operatorname{semi}}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m\geq n}\,}\operatorname{Maps}(\mathcal{F}_{\bullet}^{m},\mathcal{G}^{m}_{\bullet})

is an equivalence. But this can be proved by using the same trick as in the proof of Proposition
11.7.1
.

It remains to show the image of

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{n}/H^{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T/H)

generates the target. Note that

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{n}/H^{n})\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n\geq m,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T^{m}/H^{n}).

We only need to show:

(i)

The image of

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T^{m}/H)\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T/H)

generates the target.

(ii)

For each
\displaystyle m
, the image of

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n\geq m,*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m}/H^{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(T^{m}/H)

generates the target.

Note that
\displaystyle p_{m}:T/H\to T^{m}/H
is affine schematic. Hence for any
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}\in\operatorname{Coh}(T/H)
, we have a well-defined morphism

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m}\,}(p_{m})^{*}_{\textnormal{ren}}\circ(p_{m})_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(\mathcal{M})\to\mathcal{M}.

To prove (i), we only need to show this is an equivalence. Note that each term in the colimit is bounded. Hence we only need to prove

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{m}\,}(p_{m})^{*}\circ(p_{m})_{*}\circ\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{M})\to\textnormal{ren}(\mathcal{M})

is an equivalence in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T/H).
By Theorem
11.6.1
, we only need to prove its
\displaystyle*
-pullback along
\displaystyle T\to T/H
is an equivalence. But this follows from the base-change isomorphisms and the equivalence

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T^{m})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T).

This proves (i).

It remains to prove (ii). Since
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H)
is closed under truncations, we only need to show
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H)^{\heartsuit}
is contained in the image. Write
\displaystyle q:T^{m}\to T^{m}/H
and
\displaystyle q_{n}:T^{m}\to T^{m}/H^{n}
for the projections. Using Theorem
11.6.1
and the base-change isomorphisms, it is easy to see the adjoint pairs
\displaystyle(q^{*},q_{*})
,
\displaystyle((q_{n})^{*},(q_{n})_{*})
are comonadic. We claim the natural transformation

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n\geq m}\,}(q_{n})^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}\to q^{*}\circ q_{*}

between comonads on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m})
is an equivalence. To prove the claim, we only need to show it is an equivalence between underlying functors. Then it follows from the base-change isomorphisms and the equivalence

\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-pull}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T^{m}\times_{B}H^{n})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*}(T^{m}\times_{B}H).

It follows from definition that

\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H)^{\heartsuit}\simeq[q^{*}\circ q_{*}]\operatorname{-comod}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m}))\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m})}\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m})^{\heartsuit}

and

\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H^{n})^{\heartsuit}\simeq[q_{n}^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}]\operatorname{-comod}(\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m}))\times_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m})}\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m})^{\heartsuit}.

Note that the comonads
\displaystyle q^{*}\circ q_{*}
and
\displaystyle q_{n}^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}
are t-exact. Now consider a given
\displaystyle(q^{*}\circ q_{*})
-comodule
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
such that the underlying object
\displaystyle\underline{\mathcal{M}}
is contained in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m})^{\heartsuit}
. Since
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
is compact in
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{m})
, the coaction morphism

\underline{\mathcal{M}}\to q^{*}\circ q_{*}(\underline{\mathcal{M}})\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{n\geq m}\,}(q_{n})^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}(\underline{\mathcal{M}})

factors through
\displaystyle\underline{\mathcal{M}}\to(q_{n})^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}(\underline{\mathcal{M}})
for some
\displaystyle n
. By enlarging
\displaystyle n
, we can assume this map is a coaction morphism
66
66

66

There are no higher compatibilities for coactions in an abelian category!
. By definition,
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
is the co-restriction of the above
\displaystyle q_{n}^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}
-comodule structure on
\displaystyle\underline{\mathcal{M}}
along
\displaystyle q_{n}^{*}\circ(q_{n})_{*}\to q^{*}\circ q_{*}
. In other words, any object in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H)^{\heartsuit}
is an image of an object in
\displaystyle\operatorname{Coh}(T^{m}/H^{n})^{\heartsuit}
. This finishes the proof.

∎

Definition 11.10.3
.

Let
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
be an affine base scheme. A weakly renormalizable prestack
\displaystyle S
over
\displaystyle B
is
of quotient type
if it can be written as
\displaystyle S\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha\in I}\,}S^{\alpha}
as in Proposition
11.10.1
such that each
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}
is of the form
\displaystyle S^{\alpha}\simeq T/H
as in Proposition
11.10.2
with
\displaystyle T\to B
of bounded Tor dimension.

Lemma 11.10.4
.

Let
\displaystyle S=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha\in I}\,}S^{\alpha}
be of quotient type over
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. Then for any
\displaystyle B^{\prime}\to B
in
\,{}^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, the fiber product
\displaystyle S\times_{B}B^{\prime}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle B^{\prime}
, and the map
\displaystyle S\times_{B}B^{\prime}\to S
is vafp.

Proof.

The first claim is obvious. To prove the second claim, since
\displaystyle S\times_{B}B^{\prime}\to S
is a base-change of
\displaystyle B^{\prime}\to B
, we only need to show
\displaystyle S\times_{B}B^{\prime}\to S
is uafp. Let
\displaystyle U\in\operatorname{Cov}(S)
be a flat apaisant cover, by Remark
11.4.12
, we only need to show there exists a presentation
\displaystyle U=\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{\alpha}\,}U^{\alpha}
of
\displaystyle U
as an apaisant indscheme such that each
\displaystyle U^{\alpha}\times_{B}B^{\prime}
is eventually coconnective. Now
\displaystyle U^{\alpha}:=S^{\alpha}\times_{S}U
satisfies this condition because it is an apaisant scheme of bounded Tor dimension over
\displaystyle B
.

∎

Definition 11.10.5
.

For a laft prestack
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. A convergent prestack
\displaystyle Y_{B}
over
\displaystyle B
is
of quotient type
if for
any
test scheme
\displaystyle s:S\to B
with
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, the fiber product
\displaystyle Y_{s}:=Y_{B}\times_{B}S
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle S
. By Lemma
11.10.4
, when
\displaystyle B
is affine, this definition is compatible with the previous one.

Example 11.10.6
.

\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{\operatorname{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
. To see this, note that any
\displaystyle s:S\to\textnormal{Ran}_{\operatorname{dR}}
factors (non-canonically) through
\displaystyle X^{I}\to\operatorname{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}
for some
\displaystyle I
. Hence we only need to check
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G\backslash\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle X^{I}
. Recall that
\displaystyle[\operatorname{Gr}_{G}]_{X^{I}}=[\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}
is a
classical
ind-finite type indscheme, hence there exists a presentation
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}G/\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits}Y_{\alpha}
such that each
\displaystyle Y_{\alpha}
is stablized by the (left)
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}
-action. Then we only need to check each
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}\backslash Y_{\alpha}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle X^{I}
. Let
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}\simeq\lim_{m}H_{m}
be as in Section
10.3
. For fixed
\displaystyle\alpha
, there exists a large enough
\displaystyle m
such that the action of
\displaystyle[\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}}
on
\displaystyle Y_{\alpha}
factors through
\displaystyle H_{m}
. Hence we obtain a desired cofiltered system of actions
\displaystyle\{H_{n},Y_{\alpha}\}_{n\geq m}
whose limit is
\displaystyle([\mathcal{L}^{+}G]_{X^{I}},Y_{\alpha})
. It remains to check
\displaystyle Y_{\alpha}\to X^{I}
is of bounded Tor dimension, but this is obvious because
\displaystyle Y_{\alpha}
is classical and
\displaystyle X^{I}
is smooth.

Remark 11.10.7
.

If
\displaystyle Y_{B}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, then
\displaystyle Y_{B}
is weakly renormalizable. To see this, let
\displaystyle\{B_{i}\to B\}
be a finite Zariski cover of
\displaystyle B
. By definition, each
\displaystyle Y_{B_{i}}:=Y_{B}\times_{B}B_{i}
is weakly renormalizable. Let
\displaystyle S_{i}\to Y_{B_{i}}
be a flat apaisant cover. Then the disjoint union
\displaystyle\sqcup S_{i}\to Y_{B}
is a flat apaisant cover.

Corollary 11.10.8
.

If
\displaystyle Y_{B}
(resp.
\displaystyle Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}}
) is of quotient type over
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
(resp.
\displaystyle B^{\prime}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
). Then the external tensor product functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{B})\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{B}\times Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}})

is an equivalence.

Proof.

Follows from Proposition
11.9.14
, Proposition
11.10.1
, Proposition
11.10.2
and
[
DG13
, Corollary 4.2.3]
.

∎

11.11
IndCoh as a crystal of categories

In this subsection, we show that for a prestack
\displaystyle Y_{B_{\operatorname{dR}}}
over a laft de-Rham prestack
\displaystyle B_{\operatorname{dR}}
such that its fibers
\displaystyle Y_{x}
at
\displaystyle x\in B_{\operatorname{dR}}
are nice enough, there is a canonical
crystal of categories
on
\displaystyle B_{\operatorname{dR}}
such that its fibers at
\displaystyle x
is
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{x})
(resp.
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{x})
). In particular, given a (nice enough) factorization space, we can obtain two factorization categories that are dual to each other.

Warning 11.11.1
.

If we replace
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
by a general laft prestack
\displaystyle B
, then we can
not
obtain a
quasi-coherent
sheaf of of categories on
\displaystyle B
such that its fibers at
\displaystyle x
is
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{x})
or
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{x})
.

Construction 11.11.2
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B}
be of quotient type over
\displaystyle B\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. There is a canonical
\displaystyle(\textnormal{IndCoh}(B),\overset{!}{\otimes})
-action on
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{B})
whose action functor is

\textnormal{IndCoh}(B)\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{B})\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(B\times Y_{B})\xrightarrow{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{B}).

Note that the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functor is well-defined because
\displaystyle Y_{B}\to B\times Y_{B}
is vafp.

The above
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(B)
-action is functorial in
\displaystyle Y_{B}
in theo following sense. For
\displaystyle f:Y_{B}\to Y_{B}^{\prime}
defined over
\displaystyle B
, the base-change isomorphims provide
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(B)
-linear structure on
\displaystyle f_{*,\operatorname{ren}},f_{\operatorname{ren}}^{!},f^{*}_{\operatorname{ren}}
as long as whenever functors are defined.

Construction 11.11.3
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B}
be of quotient type over a laft prestack
\displaystyle B
. For any laft prestack
\displaystyle T\to B
over
\displaystyle B
, we define

\mathbf{\Gamma}(t:T\to B,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)):=\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}),

where the limit is taken for any test scheme
\displaystyle S\to T
with
\displaystyle S\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, and
\displaystyle s
is the composition
\displaystyle S\to T\to B
. Note that the
\displaystyle!
-pullback functors are well-defined because each
\displaystyle Y_{s^{\prime}}\to Y_{s}
is vafp (Lemma
11.10.4
). When there is little danger ambiguity, we also write

\mathbf{\Gamma}(T,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

for this category.

By Construction,
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))
has a module structure for the symmetric monoidal category

\textnormal{IndCoh}(T)\simeq\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T_{\operatorname{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S),

and such module structure is functorial in
\displaystyle T
, i.e., for
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\to T
defined over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
, the retriction functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(T,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(T^{\prime},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

intertwines the symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(T^{\prime})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(T)
.

Remark 11.11.4
.

Let
\displaystyle T\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
be defined over
\displaystyle B
. Using Lemma
11.9.14
, one can show the functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{t})\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(T,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

is an equivalence.

Remark 11.11.5
.

Let
\displaystyle T_{\textnormal{dR}}
be defined over
\displaystyle B
such that
\displaystyle T\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. By
[
GR17a
, Chapter 2, Corollary 4.3.4]
and
, we have

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\in(>^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{\operatorname{nil-isom\,to\,}T_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\in(>^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{\operatorname{nil-isom\,to\,}T_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push},S\in(>^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{\operatorname{nil-isom\,to\,}T_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}).

Note that the last line is compactly generated hence dualizable. It folllows that

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))^{\vee}

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\in(>^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{\operatorname{nil-isom\,to\,}T_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\in(>^{-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{/T_{\textnormal{dR}}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}).

Proposition 11.11.6
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}
be of quotient type over a laft de-Rham prestack
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
. Then

[T\in(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{AffSch}_{\operatorname{aft}})_{/B}]\mapsto[\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\in\textnormal{DMod}(T)\operatorname{-mod}]

defines a crystal of categories on
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
. In other words, for any
\displaystyle T^{\prime}\to T
, the functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{DMod}(T^{\prime})\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

is an equivalence.

Remark 11.11.7
.

The proof below actually works for any
separated
scheme
\displaystyle T\in(^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft,sep}})_{/B}
.

Proof.

It follows from definition that the desired functor is equivalent to the following composition

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{DMod}(T^{\prime})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle[\lim_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))]\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}[\lim_{V\to T_{\textnormal{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}},V\to T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}},V\to T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}},V\to T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(S)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V)]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}},V\to T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}[\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)),

where the last equivalence is due to

T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}}\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}},V\to T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}\,}S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V

as a prestack over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
.

Hence we only need to prove:

(i)

The functors

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\mapsto\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}\mapsto\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))]\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\mathcal{D}
commute with limits;

(ii)

The functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

is an equivalence.

Too prove claim (i), we only need to show
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)
and
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))
are dualizable as
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(T)
-module categories. Note that they are compactly generated hence dualizable as plain categories. Then
[
Lin21
, Lemma B.3.3]
implies the desired claim.

We now prove (ii). By Corollary
11.10.8
, we have

\mathbf{\Gamma}(S,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}(V)\simeq\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)),

where
\displaystyle S\times V
is defined over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
via the composition
\displaystyle S\times V\to S\to B_{\textnormal{dR}}
. Hence the desired functor can be identified with the functor

b:\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}}\times T_{\textnormal{dR}})}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}})\to\mathbf{\Gamma}((S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)).

Consider the functor

\textbf{Id}\otimes\Delta^{!}:\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes_{\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}}\times T_{\textnormal{dR}})}\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}}).

Note that it has a fully faithful left adjoint
\displaystyle\textbf{Id}\otimes\Delta_{*}
. Hence we only need to show
\displaystyle b\circ(\textbf{Id}\otimes\Delta^{!})
also has a fully faithful left adjoint, and the two co-localization functors on

\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\simeq\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times V).

can be identified.

By definition, the endo-functor
\displaystyle\textbf{Id}\otimes(\Delta_{*}\circ\Delta^{!})
is given by the action of
\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(\omega)\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}}\times T_{\textnormal{dR}})
on

\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times V)
. Let
\displaystyle\delta:S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V\to S\times V
be the base-change of
\displaystyle\Delta
. Note that
\displaystyle S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V
is the formal completion of
\displaystyle S\times V
along
\displaystyle S^{\operatorname{cl,red}}\times_{T}V^{\operatorname{cl,red}}
. Hence by
[
GR14
, Proposition 6.5.2]
,
\displaystyle S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V
is a (laft) indscheme. The base-change isomorphism implies
\displaystyle\Delta_{*}(\omega)
is sent to
\displaystyle\delta_{*}(\omega)
by the (symmetric monoidal)
\displaystyle!
-pullback functor

\textnormal{IndCoh}(T_{\textnormal{dR}}\times T_{\textnormal{dR}})\to\textnormal{IndCoh}(S\times V).

Hence the endo-functor
\displaystyle\textbf{Id}\otimes(\Delta_{*}\circ\Delta^{!})
is also given by the action of
\displaystyle\delta_{*}(\omega)\in\textnormal{IndCoh}(S\times V)
on

\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times V)
. Now consider the following base-change of
\displaystyle\delta
:

d:Y_{s}\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V\to Y_{s}\times V.

Note that
\displaystyle Y_{s}\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V
is weakly renormalizable
67
67

67

Proof: Let
\displaystyle U
be a flat apaisant cover of
\displaystyle Y_{s}
. By Lemma
11.4.5
,
\displaystyle U\times_{S}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V)
is an apaisant indscheme, which is a flat apaisant cover of
\displaystyle Y_{s}\times_{S}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V)
.
. Hence by the base-change isomorphism (see Lemma
11.9.18
), the above action can be identified with
\displaystyle d_{*,\textnormal{ren}}\circ d_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}
.

On the other hand, note that the base-change of
\displaystyle d
along itself is an isomophism. The base-change isomorphism implies
\displaystyle d_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
is fully faithful. Hence we only need to identify the functor

\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\to\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

with
\displaystyle d_{\textnormal{ren}}^{?}
. Let
\displaystyle S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V\simeq\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}Z_{i}
be a presentation of the laft indscheme such that
\displaystyle Z_{i}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
. It follows from definition (and Remark
11.11.4
) that the left adjoint of the above functor is given by the following composition:

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(S\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V,\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times_{S}Z_{i})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{*\operatorname{-push}}\,}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times_{S}Z_{i})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times_{S}\mathbin{\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\displaylimits_{i}\,}Z_{i})

\displaystyle\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}V)

\displaystyle\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times V).

Proposition
11.10.1
implies the third functor is an equivalence, which finishes the proof.

∎

Definition 11.11.8
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}
be of quotient type over a laft de-Rham prestack
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
. We denote by
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)
the crystal of categories over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
provided by Proposition
11.11.6
. For
\displaystyle t:T\to B
, we denote the corresponding section as

[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)]_{t_{\textnormal{dR}}}:=\mathbf{\Gamma}(t_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)).

When there is no danger of ambiguity, we also use
\displaystyle[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)]_{T_{\textnormal{dR}}}
.

By Remark
11.11.5
and
[
Lin21
, Lemma B.3.3]
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)
is a dualizable object in the symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle\operatorname{CrsyCat}(B_{\textnormal{dR}})
, and the sections of its dual
\displaystyle[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)]^{\vee}
are given by

\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)]^{\vee})\simeq\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))^{\vee}\simeq\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T_{\textnormal{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}).

It follows from the proof of Proposition
11.11.6
that the above identification is functorial in
\displaystyle T_{\textnormal{dR}}
. Hence we use the notation

\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y):=[\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)]^{\vee}.

Construction 11.11.9
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}
be of quotient type over a laft de-Rham prestack
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
and
\displaystyle f:B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}\to B_{\textnormal{dR}}
be any map between laft de-Rham prestacks. Then the fiber product
\displaystyle Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}:=Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}
is of quotient type over
\displaystyle B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}
and Proposition
11.11.6
provides an identification

\mathbf{cores}_{f}(\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\simeq\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime})

as crystals of categories on
\displaystyle B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}
. Therefore we also have

\mathbf{cores}_{f}(\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\simeq\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}).

Construction 11.11.10
.

Let
\displaystyle Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}
(resp.
\displaystyle Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
) be of quotient type over a laft de-Rham prestack
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
(resp.
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}^{\prime}
). By Corollary
11.10.8
and Lemma
11.10.4
,

(Y\boxtimes Y^{\prime})_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}\times B_{\textnormal{dR}}^{\prime}}:=Y_{B_{\textnormal{dR}}}\times Y^{\prime}_{B^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}}

is of quotient type over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}\times B_{\textnormal{dR}}^{\prime}
. Moreover, for
\displaystyle T_{\textnormal{dR}}
(resp.
\displaystyle T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}}
) over
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}
(resp.
\displaystyle B_{\textnormal{dR}}^{\prime}
) such that
\displaystyle T,T^{\prime}\in\,^{>-\infty}\operatorname{Sch}_{\operatorname{aft}}
, we have an equivalence

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}))

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle[\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T_{\operatorname{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s})]\otimes[\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T_{\operatorname{dR}},S^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}}}[\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s})\otimes\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}})]

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\lim_{!\operatorname{-pull},S\to T_{\operatorname{dR}},S^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}}}\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y_{s}\times Y^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}})

\displaystyle\displaystyle\simeq

\displaystyle\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}}\times T^{\prime}_{\textnormal{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y\boxtimes Y^{\prime})),

where the second line is equivalent to the third because
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y))
and
\displaystyle\mathbf{\Gamma}(T^{\prime}_{\operatorname{dR}},\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y^{\prime}))
are compactly generated. Hence we obtain an equivalence

Remark 11.11.16
.

Construction
11.11.15
breaks the symmetry between the
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
theory because in this paper we do not consider
co-unital
factorization categories. Namely, as the dual of the unital factorization category
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh_{*,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)
, the factorization category
\displaystyle\mathcal{I}nd\mathcal{C}oh^{!,\textnormal{ren}}(Y)
should be equipped with a co-unital structure. However, since we are more accustomed to unital structures
70
70

70

We prefer algebras than co-algebras.
, we produced a unital structure out of the co-unital one by replacing the
dual functors
by
conjugate functors
. It is this ad-hoc procedure that breaks the symmetry between
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}^{!,\textnormal{ren}}
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{IndCoh}_{*,\textnormal{ren}}
.
