\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}(X\times_{X\times X}X)
, i.e. quasi-coherent sheaves on the derived loop space
\displaystyle\mathcal{L}X:=\textnormal{Map}(S^{1},X)
, by acting as kernel via the diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\mathcal{L}X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{X\times X}

Write
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(X):=\textnormal{Mod}_{A}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\textnormal{Vect})
, so our statement becomes
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(X)\simeq\textnormal{QCoh}(\mathcal{L}X)
. More generally, the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{QCoh}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(X)
can be identified with quasi-coherent sheaves on the
\displaystyle n
-fold based loop space. This provides a geometric interpretation of the notion of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-modules.

12.1
Relative
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-Hochschild Cohomology

In this subsection, we define the relative
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-Hochschild cohomology and state a precise version of Theorem
12.0.2
.

Construction 12.1.1
.

Consider the (very large) category
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
of left
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-modules in
DGCat
. By
[
Lur12
, 5.1.4]
, it has an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n-1}
-structure.

Example 12.1.2
.

When
\displaystyle n=1
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
is a
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{0}
-category with the distinguished object given by
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
, considered as a left module of itself.

Example 12.1.3
.

When
\displaystyle n=2
,
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
is a monoidal category with the multiplication given by

\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\times\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}}(\textnormal{DGCat}),\;(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{N})\mapsto\mathcal{C}\otimes_{(\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{M}\otimes\mathcal{N}),

where the relative tensor product is formed by using the multiplication functor
\displaystyle m:\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}
. Note that
\displaystyle m
is a monoidal functor because
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
is assumed to have an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-structure.

Construction 12.1.4
.

Consider the category
\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})
of left
\displaystyle A
-modules in
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
. Note that it has a natural right
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-module structure. Similarly to
[
Lur12
, 4.8.5.20]
, we will show

•

\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\in\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
has a canonical
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n-1}
-algebra structure.

To define this structure, we consider the (very large) category
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
of
DG categories with marked objects
. Its objects are pairs
\displaystyle(\mathcal{D},B)
where
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
is a cocomplete DG-category and
\displaystyle B
is an object in it; the morphisms
\displaystyle(\mathcal{D}_{1},B_{1})\to(\mathcal{D}_{2},B_{2})
are given by continuous functors
\displaystyle F:\mathcal{D}_{1}\to\mathcal{D}_{2}
together with morphisms
\displaystyle b:F(B_{1})\to B_{2}
. A morphism as above in
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
is
strict
if
\displaystyle b
is an isomorphism, i.e., if it preserves the marked objects.

It is clear that
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
carries a natural symmetric monoidal structure given by

(\mathcal{D}_{1},B_{1})\otimes(\mathcal{D}_{2},B_{2}):=(\mathcal{D}_{1}\otimes\mathcal{D}_{2},B_{1}\boxtimes B_{2}).

By definition,
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C},A)
is an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-algebra in
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
.

On the other hand, we consider the (very large) category
\displaystyle{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})
of
DG monoidal categories with right modules
. Its objects are pairs
\displaystyle(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M})
where
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
is an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-algebra in
DGCat
and
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
is a right
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
-module; the morphisms
\displaystyle(\mathcal{O}_{1},\mathcal{M}_{1})\to(\mathcal{O}_{2},\mathcal{M}_{2})
are given by continuous
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-functors
\displaystyle F:\mathcal{O}_{1}\to\mathcal{O}_{2}
and continuous functors
\displaystyle G:\mathcal{M}_{1}\to\mathcal{M}_{2}
such that
\displaystyle F,G
are compatible with the module structures in the usual sense. It is clear that
\displaystyle{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})
inherits a symmetric monoidal structure from
DGCat
.

Consider the functor

\displaystyle\Phi:{\textup{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{1}}}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\to{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}),\;(\mathcal{D},B)\mapsto(\mathcal{D},B{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D})),

\displaystyle((F,b):(\mathcal{D}_{1},B_{1})\to(\mathcal{D}_{2},B_{2}))\mapsto((F,\mathbf{ind}_{b}\circ F):(\mathcal{D}_{1},B_{1}{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D}_{1}))\to(\mathcal{D}_{2},B_{2}{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D}_{2}))),

where the functor
\displaystyle\mathbf{ind}_{b}\circ F
is the composition

B_{1}{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D}_{1})\overset{F}{\longrightarrow}F(B_{1}){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D}_{2})\overset{\mathbf{ind}_{b}}{\longrightarrow}B_{2}{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D}_{2}).

It is clear that
\displaystyle\Phi
has a natural symmetric monoidal structure.

By enlarging the universe, we have a notion of the (very very large) category
\displaystyle\mathcal{CAT}
of very large categories, such that
DGCat
is an object in it. Consider the (very very large) category
\displaystyle\mathcal{CAT}_{*}
defined similarly as
\displaystyle\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}
. We have a functor

\Psi:{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\mathcal{CAT}_{*},\;(\mathcal{O,\mathcal{M}})\mapsto(\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}),\mathcal{M}).

It also has a natural
right-lax
symmetric monoidal structure. Combining the above two paragraphs, we obtain a
right-lax
symmetric monoidal functor
\displaystyle\Psi\circ\Phi
. Hence it induces a functor
\displaystyle{\textup{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\to{\textup{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\mathcal{CAT}_{*})
.
By construction, it sends
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C},A)
to

(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}),A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\in{\textup{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\mathcal{CAT}_{*}).

Unwinding definitions, this means
\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\in\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
has a canonical
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n-1}
-algebra structure as desired.

Example 12.1.5
.

When
\displaystyle n=1
, we obtain an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{0}
-structure on
\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\in\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
, i.e., a right
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-linear functors
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}\to A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})
. By construction, it is the functor that sends
\displaystyle X\in\mathcal{C}
to
\displaystyle m(A,X)
equipped with the obvious left
\displaystyle A
-module structure.

Example 12.1.6
.

When
\displaystyle n=2
, we obtain an
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-structure on
\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\in\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
. By construction, the multiplication is given by

(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\otimes A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\otimes_{(\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C})}\mathcal{C}\simeq(A\boxtimes A){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C})\otimes_{(\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C})}\mathcal{C}\simeq m(A,A){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\overset{\operatorname{ind}}{\longrightarrow}A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}),

where the last functor is induced by the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-map
\displaystyle m(A,A)\to A
.

Definition 12.1.7
.

Rougly speaking, for
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}\in\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))
, the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-Hochschild cohomology of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
relative to
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
is the universal DG
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-category, viewed as an algebra in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\operatorname{DGCat})
, that acts on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}\in\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\operatorname{DGCat})
in a way compatible with the right action of
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
.

More precisly,

\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D}):=\mathbf{Maps}_{\mathcal{D}-\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}),

where the RHS is the mapping DG category inside the
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}
-enriched category
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))
.
As in
[
Lur12
, 5.3.1.15]
,
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D})
carries the structure of a DG
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-category.

Example 12.1.8
.

We have
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\mathcal{C}
as DG
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-categories.

Construction 12.1.9
.

It follows from definition that we have an action of
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D})
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
viewed as objects in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\operatorname{DGCat})
. In particular, we have a forgetful functor

\operatorname{oblv}:\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D}

between DG
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n-1}
-categories. Explicitly, it is defined as the composition

\mathbf{Maps}_{\mathcal{D}-\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})\to\operatorname{LFun}(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})\to\mathcal{D},

where the last functor is taking value at the monoidal unit of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
.

To describe the functoriality of
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D})
in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
, we need the following definition:

Definition 12.1.10
.

Let
\displaystyle F:\mathcal{D}_{1}\to\mathcal{D}_{2}
be a morphism in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))
. We say
\displaystyle F

satisfies the projection formula
if the right adjoint
\displaystyle F^{R}:\mathcal{D}_{2}\to\mathcal{D}_{1}
, which is a priori right-lax
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{1}
-linear, is strictly
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{1}
-linear. In particular,
\displaystyle F^{R}
is also strictly
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-linear and continuous.

Remark 12.1.11
.

The above definition also makes sense when
\displaystyle n=\infty
. In this case, the pullback functor
\displaystyle f^{*}:\textnormal{QCoh}(Y)\to\textnormal{QCoh}(X)
for quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes satisfies the projection formula in the above sense.

Example 12.1.12
.

One can verify that the induction functor
\displaystyle\operatorname{ind}:\mathcal{C}\to A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})
satisfying the projection formula.

Construction 12.1.13
.

Let
\displaystyle F:\mathcal{D}_{1}\to\mathcal{D}_{2}
be a morphism in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))
satisfying the projection formula. Then we have a functor

\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D}_{2})\to\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D}_{1})

defined as

\mathbf{Maps}_{\mathcal{D}_{2}-\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D}_{2},\mathcal{D}_{2})\to\mathbf{Maps}_{\mathcal{D}_{1}-\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D}_{1},\mathcal{D}_{1}),\;T\mapsto F^{R}\circ T\circ F.

It follows formally that the above functor has a canonical
right-lax

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-structure
71
71

71

The details will be provided in the second author’s thesis. Also, we do not need this claim to prove the main result of this paper. Namely, without it, we can still prove a weaker version of Theorem
12.0.2
which says there is a canonical equivalence
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\simeq A{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{C})
between plain categories. This weaker result is enough for our purpose.

.

Example 12.1.14
.

Explicitly, the right-lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D}_{2})\to\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{D}_{1})
is given by the natural transformation

F^{R}\circ T\circ F\circ F^{R}\circ T^{\prime}\circ F\to F^{R}\circ T\circ T^{\prime}\circ F

induced by the counit adjunction
\displaystyle F\circ F^{R}\to\operatorname{Id}
.

Construction 12.1.15
.

We apply the above construction to the induction functor
\displaystyle\operatorname{ind}:\mathcal{C}\to A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})
and obtain a right-lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-functor

\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\to\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq\mathcal{C}.

It follows from constructinon that the unit of LHS is sent to the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-algebra
\displaystyle A
in RHS. Hence the above functor factors through a

Lemma 12.1.16
.

The right-lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\to A{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{C})
is strict.

Proof.

We only need to prove the underlying right-lax
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-functor is strict. However, this follows from the explicit description in Example
12.1.14
.

∎

The rest of this section is to prove the following precise version of Theorem
12.0.2
:

Proposition 12.1.17
.

The
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{HH}_{\mathbb{E}_{n},\,/\mathcal{C}}(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\to A{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{C})
constructed above is an equivalence.

Remark 12.1.18
.

When
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
can be promoted to a symmetric monoidal category, the proposition was proved in
[
Fra13
, Proposition 4.36]
. The idea is to express both sides as
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(A){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})
, where
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(A)
is the enveloping algebra of the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-aglebra
\displaystyle A
. Unfortunately, the construction of
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(A)
only makes sense when
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
is symmetric monoidal. Indeed, in the general case,
\displaystyle A{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{C})
does not have a
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
-action.

Nevertheless, we will prove the proposition based on the following observation: there exists a
relative
enveloping algrbra
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A)
of
\displaystyle A
inside
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{C})
such that we have a canonical equivalence

A{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{C})\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}),

where the definition of the RHS uses the left action of
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{C})
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
that corresponds to the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-action on
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}
on itself. Then one can generalize the proof of
[
Fra13
, Proposition 4.36]
by carefully replace the enveloping algrbras by the relative ones.

We will construct and study
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A)
in
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign

12.2
and use it to prove the proposition in
\displaystyle\lx@sectionsign

12.3
.

12.2
Enveloping Algebras

Construction 12.2.1
.

Recall the (very large) symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}
of DG categories with a marked object in it. Note that the tensor product in
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}
distributes with sifted colimits (in fact with all small colimits). Hence for
\displaystyle(\mathcal{D},B)\in\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})
, we have an adjoint pair

\operatorname{ind}_{(\mathcal{D},B)}:\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}\adjoint(\mathcal{D},B){-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}):\operatorname{oblv}_{(\mathcal{D},B)}

such that both functors are
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}
-linear. Hence the corresponding monad is given by tensoring with an associative algebra object
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B)
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}
, which is known as the
enveloping algebra
of
\displaystyle(\mathcal{D},B)
. We have

(\mathcal{D},B)\textnormal{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})

(60)

compatible with the forgetful functors to
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}
. Also, the functor

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}:\textnormal{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})\to\textnormal{Alg}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})

is symmetric monoidal.

Since
\displaystyle\operatorname{oblv}_{*}:\operatorname{DGCat}_{*}\to\operatorname{DGCat}
is symmetric monoidal, the algebra
\displaystyle\operatorname{oblv}_{*}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B))
is just the enveloping algebra
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})
of
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
in
\displaystyle\operatorname{DGCat}
. We have

\mathcal{D}\textnormal{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat})\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D}){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{DGCat}).

(61)

Recall that knowing
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B)
is equivalent to knowing an associative algebra object inside
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})
. We refer this algebra as the
relative enveloping algebra
of
\displaystyle B
and denote it by
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(B)\in U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})
.

Let
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
be any object in
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}\textnormal{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat})
. e can use (
61
) to view it as a left module of
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})
. By (
60
), we have

(\mathcal{D},B)\textnormal{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})\times_{\mathcal{D}\textnormal{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\operatorname{DGCat})}\{\mathcal{M}\}\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{DGCat}_{*})\times_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D}){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{DGCat})}\{\mathcal{M}\}.

In other words,

B{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}}(\mathcal{M})\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(B){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{M}),

where the LHS is defined via the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{n}
-
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}
-module on
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
while the RHS is defined via the left
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})
-module structure on
\displaystyle\mathcal{M}
.

Example 12.2.2
.

When
\displaystyle n=1
, we have
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{1}}(\mathcal{D})\simeq\mathcal{D}\otimes\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{rev}}
and
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{1}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(B)\simeq B\boxtimes B^{\operatorname{rev}}
. Note that
\displaystyle B^{\operatorname{rev}}
only makes sense inside the monoidal category
\displaystyle\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{rev}}
.

Remark 12.2.3
.

Argument from
[
Fra13
, 3.16]
carries through and allows us to compute it as the factorization homology

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B)\simeq\int_{S^{n-1}\times\mathbb{R}}(\mathcal{D},B)

where on RHS we consider
\displaystyle(\mathcal{D},B)
as a factorizable cosheaf valued in
\displaystyle\mathcal{CAT}_{*}
over
\displaystyle\mathbb{R}^{n}
. In partuclar, we have

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D},B)\simeq(\mathcal{D},B)^{\operatorname{rev}}\otimes_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D},B)^{\operatorname{rev}}}(\mathcal{D},B).

Hence we have

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\mathcal{D})\simeq\mathcal{D}^{\operatorname{rev}}\otimes_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{D})^{\operatorname{rev}}}\mathcal{D},\;U_{\mathbb{E}_{n}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(B)\simeq B^{\operatorname{rev}}\boxtimes_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(B)^{\operatorname{rev}}}B^{\operatorname{rev}}.

Construction 12.2.4
.

The functor

\operatorname{Mod}:\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})\to\textnormal{DGCat},\;(\mathcal{D},B)\mapsto B{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{D})

is symmetric monoidal and commutes with sifted colimits. It follows that we have a commutative diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\operatorname{Mod}}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Alg}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{\operatorname{Mod}}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}).}

In other words, for
\displaystyle(\mathcal{C},A)\in\operatorname{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n}}(\textnormal{DGCat}_{*})
, we have

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}))\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A){\textup{-mod}}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}))

(62)

as DG monoidal categories.

Example 12.2.5
.

When
\displaystyle n=2
, the above equivalence reads as

A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})\otimes A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{rev}}\simeq(A\boxtimes A^{\operatorname{rev}}){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}\otimes\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{rev}}).

Indeed, this follows from
\displaystyle A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})^{\operatorname{rev}}\simeq A^{\operatorname{rev}}{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{rev}})
.

Construction 12.2.6
.

Similarly, we consider the (very large) symmetric monoidal category
\displaystyle{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})
of DG monoidal categories with right modules. Note that the two forgerful functors

{(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})\to\operatorname{DGCat}

are symmetric monoidal and commute with sifted colimits. Hence we can define

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}:\operatorname{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\to\operatorname{Alg}^{\mathbb{E}_{1}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}))

such that

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M}){\textup{-mod}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\simeq(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M}){-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat})),

and

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M})\simeq(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O}),U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{M})).

Note that we can view
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}
as an object in

\mathcal{O}{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O}){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat})).

Hence we have

\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M}){\textup{-mod}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\times_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O}){\textup{-mod}}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}))}\{\mathcal{O}\}\simeq

\displaystyle\simeq(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M}){-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}({(\textnormal{Alg},\textnormal{Mod}^{r})}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\times_{\mathcal{O}{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\operatorname{Alg}(\textnormal{DGCat}))}\{\mathcal{O}\}.

Unwinding the definitions, this says

U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{M}){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\simeq\mathcal{M}{-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})),

where
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{M})\in\operatorname{Alg}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O}){\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))
and the LHS is defined using the
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{O}){\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
-action on
\displaystyle\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
.

Example 12.2.7
.

When
\displaystyle n=2
, the above equivalence reads as

(\mathcal{M}\otimes\mathcal{M}^{\operatorname{rev}}){\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\simeq\mathcal{M}\operatorname{-bimod}(\mathcal{O}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})).

Example 12.2.8
.

Applying the above construction to
\displaystyle(\mathcal{O},\mathcal{M}):=(\mathcal{C},A\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{C}))
and using the equivalence (

), we obtain

(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A)\operatorname{-mod}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C})))\operatorname{-mod}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat}))\simeq(A{\textup{-mod}}(\mathcal{C})){-\textup{mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}}(\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})).

We emphasize that
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}^{\operatorname{rel}}(A)\operatorname{-mod}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}))
is an algebra in
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{n-1}}(\mathcal{C}){\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
, which acts on
\displaystyle\mathcal{C}{\textup{-mod}^{r}}(\textnormal{DGCat})
.

Proof of Proposition

.

Proof of Lemma
2.8.6

The forgetful functor

U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{DGCat})\simeq\Rep_{q}(T)\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\textnormal{DGCat})\xrightarrow{\oblv}\Rep_{q}(T)\operatorname{-mod}(\textnormal{DGCat})

preserves the base point
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
, thus induces a monoidal functor
\displaystyle\textnormal{ins}:\Rep_{q}(T)\to U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
(topologically, this corresponds to the inclusion
\displaystyle\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}\setminus\{0\}
).
Furthermore, we have an algebra

U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})\in\textnormal{Alg}(U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T)))

such that
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))\simeq\Omega_{q}\operatorname{-mod}^{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
. Looking again at
\displaystyle\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2}\setminus\{0\}
but this time considering the
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{2}
-algebra
\displaystyle(\Rep_{q}(T),\Omega_{q})
within
\displaystyle\mathcal{CAT}_{*}
, we see that there is a morphism
\displaystyle\textnormal{ins}(\Omega_{q})\to U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})
of
\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}
-algebras within
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
.

The category
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))
is a
\displaystyle(\Rep_{q}(T),U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T)))
-bimodule category, where
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
acts via the functor
ins
. We consider the object

\mathfrak{K}:=k\tensor_{\Omega_{q}}U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q}):=|k\boxtimes\Omega_{q}^{\bullet}\boxtimes U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})|\in\Rep_{q}(T)\tensor_{\Rep_{q}(T)}U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T))\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}(\Rep_{q}(T));

by above, this is a well-defined expression, and it is a bimodule over

\Hom_{\Omega_{q}\operatorname{-mod}^{r}(\Rep_{q}(T))}(k,k)\simeq\Hom_{U_{q}^{\textnormal{Lus}}(N)\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))_{\textnormal{loc.nilp.}}}(\textnormal{Bar}_{\Omega_{q}}(k),\textnormal{Bar}_{\Omega_{q}}(k))\simeq U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-})

as an algebra in
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
acting from left, and
\displaystyle U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})
from the right. Thus, using it as the kernel, we obtain a functor

\Rep_{q}^{\textnormal{mxd}}(G)\simeq U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}(\Omega_{q})\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T))\xrightarrow{\mathfrak{K}\tensor_{U_{\mathbb{E}_{2}}^{\textnormal{rel}}}(-)}U_{q}^{\textnormal{KD}}(N^{-})\operatorname{-mod}(\Rep_{q}(T));

it is straightforward to check that further forgetting to
\displaystyle\Rep_{q}(T)
gives the expected answer.
∎

13.1
Regular-Holonomic D-modules

For
\displaystyle S
any classical aft smooth scheme, we have (non-cocomplete) full subcategories

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}(S)\subseteq\textnormal{DMod}_{\textnormal{coh}}(S)\subseteq\textnormal{DMod}(S)

consists of objects whose cohomologies are regular holonomic D-modules (resp. coherent D-modules). Since
\displaystyle S
is a aft scheme, we have
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(S)\simeq\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{DMod}_{\textnormal{coh}}(S))
; it follows that

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(S):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}(S))

is a
full subcategory
of
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(S)
. We refer to it as the category of (ind)-regular holonomic D-modules.

More generally, for any aft scheme
\displaystyle S
, we choose a closed embedding
\displaystyle\iota:S^{\textnormal{cl}}\to T
where
\displaystyle T
is classical, aft and smooth. There is then a fully faithful functor

\textnormal{DMod}(S)\simeq\textnormal{DMod}(S^{\textnormal{cl}})\xrightarrow{\iota_{!}}\textnormal{DMod}(T)

and we define

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(S):=\textnormal{DMod}(S)\times_{\textnormal{DMod}(T)}\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(T)\subseteq\textnormal{DMod}(S).

Because for any two
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{cl}}\to T_{1},S^{\textnormal{cl}}\to T_{2}
there exists another smooth classical
\displaystyle T_{3}
such that

\displaystyle\textstyle{S^{\textnormal{cl}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\textstyle{T_{3}}

commutes, where all arrows are closed embeddings (take the pushout
\displaystyle T_{1}\sqcup_{S^{\textnormal{cl}}}T_{2}
then embed into another smooth classical scheme), by Kashiwara’s lemma this definition does not depend on the choice of
\displaystyle\iota
.

Lemma 13.1.1
.

For arbitrary map
\displaystyle f:X\to Y
between aft schemes,
\displaystyle f^{!}
and
\displaystyle f_{*}
both preserve the (ind-)regular holonomic subcategory.

Proof.

By nil-invariance we readily reduce to the case of
\displaystyle X,Y
classical. It suffices to show that any
\displaystyle f
can be completed to a diagram

\displaystyle\textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{g}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{f}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\widetilde{X}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{p}
\displaystyle\textstyle{Y\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
\displaystyle\scriptstyle{h}
\displaystyle\textstyle{\widetilde{Y}}

where
\displaystyle g,h
are closed immersions and
\displaystyle\widetilde{X}
,
\displaystyle\widetilde{Y}
are smooth. Pick arbitrary
\displaystyle X\inj X^{\prime},Y\inj Y^{\prime}
of closed immersion into smooth schemes, then set

h:=(Y\to Y^{\prime}=:\widetilde{Y})\hskip 10.00002ptg:=(X\xrightarrow{\Gamma_{h\circ f}}(X\times Y^{\prime})\inj(X^{\prime}\times Y^{\prime})=:\widetilde{X})\hskip 10.00002ptp:=\textnormal{pr}_{2}.

∎

For any laft prestack
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
and a tame twisting
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
, let

\textnormal{Split}({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X})\subseteq(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{aff}}_{\textnormal{aft}})_{/\mathcal{X}}

be the subcategory spanned by

where

. By definition of tame twisting, this is a basis for the derived éh-topology on the latter. Moreover, there exists a Grothendieck topology on

such that

is a covering iff it is in the éh-topology of
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{aff}}_{\textnormal{aft}})_{/\mathcal{X}}
.

Let

, the sheaf condition reduces to the case of untwisted D-modules.

We then set

\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{DMod},\acute{e}h,\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Ge}},\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Loc}_{1}},{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X}):=\textnormal{RKE}_{\textnormal{Split}({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X})^{\textnormal{op}}\to(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{aff}}_{\textnormal{aft}})_{/\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{op}}\xrightarrow{\textnormal{Yoneda}}(\textnormal{PreStk}_{\textnormal{laft}})_{/\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{op}}}\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{pre}}(\mathcal{X})

i.e. the Kan extension of the éh-sheaf, and finally set

\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{DMod},\acute{e}h,\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Ge}},\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Loc}_{1}},{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X})).

Similarly we define

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}},\acute{e}h,\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Ge}},\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Loc}_{1}},{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X}))

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}},\acute{e}h,\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Ge}},\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Loc}_{1}},{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}},\mathcal{X}))

Derived h-descent of
DMod
guarantees that we recover the existing notion of
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}(\mathcal{X})
when
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
is in fact trivial. Moreover, the definition of
\displaystyle\oblv({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}})
and h-descent of
DMod
guarantees that

\textnormal{DMod}_{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{DMod},\acute{e}tale,\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{dR}},\textbf{Loc}_{1},\oblv({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}),\mathcal{X}))

so our notation is unambiguous. The following fact justifies our definition in the ind-regular holonomic case as well:

Proposition 13.1.2
.

\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}:\textnormal{Sch}_{\textnormal{aft}}\to\textnormal{DGCat}
satisfies derived h-descent.

Proof.

Let
\displaystyle f:U\to V
be a derived h-cover of aft schemes. Since
DMod
itself satisfies derived h-descent, we have

\textnormal{DMod}(V)\simeq\textnormal{Tot}(\textnormal{DMod}(U^{\bullet}/V))

Now we have two full categories
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(V)
and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Tot}(\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(U^{\bullet}/V))
, where the latter is well-defined because
\displaystyle!
-pullback preserves the regular holonomic subcategories. Moreover, the first is a full subcategory of the second for the same reason. To prove the opposite inclusion, it suffices to show that, for every
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}\in\textnormal{DMod}(V)
,
\displaystyle f^{!}(\mathcal{F})
being regular holonomic implies
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
is as well.

Since
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}
is nil-invariant by definition, by replacing
\displaystyle f
with
\displaystyle f^{\textnormal{cl}}
we reduce to
\displaystyle U,V
being classical schemes and
\displaystyle f
a classical h-cover. By
[
HJ13
, Proposition 3.4]
one can assume that
\displaystyle f
factors as
\displaystyle U\to U^{\prime}\to V
where
\displaystyle U\to U^{\prime}
is a Zariski covering and
\displaystyle U^{\prime}\to V
is proper surjective.
Thus one reduce to each of the two cases.

Suppose
\displaystyle f:U=\bigsqcup_{i}V_{i}\to V
is a Zariski cover. By quasi-compactness assumption the index set
\displaystyle I
is finite, so we can run induction on the size of
\displaystyle I
, and the claim now follows from the open-closed distinguished triangle and the previous lemma. Note that this argument also carries through in the non-ind setting.

When
\displaystyle f
is proper surjective, one can directly prove

\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(V)\to\textnormal{Tot}(\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(U^{\bullet}/V))

is an equivalence using the Barr-Beck-Lurie formalism (
[
Lur12
, Corollary 4.7.5.3]
): note that
\displaystyle f^{!}
is continuous and conservative, and the diagrams in condition (2) of
loc.cit.
are all left adjointable by proper base change of D-modules.
∎

Remark 13.1.3
.

If we consider
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}
i.e. the “small” category, then the argument above shows that it satisfies Zariski descent; nevertheless, it is unclear to us whether h-descent holds.

For laft prestacks, the following constructions (carried out in
[
GR11
]
) extend to the twisted D-module setting in an evident manner, which we will assume without further elaboration:

•

The usual “six functor” formalism; and

•

Base change for arbitrary
\displaystyle!
-pull and schematic quasi-compact
\displaystyle*
-push.

13.2
Analytic Sheaves

To make contact with the analytic world it is more natural to switch to the locally ringed model of derived geometry. (The necessary comparison theorem is established in
[
Por17
]
.) For any
\displaystyle S\in\textnormal{Sch}_{\textnormal{aft}}
, we let
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{an}}
denote the derived
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-analytic space as described in
[
Por16
]
, and let
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{topos}}
denote the underlying
\displaystyle\infty
-topos. We need some basic properties:

•

By
[
Por16
, Lemma 2.3.2]

\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{topos}}
is hypercomplete and (by definition) nil-invariant;

•

Recall what we call “schemes” are 0-geometric stacks, thus by
[
Por17
, Section 2.4]
,
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{topos}}
is 0-localic. Since it always (
[
Por16
, Lemma 3.1.24]
) has enough points, by
[
Lur
, Proposition 2.5.15]
there exists an underlying sober topological space
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{top}}
such that the underlying topos is equivalent to sheaves on the locale of
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{top}}
. In fact,
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{top}}
can be identified with the set of
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-points of
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{cl}}
equipped with the analytic topology;

•

If
\displaystyle S_{1}\to S_{2}
is an closed immersion of (derived) schemes, then
\displaystyle S_{1}^{\textnormal{topos}}\to S_{2}^{\textnormal{topos}}
is an closed immersion of topoi. It follows that the induced map
\displaystyle S_{1}^{\textnormal{top}}\to S_{2}^{\textnormal{top}}
identifies
\displaystyle S_{1}^{\textnormal{top}}
as a closed subspace of
\displaystyle S_{2}^{\textnormal{top}}
;

•

By
[
GR02
, XII 1.2]
and the fact that classical truncation commutes with fiber product, the assignment
\displaystyle X\mapsto X^{\textnormal{top}}
commutes with fiber products.

We set

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}(S):=\textnormal{Shv}(S^{\textnormal{an}};\textnormal{Vect})\simeq\textnormal{Shv}(S^{\textnormal{an}})\tensor\textnormal{Vect}.

Using hypercompleteness of the topos, we know this category is equivalent to the (unbounded) derived category of the abelian category of
\displaystyle\textnormal{Vect}^{\heartsuit}
-valued sheaves on
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{an}}
. It is thus equipped with a
naïve

\displaystyle t
-structure, where an object is coconnective iff it lands in
\displaystyle\textnormal{Vect}^{\geq 0}
object-wise.

For any map
\displaystyle f:S_{1}\to S_{2}
between two such schemes, we have the usual adjunction
\displaystyle(f^{*},f_{*})
.
By the covariant Verdier duality
73
73

73

Our schemes
\displaystyle S
are assumed to be separated, so
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{top}}
is Hausdorff.
, the category is also equipped with another pair of adjunctions
\displaystyle(f_{!},f^{!})
.

Remark 13.2.1
.

Since the formation
\displaystyle X\mapsto X^{\textnormal{top}}
commutes with fiber products, it follows from
[
Lur09
, 7.3.1.19]
that we have “
\displaystyle*
-pull,
\displaystyle*
-push” and “
\displaystyle!
-pull,
\displaystyle!
-push” proper base change for
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}
. Because
\displaystyle!
-push and
\displaystyle*
-push are the same for proper morphisms, we also have “
\displaystyle!
-pull,
\displaystyle*
-push” base change.

Now we specialize to the case of
\displaystyle S
smooth and classical. Within
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}(S)
we have the full subcategory
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(S)
, the category of
algebraically constructible
sheaves, which consists of objects whose cohomologies are constructible (by our convention, this in particular means all fibers are finite-dimensional) with respect to
some
algebraic stratification. This category carries a
perverse

\displaystyle t
-structure, whose heart is the category of perverse sheaves on
\displaystyle S
.
We then define

\textnormal{Shv}_{c}^{!}(S):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(S)).

It carries an unique
\displaystyle t
-structure such that its connective part is generated by
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}^{!}(S)^{\leq 0}
.

Convention 13.2.2
.

Unless otherwise specified, we will only use the perverse
\displaystyle t
-structure on
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(S)
.

For every
\displaystyle f:X\to Y
an closed embedding between aft schemes,
\displaystyle f^{\textnormal{top}}_{*}:\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{an}}(X)\to\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{an}}(Y)
is fully faithful, as the underlying map of topological spaces is a closed embedding. Thus we take the same approach as before by specifying, for
\displaystyle S\in\textnormal{Sch}_{\textnormal{aft}}
:

\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}^{!}(S):=\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{an}}(S)\cap\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}(T)\subseteq\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{an}}(T)\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(S):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}^{!}(S))

for some (equiv. all) closed embedding
\displaystyle S^{\textnormal{cl}}\to T
where
\displaystyle T
is classical aft and smooth. These categories then inherit perverse
\displaystyle t
-structures. Same argument as above shows that arbitrary
\displaystyle!
-pull and
\displaystyle*
-push preserve the (ind-)constructible category.

Remark 13.2.3
.

The complex analytic setting differs from the D-module setting in many ways. For instance, the map
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(S)\to\textnormal{Shv}^{!}(S)
, which ind-extends the inclusion
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(S)\subseteq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}(S)
, is far from being fully faithful. (c.f. “On the derived category of sheaves on a manifold” by Neeman.) Also, the box product

\boxtimes:\textnormal{Shv}(S_{1})\tensor\textnormal{Shv}(S_{2})\to\textnormal{Shv}(S_{1}\times S_{2})

is in general not an equivalence.

Remark 13.2.4
.

The proper base change noted above (and the conserativeness of
\displaystyle!
-fibers for proper surjection, which follows from Verdier duality) together imply (via same argument as in
[
Gai13
]
) that the category
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}(S)
satisfies h-descent. The same argument in Proposition
13.1.2
then shows that
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}
satisfies h-descent, and
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}
satisfies at least Zariski descent.

We now define, for arbitrary laft prestack
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
and analytic gerbe
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}_{\textnormal{an}}
on
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
,

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!},\acute{e}h,\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{an}},\textbf{Loc}_{\textnormal{an}},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}},\mathcal{X}))

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{Shv}_{c}^{!},\acute{e}h,\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{an}},\textbf{Loc}_{\textnormal{an}},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}},\mathcal{X}))

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}(\mathcal{X}):=\Gamma(\mathcal{X},\textnormal{Twisted}(\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}^{!},\acute{e}h,\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{an}},\textbf{Loc}_{\textnormal{an}},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}},\mathcal{X}))

For laft prestacks, the following constructions extend to the (ind)-constructible setting in an evident manner, which we will assume without further elaboration:

•

The usual “six functor” formalism; and

•

Proper base change
[
Lur09
, 7.3.1.19]
.

The following fact is useful:

Lemma 13.2.5
.

Let
\displaystyle\textbf{S}\in\{\textnormal{DMod},\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}},\textnormal{Shv}^{!},\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}},\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}\}
and let
G
denote either
\displaystyle\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Tw}}
or
\displaystyle\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{an}}
, depending on the context. Suppose we have
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}\simeq\colimit_{a\in A}\mathcal{X}_{a}
a colimit in
PreStk
, and
\displaystyle\mathcal{G}
a
G
-structure on
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
. Then we have

\textbf{S}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq\limit_{a\in A}\textbf{S}_{\mathcal{G}}(\mathcal{X}_{a}).

Proof.

One can consider
\displaystyle\textbf{S}_{\mathcal{G}}
as a functor
\displaystyle(\textnormal{PreStk}_{/\mathcal{X}})^{\textnormal{op}}\to\textnormal{DGCat}
, which coincides with what we denoted above as
\displaystyle\textnormal{Twisted}(\textbf{S},\acute{e}h,\textbf{G},\textbf{L},\mathcal{G},\mathcal{X})
(where
L
denote either
\displaystyle\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Loc}_{1}}
or
\displaystyle\textbf{Loc}_{\textnormal{an}}
depending on the context), and it would suffice to prove that
\displaystyle\textbf{S}_{\mathcal{G}}
is the right Kan extension of its restriction to
\displaystyle(\textnormal{Sch}^{\textnormal{aff}}_{/\mathcal{X}})^{\textnormal{op}}
along the Yoneda embedding. The same argument as
[
GR17
, Chapter 5, Lemma 3.2.2]
shows that it suffices to know that
\displaystyle\textbf{S}_{\mathcal{G}}
satisfies Zariski descent, which we have by construction.
∎

13.3
Riemann-Hilbert

The usual Riemann-Hilbert equivalence states that, when
\displaystyle X
is a smooth aft scheme, there exists a
\displaystyle t
-exact, compact-preserving equivalence

\textnormal{RH}:\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}(S)\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr}}(S)\hskip 10.00002pt\textnormal{RH}:\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}(S)\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c}(S)

that intertwines the right D-module
\displaystyle t
-structure one LHS and perverse
\displaystyle t
-structure on RHS, as well as all six functors.

For
\displaystyle S
a general aft scheme, fix some closed embedding
\displaystyle f:S^{\textnormal{cl}}\to T
,
\displaystyle T
classical smooth aft, and let
\displaystyle j:U\to T
be the inclusion of the complement. Then
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}(S)
can be characterized as the subcategory of
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}(T)
consisting of objects
\displaystyle\mathcal{F}
such that
\displaystyle j^{!}(\mathcal{F})\simeq 0
; the same description works for
\displaystyle\textnormal{Shv}_{\textnormal{constr}}^{!}(S)
. It follows that the above equivalence can be extended to arbitrary aft scheme
\displaystyle S
.

Next,
[
Zha20
, Lemma 3.7]
gives a the gerbe analytification map

\textnormal{RH}:\overset{\circ}{\textbf{Ge}}\to\textbf{Ge}_{\textnormal{an}}

which intertwines the action of (tame) local systems on two sides of Riemann-Hilbert. Thus, termwise application of the equivalence, we have

Corollary 13.3.1
.

For any laft prestack
\displaystyle\mathcal{X}
and a tame de Rham gerbe
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
, there are equivalences

\textnormal{RH}:\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}_{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{RH}({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}})}(\mathcal{X})

\textnormal{RH}:\textnormal{DMod}^{\textnormal{rh}}_{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{c,\textnormal{RH}({\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}})}(\mathcal{X}).

We will now specialize to the case of
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
for any smooth curve
\displaystyle X
, with a fixed
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
point
\displaystyle x\in X(\mathbb{C})
. We will further fix a factorizable tame twisting
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
.

Convention 13.3.2
.

For any space
\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}
that maps to
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
in an unambiguous manner, we will abuse notation and let
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
denote the pullback to
\displaystyle\mathcal{Y}
as well.

For each
\displaystyle p\in\mathsf{Dbl}
, we have the corresponding indscheme
\displaystyle[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)}\subseteq[\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}
; we set

\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-constr}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})\subseteq\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{hol},\textnormal{RS}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})

denote the full subcategories of objects that are locally constant along each strata of the cardinality stratification of the Ran space; we refer to such objects as
Ran-constructible
twisted D-modules. We also set

\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)}):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-constr}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})).

Similarly, let

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-constr},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})\subseteq\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{constr},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})

denote the full subcategory consisting of objects locally constant along the same strata, and set

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)}):=\textnormal{Ind}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-constr},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)}).

Clearly, Riemann-Hilbert preserves these subcategories.

Definition 13.3.3
.

We let

\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}))\subseteq\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}})

denote the full subcategory consisting of factorization algebras whose underlying sheaf belongs to the full subcategory
\displaystyle\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})
for each
\displaystyle p
under the equivalence from Proposition
10.5.13
. Similarly, for each
\displaystyle A
we have

A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu},x}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}}))

analogously defined using the module version of
\displaystyle U_{\textnormal{Ran}}
.

Remark 13.3.4
.

It follows from the partition description that a factorization module supported at a single point
\displaystyle x
is ind-regular holonomic (resp. ind-Ran-constructible) if and only if the underlying algebra object is. In other words, we have

A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu},x}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}}))\simeq A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu},x}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}}))

Definition 13.3.5
.

We let

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}})

denote the weakly constructible factorization category corresponding to the system
\displaystyle\{\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{U_{\textnormal{Ran}}(p)})\}
as defined in Definition
6.1.8
. We likewise have a constructible factorization module category

\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}}).

Combine discussions above, we arrive at

Corollary 13.3.6
.

Let
\displaystyle X
be a smooth
\displaystyle\mathbb{C}
-curve and
\displaystyle x\in X(\mathbb{C})
. Let
\displaystyle{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}
be a tame twisting on
\displaystyle X
.
The Riemann-Hilbert equivalence induces an equivalence

\textnormal{RH}:\textnormal{FactAlg}_{\textnormal{nu}}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}^{\textnormal{Ran-c}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}))\simeq\textnormal{FactAlg}^{\textnormal{dual}}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part}}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}}))

and, for every
\displaystyle A
on the LHS, an equivalence

\textnormal{RH}:A\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu},x}(\textnormal{DMod}_{{\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{dR}}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}}))\simeq\textnormal{RH}(A)\textnormal{-FactMod}_{\textnormal{nu},\textnormal{constr},\textnormal{Part},x}(\textnormal{Shv}^{!}_{\textnormal{Ran-c},\mathscr{G}_{\textnormal{Betti}}}([\textnormal{Gr}_{\check{T}}]_{\textnormal{Ran}_{x}})).
